rec.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
rec.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
rec.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

rec.title: Torseurs sur la droite affine sous des groupes lisses
rec.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
rec.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.
Travail en commun K. Cesnavicius et F. Scavia.

rec.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Martin Ortiz
rec.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

rec.abstract: Dans cet exposé, je partirai de certaines conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki reliant la dimension cohomologique des corps à l'existence de certains zéro-cycles sur des hypersurfaces de petit degré. On verra qu'en remplaçant les hypersurfaces de petit degré par des espaces homogènes il est possible d'obtenir des caractérisations de nature diophantienne de la dimension cohomologique. Il s'agit de travaux en commun avec Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche.

rec.title: A Dieudonné theory for analytic p-divisible groups
rec.speaker: Lucas Gerth
rec.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. From this, for S a perfectoid space, we construct an analytic Dieudonné theory with values in mixed characteristic shtukas. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

rec.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
rec.speaker: Emma Weschler
rec.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

rec.title: Numerical semigroups, conjectures, algorithms, and applications.
rec.speaker: Maria Bras-Amorós
rec.abstract:
A numerical semigroup is a subset of N containing zero, with finite complement, and such it is closed under addition. We will introduce the main results on the topic, the connection with algebraic geometry, and the construction of different trees for their classification by different parameters.
Some open conjectures will be presented relating the parameters of a numerical semigroup as well as concerning their growth with respect to the maximum gap, i.e. the Frobenius number, and with respect to the number of gaps, i.e., the genus. We will expose the partial known results and the state of the art of the algorithms for counting semigroups. >
We will finally get a glimpse into the role that numerical semigroups have in the area of error-correcting codes and in music theory.

rec.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
rec.speaker: Nina Gantert
rec.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.

rec.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
rec.speaker: Maxime Marivain
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

rec.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
rec.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

rec.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
rec.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
rec.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

rec.title: Catalan sums, infinite noodle and 1/Pi
rec.speaker: Paul Thévenin
rec.abstract:
We investigate a family of infinite sums of products of Catalan numbers, indexed by trees.
These sums naturally appear in the study of the infinite noodle, which is an infinite random discrete planar graph.
This infinite noodle is the limit, in a local sense, of large uniformly random meandric systems,
which are configurations of non-crossing loops in the plane.
In particular, we show that our sums are all polynomials in 1/Pi with rational coefficients, and provide an algorithm to compute them.
This is joint work with Alin Bostan and Valentin Féray.

rec.title: Empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in populations with density-dependent interactions
rec.speaker: Madeleine Kubasch
rec.abstract: We study a density-dependent Markov jump process describing a population where each individual is characterized by a type, and reproduces at rates depending both on its type and on the population type distribution. We are interested in the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in the population process. First, we exhibit a time-inhomogeneous Markov process, which allows to capture the behavior of a sampled lineage in the population process. This is achieved through a many-to-one formula, which relates the expected value of a functional evaluated over the lineages in the population process to the expectation of the functional evaluated along this time-inhomogeneous process. This provides a direct interpretation of the underlying survivorship bias. Second, we consider the large population regime, when the population size grows to infinity. Under classical assumptions, the population type distribution converges to a deterministic limit. Here, we focus on the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in this large population limit, for which we establish a many-to-one formula. Using coupling arguments, we further quantify the approximation error which arises when sampling in this large population approximation instead of the finite-size population process.

rec.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
rec.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
rec.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.

rec.speaker: Adam MORGAN
rec.abstract: I will discuss joint work with Alex Bartel in which we study the frequency of failures of the Hasse principle in quadratic twist families of torsors under an abelian variety. rec.title: Minimal model for localization of topological Fukaya categories of surfaces
rec.speaker: Pierre BODIN
rec.abstract:
In the first half of this talk, I will present the construction of the topological Fukaya category of a graded marked surface, as introduced by Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and present some of its main properties.
In the second half, I will present a minimal model for the localization of this category at a spherical object corresponding to a simple closed curve on the surface. This new description will then be used to describe the indecomposable objects of the localization in terms of graded curves on the singular surface obtained by collapsing the simple closed curve to a point.

rec.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
rec.speaker: Serge Cantat
rec.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

rec.title: Characterizing totally geodesic manifolds in negative curvature
rec.speaker: David Fisher
rec.abstract: The talk centers around the question of what invariant sets for Anosov flows and diffeomorphisms can look like. It is known that closed invariant sets can be arbitrarily bad and for example be fractals of arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. An old and interesting question, first raised by Hirsch in 1968 is what closed invariant submanifolds can look like. There are many surprising rigidity results in this direction, some quite old, and recently Rose Eliott Smith and I proved a new one, giving a dynamical characterization of totally geodesic submanifolds in negative curvature. I will explain the theorem and both the classical motivation and some more contemporary motivation. If time permits I will give some hints about the proof and particularly how it uses very old results from Smale and Mane.

Dans cette thèse, nous présenterons des asympotiques d'états cohérents propagés par une équation de Schrödinger associée à un Hamiltonien donné. Ces résultats étendent ceux obtenus par Combescure et Robert, dans lesquels un état cohérent propagé est approché dans la limite $h\to 0$ par des paquets gaussiens déformés dits états cohérents comprimés. Cette description reste valide pour des temps $t$ pouvant tendre vers l'infini quand $h\to 0$, dans le régime $|t|\leq |\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ où $\lambda_0$ est l'exposant de Lyapunov maximal de la dynamique classique. L'échec de cette approximation au temps $|\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ est relié à la flexion des paquets d'ondes évolués : une fois étalés à l'échelle $h^{1/3}$, les états comprimés ne founissent plus une description appropriée. Pour obtenir une représentation valide jusqu'à des temps $|t|\leq C|\log h|$ avec un plus grand $C$ (par exemple jusqu'au temps d'Ehrenfest $|\log h|/(2\lambda_0)$ où un étalement à des échelles macroscopiques est autorisé), on ajoute des hypothèses sur le flot $\Phi_t$ associé à la dynamique classique, imposant des contraintes sur les directions d'élongation. La description obtenue met en évidence que les états propagés ne doivent plus être considérés comme microlocalisés en un point mais plutôt le long d'une sous-variété isotrope (correspondant à des directions instables).
Ces résultats seront ensuite appliqués à l'étude de l'équation des ondes amorties sur une variété Anosov, on expliquera comment une telle asymptotique d'états cohérents propagés peut être utilisée pour obtenir des estimées de propagateurs, permettant d'obtenir un trou spectral et des estimées de résolvante pour l'opérateur associé, et ainsi de montrer la décroissance exponentielle de l'énergie des solutions.

imj-91.name: Séminaire Arithmetic Geometry Preprint Seminar
imj-91.department: Formes Automorphes; Théorie des Nombres; Topologie et Géométrie Algébriques
imj-91.organizers: Yves André, Javier Fresán, Wiesława Nizioł
imj-91.description: Souvent, il nous arrive de vouloir étudier en détail une prépublication qui nous intéresse particulièrement, peut-être décisive pour notre travail, mais d’autres tâches renvoient ce voeu aux calendes. Le but de ce séminaire est de nous inciter à réaliser ce voeu, en faisant aussi profiter tour à tour les collègues géomètres arithméticiens des efforts investis dans cette lecture. Il s’agira donc d’exposer, en deux heures, une prépublication significative d’autrui de son choix, devant un public varié de géomètres arithméticiens.

imj-95.description:
[K-OS] KNOT ONLINE SEMINAR
[K-OS] is an online research seminar which focuses on knot theory and low-dimensional topology. Talks will be delivered by authors of recent arXiv articles that made a breakthrough in our field. It happens the 3rd Thursday of months Thursdays from 16:00 to 17:00 (CET/CEST Berlin, Brussels, Madrid, Paris, Rome, Vienna, Warsaw, Zurich) on Zoom.
It is organized by Alexandra Kjuchukova, Lukas Lewark, Louis-Hadrien Robert and Emmanuel Wagner. It benefits from logistical support from the CNRS, the university of Paris and the university of Regensburg.

imj-96.name: Groupe de travail Preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau
imj-96.description:
Voici le calendrier du groupe de travail sur la preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau :
0) 24/01 Introduction générale : Conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel et morphismes de Lattès, stratégie de la preuve
1) 31/01 Analytification de Berkovich sur un corps valué complet et sur un anneau de Banach
2) 07/02 Théorie du (pluri)potentiel global sur les espaces de Berkovich : métriques FS, CPSH (continue psh), métrique d'équilibre d'un système dynamique polarisé (thèse de Pille-Schneider); sur un corps: mesures de MA de métriques CPSH, estimée de Chern-Levine-Nirenberg (Boucksom-Eriksson?)
3) 07/03 Continuité des mesures canoniques (Haar ou Dirac au point de Gauss) sur P^1 [I, Thm 6.8] et des mesures d'équilibre (via Chern-Levine-Nirenberg)
4) 21/03 Hauteurs, énergie mutuelle des mesures et continuité [II et Favre--Riviera-Letelier]
5) 04/04 Cas des Lattès : minoration centrale (énergie mutuelle d'intervalles en valuation triviale) et globale [II, section 6]
6) 18/04 Minoration globale de l'énergie mutuelle et fin de la preuve [II, sections 7-8]
Les séances auront lieu de 10h à 12h en salle 15.25.502 à Jussieu sauf pour le 24/1 qui aura lieu en salle 15.16.413.

m2fonda-gt-combi.name: GT M2 — Combinatoire et entropie
m2fonda-gt-combi.description: Entropy methods in additive combinatorics (Green–Manners–Tao, Hochman), Jan.–Feb. 2026.

m2fonda-gt-dag.name: GT M2 — Géométrie dérivée (DAG Jussieu working group)
m2fonda-gt-dag.description: Goal: postnikov towers of connective E∞-rings are square-zero extensions (Lurie, Higher Algebra 7.4.1.28). Weekly programme started 2 Oct 2025 (∞-categories, stable ∞-categories, E∞-rings, cotangent complex).

m2fonda-gt-dgt.name: GT M2 — Géométrie différentielle non lisse et applications
m2fonda-gt-dgt.description: Optimal transport, metric measure spaces, CD/RCD conditions and stability under lower Ricci bounds (Jan. 2026).

m2fonda-gt-groups.name: GT M2 — Groupes et courbure
m2fonda-gt-groups.description: Curvature and fundamental groups (Bonnet, Cartan–Hadamard, Preissmann, Milnor), then hyperbolic groups (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-hyper.name: GT M2 — Géométrie hyperkählérienne
m2fonda-gt-hyper.description: Holonomy and Berger's classification, Calabi–Yau, variations of Hodge structure, period map and global Torelli (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-k.name: GT M2 — K-théorie (groupe de lecture)
m2fonda-gt-k.description: Algebraic K-theory following Srinivas: K0, K1, K2, then higher K-groups via the plus and Q constructions (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-langlands.name: GT M2 — Langlands p-adique en dimension deux
m2fonda-gt-langlands.recurrence: Tuesdays 16:40–18:40, Jussieu 15-16-101 (as stated in the PDF of 4 Nov. 2025)
m2fonda-gt-langlands.description: p-adic Langlands for GL2(Qp): (φ,Γ)-modules, Fontaine rings, following Astérisque 319/330/331.

m2fonda-gt-mmp.name: GT M2 — Programme minimal
m2fonda-gt-mmp.description: Minimal model program; call for speakers (2025–26).

m2fonda-gt-rh.name: GT M2 — Correspondance de Riemann-Hilbert
m2fonda-gt-rh.description: Flat connections, local systems and representations of π1; Gauss–Manin connection; then regular singularities or D-modules (Nov. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-shen.name: Sujet proposé — Faisceaux cohérents et super-connexions
m2fonda-gt-shen.description: Topic proposed by Shu Shen (not yet organised): coherent sheaves, derived categories, antiholomorphic superconnections and Block's equivalence (Bismut–Shen–Wei).

m2fonda-gt-vss.name: GT M2 — Sexual and gender-based violence and discrimination working group
m2fonda-gt-vss.description: Student working group of the M2, 2025–2026 (presentation PDF updated 2025-12-16). Sessions are arranged among the participants and not published with dates.

paris-apres-midi-topologie.description: Afternoons of several topology talks announced in the LAGA topology seminar listing, e.g. « Après-midi parisienne de topologie » (8 Jan 2026, LAGA) and « Après-midi topologie algébrique » (26 Mar 2026, Sophie Germain). arxiv:2504.01272.title: The N-Body Problem on Coadjoint Orbits
arxiv:2504.01272.summary: We show (Theorem 3) that the symplectic reduction of the spatial $n$-body problem at non-zero angular momentum is a singular symplectic space consisting of two symplectic strata, one for spatial motions and the other for planar motions. Each stratum is realized as coadjoint orbit in the dual of the Lie algebra of the linear symplectic group $Sp(2n-2)$. The planar stratum arises as the frontier upon taking the closure of the spatial stratum.

arxiv:2608.22514.title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
arxiv:2608.22514.summary: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields $V_1,\dots,V_p$ with random run times and evolves according to either a \emph{flight} dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a \emph{gliding} dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions.
arxiv:2608.22514.authors: Olga Aryasova, Ilya Pavlyukevich, Yusif Sualah

arxiv:2610.41635.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
arxiv:2610.41635.summary: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.
arxiv:2610.41635.authors: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins

arxiv:2611.06937.title: A uniform double-factorial construction for consecutive-pattern packings
arxiv:2611.06937.summary: For every overlap $m\geq 3$ and every pattern length $K\geq 2m+1$, we construct an explicit permutation $p\in\mathfrak{S}_K$ such that the number of permutations containing $j$ prescribed occurrences of $p$, with successive starts separated by $K-m$, is $(2j-1)!!$ for every $j\geq 1$. Additional occurrences are permitted. We prove that the corresponding occurrence poset is the ordinal sum of a chain on $m+j(K-m-2)$ elements and a comb on $2j$ elements.

arxiv:2611.06949.title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
arxiv:2611.06949.summary: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $\Sigma_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$.

arxiv:2611.06960.title: Limits of Generalized Magnitudes of Dissimilarity Spaces
arxiv:2611.06960.summary: For a finite symmetric nonnegative dissimilarity matrix $D=(d_{ij})$ with zero diagonal, we study the high-resolution limit ($t\to \infty$) of $\mathbf{1}^T(e^{-td_{ij}})^+\mathbf{1}$. We prove that this limit always exists in the extended real line and is rational whenever finite, without weightability or invertibility assumptions. At fixed cardinality, a finite rational polyhedral fan governs rank and leading asymptotics.

arxiv:2611.06964.title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Tur\'an density at intermediate levels
arxiv:2611.06964.summary: An $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is uniformly dense with respect to $j$-graphs if, up to a small error, at least a prescribed proportion of the $r$-cliques of every $j$-uniform hypergraph on the same vertex set are edges of $H$. For a forbidden hypergraph $F$, its uniform Tur\'an density at level $j$ is the supremum of these density bounds over arbitrarily large $F$-free hypergraphs with the error tending to zero. For every $r\ge4$ and $1\le j\le r-3$, this paper proves that this Tur\'an density is zero precisely when $F$ admits a vertex ordering in which every $(j+1)$-set shared by two edges occupies the same positions in both edges.

arxiv:2611.06981.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
arxiv:2611.06981.summary: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices.
arxiv:2611.06981.authors: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura

arxiv:2611.06983.title: Classification and $C_2$-cofiniteness of rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights
arxiv:2611.06983.summary: We obtain classification results for rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights. More precisely, we prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of OZ type strongly generated by its conformal weight two subspace $V_2$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of Virasoro minimal models. We also prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type generated as a vertex algebra by its conformal weight one subspace $V_1$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of simple affine vertex operator algebras associated with finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras at positive integral levels.

arxiv:2611.06985.title: Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r\geq 17$ contains a second Hamilton cycle
arxiv:2611.06985.summary: A conjecture of Sheehan states that every Hamiltonian $4$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle. A natural problem is to find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every Hamiltonian $r$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle when $r\geq k$. Thomassen proved that $k\leq 300$.
arxiv:2611.06985.authors: Haiyang Liu, Xu Liu, Bo Ning

arxiv:2611.06990.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
arxiv:2611.06990.summary: Data arising in scientific applications often exhibits complex nonlinear structure. Identifying and parameterizing said nonlinearities can enable better modeling, enhance predictive analysis, data interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection. In this paper, we develop theoretical and computational methods to detect and parametrize Euclidean point cloud data lying near a wedge sum of tori.
arxiv:2611.06990.authors: Tanishq Bhatia, Jose A. Perea, Tarek M. Zikry

arxiv:2611.06998.title: Resolving Tusn\'ady's Problem
arxiv:2611.06998.summary: We prove a lower bound of $\Omega_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusn\'ady's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.

arxiv:2611.07000.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
arxiv:2611.07000.summary: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism.
arxiv:2611.07000.authors: Michele Del Zotto, Abhijit Gadde, Pavel Putrov

arxiv:2611.07046.title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
arxiv:2611.07046.summary: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations.

arxiv:2611.07079.title: The odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$
arxiv:2611.07079.summary: We introduce a class of interesting algebraic varieties --- odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k,2n+1)$ and study them with an emphasis on the case of the submaximal odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(n,2n+1)$, which we call catalecticant varieties. The main result of the paper is a construction of a full exceptional collection in the derived category of the catalecticant sixfold $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$.

arxiv:2611.07080.title: Ramification of Weighted Central Paths and Super-linear Interior-Point Methods for Semi-definite Optimization
arxiv:2611.07080.summary: The local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization is closely tied to the regularity of the central path at its limiting point. Without strict complementarity, the central path can exhibit fractional power asymptotics and need not be differentiable in the ordinary barrier parameter. We show that this obstruction can be removed simultaneously for a family of weighted \AHO~central paths.
arxiv:2611.07080.authors: Ali Mohammad-Nezhad, Pouya Sampourmahani, Tamas Terlaky

arxiv:2611.07082.title: Seeking the dense half in $K_4$-free graphs
arxiv:2611.07082.summary: We show that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a balanced bipartition such that neither part contains more than $0.0671n^2 + o(n^2)$ edges. This improves the previous best bound of $0.074n^2$ by Xu and Zhang. We also formulate a conjecture that the tight bound for this problem is $\frac{425}{6498}n^2 \approx 0.0654n^2$, and present a construction showing that it would be best possible.
arxiv:2611.07082.authors: Ignacy Buczek, Andrzej Grzesik, Piotr Kuc

arxiv:2611.07104.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
arxiv:2611.07104.summary: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution.

arxiv:2611.07117.title: An improved lower bound for maximal partial Room squares
arxiv:2611.07117.summary: We establish a new asymptotic lower bound for the volume of a maximal partial Room square of even order $n$. We prove that its volume is at least $\frac{2\sqrt{66}-6}{57}n^2-O(n)$, improving the leading coefficient $1/8$ in the lower bound obtained by Meszka and Rosa. The proof combines two counting arguments, one based on a transversal of empty cells and the other on the graph of occurring symbol pairs.

arxiv:2611.07118.title: Perfect Partitions of Regular Bipartite Graphs
arxiv:2611.07118.summary: Let $I_{n,n}$ be a fixed perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $L_{n,1}=K_{n,n}-I_{n,n}$. A perfect set of $L_{n,1}$ is a $1$-factorization of $L_{n,1}$, that is, a set of $n-1$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings whose union is $E(L_{n,1})$; a perfect partition of $L_{n,1}$ is a partition of the set of all perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ into perfect sets. Brualdi, Chiang, and Li (2005) asked whether $L_{n,1}$ admits a perfect partition.
arxiv:2611.07118.authors: Melanie J. Ferreri, Archana L. Parameswaran, Gexin Yu

arxiv:2611.07138.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
arxiv:2611.07138.summary: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric.

arxiv:2611.07145.title: An improved bound for the intersection of two longest cycles in $k$-connected graphs
arxiv:2611.07145.summary: A conjecture attributed to Smith states that in every $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest cycles intersects in at least $k$ vertices. We prove that every two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices intersect in at least $\min\{k,10k-n-30\}$ vertices. Consequently, Smith's conjecture holds whenever $k\ge \frac{n+30}{9}$.

arxiv:2611.07150.title: Isospectral Deformations of Diagonal Matrices by Symmetric Matrices in Dimension Four
arxiv:2611.07150.summary: For a diagonal matrix $D$ with distinct diagonal entries in an algebraically closed field $K$ we study the symmetric matrices $Q$ with entries in $K$ such that the affine line $D+tQ$ has the same eigenvalues in $K$ as $D$. We study the equality of characteristic polynomials, $\chi_{D+tQ}(x)=\chi_D(x) \text{ for all }\: t\in K$ and examine the resulting system of equations. For generic diagonal matrices of size at most $4$ we show that only the trivial symmetric matrix $Q=0$ satisfies this isospectral condition.

arxiv:2611.07202.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
arxiv:2611.07202.summary: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.

arxiv:2611.07204.title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
arxiv:2611.07204.summary: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound.

arxiv:2611.07207.title: A Complete Equational Theory for Quantum Circuits with Generalized Control
arxiv:2611.07207.summary: Controlled subcircuits are commonplace in quantum algorithms as they represent the quantum analogue of branching statements (if then). We introduce a generalization of controlled subcircuits in the form of a binary operation which sends pairs of unitary quantum circuits to a generalized controlled operation, whose semantics are based on matrix exponentials and logarithms. The family of quantum circuits with generalized controlled operations and circuit exponentiation is denoted HQC for Hierarchical Quantum Circuits.
arxiv:2611.07207.authors: William Schober (Universit\`a della Svizzera italiana), Scott Wesley (Dalhousie University)

arxiv:2611.07221.title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
arxiv:2611.07221.summary: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}), \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{C}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of…

arxiv:2611.07236.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
arxiv:2611.07236.summary: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits.
arxiv:2611.07236.authors: Sylvain Crovisier, Alejo Garc\'ia-Sassi, Yuri Lima, F\'abio Tal

arxiv:2611.07239.title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
arxiv:2611.07239.summary: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones.

arxiv:2611.07251.title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
arxiv:2611.07251.summary: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in A\Gamma$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in A\Gamma$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.

arxiv:2611.07252.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
arxiv:2611.07252.summary: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero.

arxiv:2611.07255.title: Values of differentials of plane branches: block decomposition and semiroots
arxiv:2611.07255.summary: We study the passage of special gaps from a Zariski semiroot to a plane branch. A decomposition into rectangular blocks allows us to compute the maximal valuations of the coefficients of differentials and describe the image of the transition map. We treat vertical and horizontal decompositions, as well as decompositions with alternations, obtaining criteria for the preservation of special gaps.

arxiv:2611.07262.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
arxiv:2611.07262.summary: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags.

arxiv:2611.07266.title: Quadratic Extractors
arxiv:2611.07266.summary: A quadratic source is a random variable $X\sim\mathbb{F}_2^n$ generated by applying $n$ quadratics to a hidden uniform string. Previously, the best-known explicit extractor for this model required min-entropy roughly $k=n-\sqrt{\log n}$. In this paper, we give an explicit construction for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$.
arxiv:2611.07266.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Jesse Goodman, David Zuckerman

arxiv:2611.07267.title: Pattern avoidance classes of parking permutations with fixed lucky sets
arxiv:2611.07267.summary: For a parking function, the resulting sequence after all cars have parked is called the associated parking permutation. For each parking function, cars that park in their preferred spot are called lucky cars. In this paper, we enumerate parking permutations that avoid a specified set of permutation patterns in $\mathfrak{S}_3$ and whose lucky cars are the first $k$ cars.

arxiv:2611.07290.title: Rational Tur\'an exponents of a single $k$-uniform hypergraph
arxiv:2611.07290.summary: For a fixed $k$-uniform hypergraph $F$, let $\mathrm{ex}_k(n,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $F$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that for every integer $k\ge2$ and every rational $r\in[0,1]$ there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph $F_{k,r}$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathrm{ex}_k(n,F_{k,r})=\Theta(n^{k-r}). \end{equation*} The case $k=2$ is the rational exponents conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Simonovits \cite{Erdos1988}, also known as Erd\H{o}s problem \#571 \cite{BloomErdoswebsite}; a proof was announced in September 2026 and is expounded by Conlon et al.\ \cite{Conlon-Janzer-Jiang-Kim-Lee-Liu-Longbrake-Yepremyan}.

arxiv:2611.07292.title: Ultrahomogeneous hypertournaments
arxiv:2611.07292.summary: A $k$-hypertournament is a higher-arity generalisation of a tournament, consisting of a set together with an irreflexive $k$-ary relation such that the automorphism group of each substructure of size $k$ is the alternating group $\mathrm{A}_k$. We show that, for each $k \geq 3$, there are continuum-many non-isomorphic countable ultrahomogeneous $k$-hypertournaments, answering a question of Cherlin.

arxiv:2611.07303.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
arxiv:2611.07303.summary: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$.
arxiv:2611.07303.authors: Saad A. Awan, Steven J. Miller, Linh Nguyen, Steven Senger, Elvis Wong

arxiv:2611.07314.title: On the number of edges in quasiplanar graphs
arxiv:2611.07314.summary: A $k$-quasiplanar graph is a graph drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. Pach, Shahrokhi, and Szegedy conjectured that every such graph on $n$ vertices has $O_k(n)$ edges. ChatGPT produced a proof of this conjecture.
arxiv:2611.07314.authors: J\'anos Pach, G\'abor Tardos, Ji Zeng

arxiv:2611.07333.title: On explicit units in a family of cubic fields and the arithmetic of curves arising from powers of these units
arxiv:2611.07333.summary: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $K_b$ be the cubic field generated by the unique real root of $x^3-3bx-b^3$, let $\eta_0$ be its fundamental unit, and let $\eta_b$ be the explicit unit studied in the companion paper (arXiv:2609.37389). Write $\eta_b=\eta_0^{n(b)}$. Deciding whether $n(b)$ is divisible by $q$ amounts to finding the integral points of a plane curve $C_q$ of degree $2q$.

arxiv:2611.07351.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
arxiv:2611.07351.summary: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition.

arxiv:2611.07365.title: The $q$-Poincar\'e sum and separability in a Coxeter group
arxiv:2611.07365.summary: Given a finite Coxeter group $W$ and an element $q$ of a commutative ring $\mathbf{k}$, we define the element $\mathbf{L}_{q} :=\sum_{w\in W}q^{\ell\left( w\right) }w$ of its group algebra $\mathbf{k}\left[ W\right] $. We say that an element $w\in W$ is $W$\emph{-length-symmetric} if its coefficient in the commutator $\left[ \mathbf{L}_{a},\mathbf{L}_{b}\right] $ is $0$ for all $\mathbf{k}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbf{k}$. We prove several sufficient criteria for elements to be $W$-length-symmetric.

arxiv:2611.07396.title: Discrete history operators: Exact state-space realization for sequence memory
arxiv:2611.07396.summary: A prescribed finite-dimensional analysis of an evolving discrete history need not admit an exact recurrence driven only by its current state and the entering input. We study exact realizations of causal linear discrete history operators (DHOs). Operator factorization and kernel inclusion characterize exact closure, while the cross-projection defect characterizes closure failure for orthonormal analyses.
arxiv:2611.07396.authors: Bin Zhou, Rong Gao, Zhao-Yan Li

arxiv:2611.07407.title: The Higman-Sims graph and a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$
arxiv:2611.07407.summary: The Higman-Sims graph is the unique strongly regular graph with parameters $(100,22,0,6)$. In this paper, we show that the only distance-regular antipodal double cover of the Higman-Sims graph is its bipartite double cover. Our main tool is a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$.

arxiv:2611.07421.title: Prescribed Color Patterns in Tight Hamilton Cycles and Spanning Trees
arxiv:2611.07421.summary: We compare transversal and pattern thresholds for two spanning structures. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and $\alpha>0$, we prove that every sufficiently large $n$-vertex $k$-graph collection with minimum codegree at least $(1/2+\alpha)n$ contains a tight Hamilton cycle with any prescribed color pattern. Hence the transversal and pattern thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles coincide asymptotically.

arxiv:2611.07429.title: Connected graphs having maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius
arxiv:2611.07429.summary: Let $\rho(G)$ denote the signless Laplacian spectral radius of a graph $G$, and let $\mathcal C_{n,m}$ be the family of connected graphs of order $n$ and size $m$. A graph is $Q$-maximal if it maximizes $\rho(G)$ over this family. Motivated by a question of Chang and Tam (2011), we study this extremal problem using scalar identities and coronal methods for threshold graphs.
arxiv:2611.07429.authors: Di-Jian Wang, Hong-Yan Ge, Shi-Cai Gong, Bo-Jun Yuan

arxiv:2611.07446.title: Periodic counting, carry synchronization, and primes in nonstandard numeration systems
arxiv:2611.07446.summary: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ be a finite digit set containing zero, with maximum residue multiplicity $\mu=\max_{0\le r<b}\#\{d\in D:d\equiv r\pmod b\}$ and cardinality $q=\#D\ge2$. Under the condition $\mu<q$, we prove that the summatory representation function satisfies an asymptotic formula with a strictly positive, H\"older continuous, $1$-periodic fluctuating profile and an error of $O_D(x^{\log_b\mu})$. An exact periodic factorization of the Laplace generating function furnishes an explicit, computable Fourier expansion for the periodic profile via Gamma factors, and yields the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series to the entire…

arxiv:2611.07454.title: Brauer groups of generalised Markoff surfaces
arxiv:2611.07454.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero with $a,b,c\in k^\times$ and let $m\in k\setminus\{0,4abc\}$. We compute the Brauer group of the generalised Markoff surface $ax^2+by^2+cz^2-xyz=m$. We also construct several counterexamples to the integral Hasse principle, which are explained by the Brauer--Manin obstruction.

arxiv:2611.07455.title: Worldsheet skeins and block decomposition of quivers
arxiv:2611.07455.summary: Following the knot-quiver correspondence, we investigate quiver counterparts of the HOMFLYPT skein relations by interpreting link invariants in terms of holomorphic worldsheets and their multicover contributions. Extending this framework to more general worldsheet geometries, we conjecture that, up to quiver equivalence, the adjacency matrix of the quiver associated with any link in a skein triple admits a block decomposition whose diagonal blocks are quiver adjacency matrices associated with the other two links. We verify this conjecture in numerous examples.
arxiv:2611.07455.authors: Sachin Chauhan, Piotr Kucharski, Lukas Nakamura, Dmitry Noshchenko, Ramadevi Pichai, Vivek Kumar Singh, Marko Sto\v{s}i\'{c}

arxiv:2611.07466.title: Functors from Lagrangian correspondences for wrapped sheaf categories
arxiv:2611.07466.summary: We consider the category of sheaves on a manifold with microsupport in a singular conic Lagrangian, and more generally microsheaves on the Lagrangian skeleton of a Weinstein manifold with stop, which are equivalent to ind-completions of partially wrapped Fukaya categories. Compact objects in these categories are obtained as wrappings of constructible sheaves with perfect stalks; they correspond to objects built from exact Lagrangians in finitely many steps. We give a microlocal criterion on constructible (micro)sheaves with perfect (micro)stalks which guarantees that the corresponding wrapped sheaves induce integral kernels that preserve compact objects of these categories.
arxiv:2611.07466.authors: Sheel Ganatra, Christopher Kuo, Wenyuan Li, Haosen Wu

arxiv:2611.07472.title: Decomposable polytopes with few vertices
arxiv:2611.07472.summary: A polytope $P$ is decomposable if it can be written as the Minkowski sum of two polytopes that are not homothetic to it. It is well known that decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with $2d$ or fewer vertices are the simplicial prisms. More recent work shows that, with two exceptions in low dimensions, decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with exactly $2d+1$ vertices are either pentasms or capped prisms.

arxiv:2611.07497.title: Distinguishing invariants of Cayley Graphs, Hamming graphs, and wreath product actions
arxiv:2611.07497.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial group that acts on a graph $G=(V,E)$. The total distinguishing number $D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)$ (distinguishing index $D'_{\Gamma}(E)$) of the action is the least number of labels required for a total labeling (edge labeling) of $G$ so that the only elements of $\Gamma$ that preserve the labeling belong to the pointwise stabilizer of $V\cup E$ (pointwise stabilizer of $E$). We obtain upper bounds of these invariants for Cayley graphs and under various group actions, including free actions, wreath product actions, and coordinatewise actions on Cartesian powers of graphs.

arxiv:2611.07499.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
arxiv:2611.07499.summary: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(\mu)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(\mu)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$.
arxiv:2611.07499.authors: Dawei Chen, Scott Mullane, Nick Salter, Guillaume Tahar

arxiv:2611.07503.title: Strict unimodality without log-concavity for partial Petrial polynomials
arxiv:2611.07503.summary: For a simple graph $G$, the partial Petrial polynomial $P_G^{\times}(z)$ enumerates all diagonal perturbations of its adjacency matrix over $GF(2)$ by rank. We derive a rooted attachment identity and apply it to the tree $R_m$ obtained by joining a new vertex to the middle vertex of each of $m$ disjoint copies of the five-vertex path. We prove that the nonzero coefficient sequence of $P_{R_m}^{\times}(z)$ is strictly unimodal for every $m\ge1$, but is log-concave if and only if $1\le m\le3$.

arxiv:2611.07505.title: Object ideals and idempotent completeness
arxiv:2611.07505.summary: We construct an idempotent complete Frobenius exact category with an idempotent complete stable category in which a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals induces a cotorsion pair of objects that fails to be complete. This gives a negative answer to the question of Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas under idempotent completeness. The construction uses a lemma on dense triangulated subcategories and an example of Bondarko and Sosnilo in which a weight structure fails to extend to the idempotent completion.

arxiv:2611.07507.title: The Chow ring of a wonderful compactification
arxiv:2611.07507.summary: The theory of wonderful compactifications provides a common framework encompassing the constructions of important varieties such as the Fulton-MacPherson configuration spaces, the moduli space of $n$-pointed stable rational curves, and the De Concini-Procesi models of subspace arrangements, and, more generally, of smooth compactifications in which the subvarieties in a building set are replaced by a simple normal crossings boundary divisor. We give a presentation of the Chow ring of a wonderful compactification, assuming only that the Chow ring of the ambient variety surjects onto that of each subvariety in the induced arrangement. Our results recover and extend many previously known…
arxiv:2611.07507.authors: Patricio Gallardo, Javier Gonz\'alez-Anaya, Jos\'e Luis Gonz\'alez

arxiv:2611.07514.title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations
arxiv:2611.07514.summary: Using dehydration signatures as an encoding, we train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-dimensional manifolds. Our main runs each use approximately 3 exaFLOPs, spanning a 200 million parameter model trained on 60 million sphere triangulations to an 11 million parameter model trained on 1.1 billion sphere triangulations. The optimal model has 10 blocks, width 640 and generates dehydration signatures of closed manifolds of various topological types at a rate of 6.9%, 82% of which are spheres.
arxiv:2611.07514.authors: Daniel Bruwel, Ashvni Narayanan, Jonathan Spreer

arxiv:2611.07527.title: Structure of adjacency algebras of thin Jordan schemes
arxiv:2611.07527.summary: We prove that adjacency algebras of Jordan schemes over fields of characteristic zero are semisimple. We then classify the adjacency algebras of thin Jordan schemes over the fields of real numbers or complex numbers. The simple summands of the adjacency algebras over these fields are restricted to specific types of simple Jordan algebras.

arxiv:2611.07549.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
arxiv:2611.07549.summary: Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $\Lambda$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $\Lambda$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$.

arxiv:2611.07568.title: Generalized Chromatic Polynomials of Cycles and uni-cyclic Graphs
arxiv:2611.07568.summary: In \cite{R81}, Read obtained an explicit formula for the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs using the classical deletion-contraction principle. In this paper, we take a linear-algebraic approach and present a new proof of Read's formula by realizing the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs as traces of certain linear operators. As an application of this approach, we also derive explicit formulas for the generalized chromatic polynomials of uni-cyclic graphs.

arxiv:2611.07571.title: Bernstein-Sato polynomials of generic Pfaffian ideals
arxiv:2611.07571.summary: We determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein--Sato polynomial of every generic Pfaffian ideal. In the nonmaximal case, the roots lie in explicit rational windows indexed by the rank strata. Integral roots retain their label multiplicities, whereas every nonintegral root is simple, including values with several labels.

arxiv:2611.07581.title: Probability model of connectedness for graphs with logarithmical degree
arxiv:2611.07581.summary: For a graph $G$ of order $N$, an integer $k$ with $0\leq k< N$ and a real number $p$ with $0\leq p\leq 1$, let $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ be the probabilities that $G$ is disconnected when $k$ vertices are removed randomly and when each vertex is removed independently with probability $p$, respectively. We deduce a formula of $p(G,k)$ for Harary graphs and show that the phase transition on $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ occurs in the class that has logarithmical degree. We also perform simulations on $p(G,k)$ for the Hypercube and randomly generated graphs of the same scale, which suggests that the regularity is a key structural feature that guarantees nice performance on $p(G,k)$.

arxiv:2611.07584.title: Presenting Point-Glued Self-Similar Objects as Final Coalgebras in Metric Spaces via Completion: A Categorical Hutchinson Theorem
arxiv:2611.07584.summary: We study self-similar spaces obtained by repeatedly gluing finitely many scaled copies of a pointed metric space along prescribed boundary points. A finite gluing specification defines endofunctors on suitable categories of pointed sets and pointed metric spaces. Under non-degeneracy and metric admissibility assumptions, the initial algebra of the set functor carries a canonical metric.

arxiv:2611.07625.title: Multivariable Congruence Jumping: Periodic States, Integral Realizations, and Descent
arxiv:2611.07625.summary: Congruence jumping replaces coordinates by integer quotients and updates polynomial divisibility relations. We extend this procedure to several variables and retain integer coefficients by recording their common factor separately. For three-variable systems of divisibilities with signed binomial numerators, we classify all positive integer exponent tuples of period at most two under three successive coordinate jumps: seven fixed tuples and twenty-two cycles of exact period two.
arxiv:2611.07625.authors: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

arxiv:2611.07626.title: Combinatorics of noncommutative harmonic oscillator determinant
arxiv:2611.07626.summary: We obtain an explicit evaluation of the determinants that appear in the denominators of the integrands for the iterated integrals expressing special values of the spectral zeta function of the noncommutative harmonic oscillator at integers greater than 1. The determinants in question are those of cyclic tridiagonal matrices; their explicit evaluation is carried out, in addition to the inclusion-exclusion principle, conceptionally using combinatorial arguments based on monomer-dimer systems. This explicit evaluation serves as a core component in the study of arithmetic properties such as the modularity of the special values of the spectral zeta function.

arxiv:2611.07637.title: Topological Characterization of Adinkra Heights
arxiv:2611.07637.summary: Adinkras are highly structured bipartite graphs that encapsulate 1D supersymmetry representations. We classify hypercube Adinkra heights with one, two, three or four edge colors using a graph-theoretic notion of equivalence. For the 990 distinct height functions in the case of four edge colors, we show that these classes match modified twisted character classes bijectively and provide a finer classification than spectral Height Yielding Matrix Numbers (HYMNs).
arxiv:2611.07637.authors: Amanda E. Francis, S. James Gates Jr., Digvijay Roy Varier, Ursula A. Whitcher

arxiv:2611.07661.title: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes
arxiv:2611.07661.summary: Thresholds for local properties tell us which guarantees to expect from random linear codes (RLCs) and help us carry those guarantees over to structured codes. A monotone property is $b$-local if a collection of at most $b$ codewords can witness its satisfaction or failure, as in list decoding and list recovery. The threshold of $\mathcal P$ is the code dimension at which the probability that an RLC in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ satisfies $\mathcal P$ crosses $1/2$ in a sharp transition.
arxiv:2611.07661.authors: Vinayak M. Kumar, Ray Li, Jonathan Mosheiff, Gilad Shavit

arxiv:2611.07664.title: Web bases for the Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$
arxiv:2611.07664.summary: Queffelec--Sartori and Tubbenhauer--Vaz--Wedrich give a diagrammatic web category via generators and relations to describe the subcategory of Rep($\mathfrak{gl}(m|n)$) generated by tensor products of exterior powers of the defining representation. We construct the first explicit bases for homomorphism spaces in the web category for $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$, giving an alternative diagrammatic presentation of this web category, and explore connections to the combinatorics of planar networks. Our basis comes equipped with an algorithm to decompose any web into a linear combination of basis webs, giving an effective way to compute in the $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$-skein theory.

arxiv:2611.07715.title: Anti-ribbon shaped Young diagram decomposition
arxiv:2611.07715.summary: We introduce a sliding procedure on diagrams which splits the standard Young tableaux of a corner-crossed diagram, in particular of a skew shape, along a finite binary tree whose leaves are anti-ribbon diagrams. Combined with standardization, this yields a decomposition of semi-standard Young tableaux into tableaux of anti-ribbon shape, indexed by standard tableaux and governed by their descent sets. As applications, we obtain expansions of Schur functions and Schur multiple zeta functions in terms of their anti-ribbon type analogues; at the level of Schur functions, this is a tableau-level form of Gessel's fundamental quasisymmetric expansion.
arxiv:2611.07715.authors: Hideki Murahara, Maki Nakasuji, Wataru Takeda

arxiv:2611.07733.title: On the classification of $2$-distance-primitive graphs of small valency
arxiv:2611.07733.summary: A non-complete vertex-transitive graph is called 2-distance-primitive if a vertex stabilizer acts primitively on both the first and second distance neighborhoods of the vertex. Recently, Ruan, Liu and Jin [Discrete Math. 347 (2024), 113978] showed that every connected 2-distance-primitive graph of valency at most 9 either belongs to certain known families or satisfies a collection of further restrictions, with the socle of a vertex stabilizer isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ or $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$. In this paper, we resolve these remaining cases and thereby obtain a complete classification of connected 2-distance-primitive graphs of valency at most 9.
arxiv:2611.07733.authors: Xing Zhang, Xue Wang, Jun-Jie Huang

arxiv:2611.07795.title: A Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual stable Grothendieck functions
arxiv:2611.07795.summary: We give a closed boundary formula for multiplication by power sums in the dual stable Grothendieck basis. The off-diagonal coefficients are signed binomial coefficients supported on corner-connected broken ribbons, which are skew diagrams connected through edges or vertices and containing no square of four boxes. For such a diagram, the smallest power-sum index with a nonzero coefficient is the number of boxes plus the number of edge-connected components minus one.
arxiv:2611.07795.authors: Dang Tuan Hiep, Do Le Hai Thuy

arxiv:2611.07813.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
arxiv:2611.07813.summary: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$).

arxiv:2611.07816.title: The fixed-point proportion of Latt\`es maps
arxiv:2611.07816.summary: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Latt\`es map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Latt\`es map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension.

arxiv:2611.07818.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
arxiv:2611.07818.summary: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy.

arxiv:2611.07833.title: Hausdorff dimension of nonergodic directions in higher genus via effective equidistribution
arxiv:2611.07833.summary: For each fixed $g\ge3$, we prove that non-uniquely ergodic directions have Hausdorff dimension $1/2$ on almost every area-one surface in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{odd}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is odd, and in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{nonhyp}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is even. We construct these directions through cyclic splittings into $g$ slit tori. Effective equidistribution of Lindenstrauss--Mohammadi--Yang supplies sufficiently many children at each normal input.

arxiv:2611.07849.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
arxiv:2611.07849.summary: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves.

arxiv:2611.07856.title: Three-critical hypergraphs of maximum local edge connectivity two
arxiv:2611.07856.summary: For a hypergraph \(G\), let \(\chi(G)\) denote its chromatic number and \(\lambda(G)\) the maximum, over pairs of distinct vertices, of the minimum size of an edge cut separating the pair. A hypergraph is \(3\)-critical if its chromatic number is three and every proper subhypergraph is two-colorable. In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of the \(3\)-critical hypergraphs with \(\lambda(G)\le2\).

arxiv:2611.07898.title: Topological classification of Bazaikin spaces
arxiv:2611.07898.summary: In this paper, we establish a topological classification of Bazaikin spaces whose sixth cohomology groups have orders prime to \(5\). Moreover, we obtain an estimate for the number of diffeomorphism types among these spaces.

arxiv:2611.07908.title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
arxiv:2611.07908.summary: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions.
arxiv:2611.07908.authors: Julia Q. D. Du, Gurinder Singh

arxiv:2611.07917.title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
arxiv:2611.07917.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $\kappa\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $\kappa$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $\kappa$ is not critical.

arxiv:2611.07924.title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
arxiv:2611.07924.summary: For an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) and an integer \(m\ge n\), let \(f'(G,m)\) be the minimum number of distinct color sets used by proper colorings from \(m\)-element lists that are disjoint at distinct nonadjacent vertices. A clique-partition assignment gives a common list to the vertices of each part of a clique partition and uses disjoint lists on different parts. In this paper, we construct a graph on \(20\) vertices for which these assignments do not attain \(f'(G,20)\), and a fixed graph on \(25\) vertices for which they fail to attain the minimum for every allowed list size.

arxiv:2611.07927.title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
arxiv:2611.07927.summary: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.

arxiv:2611.07987.title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
arxiv:2611.07987.summary: For projective morphisms $\pi:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}\pi_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists.

arxiv:2611.07992.title: Isomorphisms and automorphisms of minimal comaximal hypergraphs of commutative rings
arxiv:2611.07992.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly $n\ge 2$ maximal ideals and let $k\ge 2$. We study the minimal $k$-uniform comaximal hypergraph $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$, whose vertices are the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical and whose edges are the irredundant $k$-element comaximal families. For $2\le k\le n$ we show that $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ is a blow-up of the hypergraph of irredundant $k$-coverings of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and that its reduced form reconstructs the maximal ideals up to permutation; for $k>n$ there are no edges.

arxiv:2611.08002.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
arxiv:2611.08002.summary: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation?

arxiv:2611.08018.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
arxiv:2611.08018.summary: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion.
arxiv:2611.08018.authors: Alexander Hock, Jakob Lindner, Raimar Wulkenhaar

arxiv:2611.08022.title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
arxiv:2611.08022.summary: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\le\gamma(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $\gamma=\gamma_t=\gamma_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number.

arxiv:2611.08044.title: Few-Weight Linear Sets and Divisibility of Rank-Metric Codes
arxiv:2611.08044.summary: We study $\mathbb F_q$-linear sets whose positive point weights belong to a prescribed finite set $A$. The integer $e=\gcd(A)$ always divides the rank of the defining subspace, but the divisibility does not by itself imply linearity over $\mathbb F_{q^e}$. We show that it does in a broad parameter range.
arxiv:2611.08044.authors: Jan De Beule, Leen Demuys, Ferdinando Zullo, Olga Polverino

arxiv:2611.08047.title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
arxiv:2611.08047.summary: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.
arxiv:2611.08047.authors: Mohammad Samy Baladram, Ryutaro Misawa, Akihiro Munemasa

arxiv:2611.08063.title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
arxiv:2611.08063.summary: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$.
arxiv:2611.08063.authors: Philip Hackney, Joachim Kock, Jan Steinebrunner
