arxiv:2611.08071.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
arxiv:2611.08071.summary: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened.

arxiv:2611.08079.title: Idiosynchromatic Poetry
arxiv:2611.08079.summary: We prove equivalences of asymmetric partition relations involving natural numbers and products of weakly compact cardinals $\kappa$, infinite cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ and natural numbers to certain classes of finitary problems in the theory of edge-coloured digraphs. We are able to determine three classes of Ramsey numbers exactly, typical examples in these classes are $r(\omega^2 2, 3)$, $r(\kappa\lambda 2, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda 3, 3)$. We moreover provide general upper bounds for $r(\omega^2 m, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda m, n)$.

arxiv:2611.08109.title: The Calkin--Wilf problems on $\ell$-ary partition functions
arxiv:2611.08109.summary: In their 1998 precursor to their celebrated paper ``Recounting the rationals,'' Calkin and Wilf listed nine open problems related to the function $b_{k,\ell}(n)$, the number of partitions of $n$ into powers of $\ell$ with each part appearing at most $k$ times. In this short paper, we answer five of their eight remaining open problems. As a consequence of our results, we extend and generalise results of both Carlitz and Reznick, and answer an open question of Reznick.

arxiv:2611.08124.title: Categorified convergence: dropping the 'ultra' from 'virtual ultracategories'
arxiv:2611.08124.summary: Virtual ultracategories are a recent categorification of topological spaces seen as sets of points together with a convergence relation between points and ultrafilters. However, a topology can also be described in terms of convergence of filters: in this paper, we thus introduce an analogue of virtual ultracategories based on filters rather than ultrafilters. At the topological level, convergence of filters is completely determined by its restriction to ultrafilters.

arxiv:2611.08143.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
arxiv:2611.08143.summary: Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of bounded twin-width. We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every monadically dependent graph class.
arxiv:2611.08143.authors: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

arxiv:2611.08165.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
arxiv:2611.08165.summary: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics.

arxiv:2611.08172.title: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field
arxiv:2611.08172.summary: A collection of classical codes $C_1,\dots,C_m$ has product expansion if every low-weight word in the sum of their extensions to the product space can be written as a sum of words supported on few lines, each line being a codeword of the corresponding $C_i$. For $m=2$ product expansion is equivalent to robust testability of the tensor code, while for $m\ge 3$ it is strictly stronger; it is the hypothesis on the local codes behind recent constructions of good quantum LDPC codes, good quantum locally testable codes, and quantum codes with transversal non-Clifford gates. No explicit family over a fixed field was previously known to achieve constant rate, linear distance for both the code and…

arxiv:2611.08176.title: Fermat quotients with CM Jacobians and trivial automorphism group
arxiv:2611.08176.summary: Let $F_n$ be the Fermat curve of degree $n$ over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D_n=F_n/S_3$ be its quotient by coordinate permutations. We prove that $D_n$ has trivial geometric automorphism group for every $n\ge 11$ with $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Its Jacobian has complex multiplication.

arxiv:2611.08186.title: On generalized token graphs with tokens of different colors
arxiv:2611.08186.summary: We generalize the concept of token graphs, and we call them supertoken graphs. In this work, we consider the variant in which tokens are distinguishable (for instance, by color) and at most one token is allowed on each vertex. We formally define this kind of supertoken graphs and present their basic properties.
arxiv:2611.08186.authors: Cristina Dalf\'o, Blas Fern\'andez, Miquel \`Angel Fiol, M\'onica A. Reyes

arxiv:2611.08190.title: Torsion points in families of elliptic curves
arxiv:2611.08190.summary: We study the specialization of torsion points in one-parameter degenerations of elliptic curves with singular fibers of Kodaira type. We describe the resulting torsion curves, their ramifications, intersection multiplicities, and irreducible and connected components.

arxiv:2611.08203.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
arxiv:2611.08203.summary: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta and Ghorpade and determines the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan.

arxiv:2611.08230.title: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets
arxiv:2611.08230.summary: We investigate the optimal asymptotic rate $R_q$ of perfect $q$-hash codes, a fundamental extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. Let $B_q=-\log_2(1-q!/q^q)/(q-1)$ denote the classical probabilistic lower bound. We prove that $R_q=B_q$ if and only if $q=2$, establishing an explicit strict improvement for every $q\ge3$ and settling the first assertion of a conjecture of Xing and Yuan (Combinatorica 43 (2023), 347--366).

arxiv:2611.08244.title: Open Problems on the Null Space and Image Space of the Adjacency Matrix
arxiv:2611.08244.summary: Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi proposed two questions concerning the null space and the image space of graphs. Although these problems have been studied in several cases, they have not yet been fully resolved. In this work, we present constructions of graphs that satisfy both the problems.
arxiv:2611.08244.authors: K Kranthi Priya, K C Sivakumar

arxiv:2611.08248.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
arxiv:2611.08248.summary: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period.

arxiv:2611.08253.title: All minimum cuts of symmetric submodular functions
arxiv:2611.08253.summary: We compute Cunningham's canonical decomposition of a symmetric submodular function on $n$ elements in $O(n^3)$ time. The decomposition represents all minimum cuts in linear space. For the pair $s,t$ produced by Queyranne's algorithm, we construct in $O(n^2)$ time a digraph representing exactly the minimum $st$-cuts of the function.

arxiv:2611.08257.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
arxiv:2611.08257.summary: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I.

arxiv:2611.08265.title: Some polynomial spaces are Euclidean balls
arxiv:2611.08265.summary: In this paper, we establish a matrix criterion for a space to be homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. As applications, we prove that the normalized space of $K$-Lorentzian polynomials on an arbitrary open convex cone $K$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball, giving an affirmative answer to Br\"and\'en and Leake's question, and we also settle Br\"and\'en's conjecture that the normalized space of homogeneous multiaffine real stable polynomials is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In addition, our results show that the normalized space of homogeneous $K$-stable polynomials of degree $d$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball.

arxiv:2611.08266.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
arxiv:2611.08266.summary: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice.

arxiv:2611.08289.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
arxiv:2611.08289.summary: Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube.
arxiv:2611.08289.authors: Fan Chang, Zhenyu Li, Guanghui Wang, Mingrui Wang

arxiv:2611.08320.title: Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators (revised and extended version)
arxiv:2611.08320.summary: Let $X$ be a separable locally compact metric space, let $E\neq\{0\}$ be a normed space, and let $G$ be a semigroup of continuous self-maps of $X$. Every $\varphi\in G$ induces the composition operator $C_\varphi f=f\circ\varphi$ on the space $C(X,E)$ of continuous functions endowed with the compact-open topology. We characterize the topological transitivity of the semigroup $\widehat{G}=\{C_\varphi:\varphi\in G\}$ by a condition that combines the run-away property of $G$ with an approximate form of injectivity, and we show that, when $E$ is separable, $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive if and only if it is hypercyclic.

arxiv:2611.08333.title: Butler's conjecture for K3 curves
arxiv:2611.08333.summary: Butler's conjectures predict that, on a general smooth curve $C$ of genus $g\ge3$, a general coherent system $[\mathcal{O}_C\otimes V\xrightarrow{\varphi}E]$ with semistable underlying bundle $E$ and $\dim V>\operatorname{rk}(E)$ has surjective evaluation map $\varphi$ and stable kernel. In this paper, we prove Butler's conjectures for $g\ge8$ in the two cases in which the Brill-Noether geometry of a general curve is known, namely rank one and the range $\mu(E)>2g-2$. By deformation and openness, it suffices to establish the result on a single Brill-Noether-Petri general curve.
arxiv:2611.08333.authors: Soheyla Feyzbakhsh, Aliaksandra Novik, Angela Ortega

arxiv:2611.08337.title: Kappa Classes on the KSBA Space of Stable Toric Pairs
arxiv:2611.08337.summary: We study kappa classes on the normalization of the main component of the Koll\'ar--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev(KSBA) moduli space of stable toric pairs. Using a toric model obtained by a lattice modification, we compute all kappa classes on the moduli space by giving a combinatorial formula for their intersection numbers with all torus-invariant cycles. In particular, we identify the first normalized kappa class with the GKZ polarization of the toric variety corresponding to the secondary polytope.

arxiv:2611.08353.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
arxiv:2611.08353.summary: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations…
arxiv:2611.08353.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci

arxiv:2611.08356.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
arxiv:2611.08356.summary: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula.
arxiv:2611.08356.authors: Asher Auel, Philip Engel, Kiran S. Kedlaya, Sair Shaikh

arxiv:2611.08357.title: Twisted Yangians of quasi-split type DI and Drinfeld type current relations
arxiv:2611.08357.summary: We study the twisted Yangian associated with the quasi-split symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{o}_{2n}, \mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ of type DI. Working in the transposed $R$-matrix presentation of arXiv:2607.14692, we show that the generating matrix $S(u)$ admits no Gaussian decomposition. We decompose instead the matrix $\widehat{S}(u) = G\,S(u)$, where $G$ is the constant term of $S(u)$.

arxiv:2611.08370.title: Modelling and analysis of a cocktail phage therapy with coinfection
arxiv:2611.08370.summary: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. We prove the global existence, uniqueness and nonnegativity of solutions, and the existence of an invariant region, under suitable conditions, in which the bacteria are eradicated exponentially fast. We determine the stability of the bacteria-free equilibrium in terms of the administered doses and give sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of coexistence equilibria, showing that coinfection may allow bacteria and phages to coexist even when the doses are large.
arxiv:2611.08370.authors: Xavier Bardina, Marc Cano, Silvia Cuadrado

arxiv:2611.08375.title: New results on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2611.08375.summary: Inspired by the work of Poljak, Ba\v{s}i\'c, Damnjanovi\'c, Stevanovi\'c, and Sto\v{s}i\'c used the Kissat SAT solver in a recent paper to systematically determine the small cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers of several families of graphs. By studying the patterns in their data, Ba\v{s}i\'c et al. formulated 15 conjectures on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers. In this paper, we confirm 9 of their conjectures, trace confirmations of 2 more to existing literature, and, perhaps surprisingly, disprove another one.
arxiv:2611.08375.authors: Gaurav Kucheriya, Jan Petr, Jun Yan

arxiv:2611.08384.title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichm\"uller Complex Manifold Structure
arxiv:2611.08384.summary: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichm\"uller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichm\"uller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles.

arxiv:2611.08391.title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
arxiv:2611.08391.summary: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.

arxiv:2611.08406.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
arxiv:2611.08406.summary: We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure. We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture.
arxiv:2611.08406.authors: Yueshi Hou, Hana Jia Kong, Zhouli Xu

arxiv:2611.08408.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-F{\o}lner sequences
arxiv:2611.08408.summary: We study the quantity $\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\phi(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $\Phi$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $\Phi$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $\phi\in\Phi$ of the limit of $\phi(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``F{\o}lnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is F\o lner.

arxiv:2611.08415.title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.08415.summary: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $\nu\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $\nu$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible.

arxiv:2611.08419.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
arxiv:2611.08419.summary: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

arxiv:2611.08421.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
arxiv:2611.08421.summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions.
arxiv:2611.08421.authors: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

arxiv:2611.08432.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
arxiv:2611.08432.summary: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. This implies the same upper bound on the asymptotic minimum degree threshold for $r$-partite graphs to admit a $K_r$-decomposition, using a well-known reduction.
arxiv:2611.08432.authors: Sean Longbrake, Michael Simkin, Liana Yepremyan, Michael Zheng

arxiv:2611.08451.title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
arxiv:2611.08451.summary: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families.

arxiv:2611.08455.title: Tusn\'ady's problem and online two-sample thinning
arxiv:2611.08455.summary: We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusn\'ady's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample.

arxiv:2611.08513.title: An Explicit Equation for the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Character Variety of $\mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$
arxiv:2611.08513.summary: Let $N$ denote the closed non-orientable surface of Euler characteristic $-1$, i.e. the connected sum of three real projective planes $N = \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$, with fundamental group presented as $\langle A,B,C \mid A^2 B^2 C^2 = I \rangle$ via the standard symmetric cross-cap model. Building on the classical trace-coordinate methods of Fricke, Vogt, and Goldman for free groups, and on the qualitative study of representation varieties of non-orientable surfaces by Benyash-Krivets and Chernousov, we give an explicit affine equation for a dense open piece of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ GIT character variety $X(N)$. We prove that the trace coordinates $a =…

arxiv:2611.08517.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
arxiv:2611.08517.summary: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them.
arxiv:2611.08517.authors: Yunpeng Meng, Baojun Wu, Tian Yang, Yuxuan Yang

arxiv:2611.08525.title: P\'osa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.08525.summary: We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $\gamma>0$, there exists $C=C(k,\gamma)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying \[ g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+\gamma\right) \binom{n-1}{k-1}p \qquad(1\le i<n/2) \] contains a Hamilton Berge cycle. The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic P\'osa-type theorem.
arxiv:2611.08525.authors: Liping Zhang, Ailian Chen, Qinghai Liu

arxiv:2611.08534.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
arxiv:2611.08534.summary: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction.

arxiv:2611.08547.title: Upper bound on the size of subgraphs avoiding cycles of girth length in graphs
arxiv:2611.08547.summary: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-free if it contains no copy of $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Although $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$ has been extensively studied for various specific graphs $G$, such as hypercubes, complete transposition graphs, and doubled Johnson graphs, very few results are known for general graphs.

arxiv:2611.08553.title: Algorithms for Short Human-Verifiable Proofs of Non-Word-Representability
arxiv:2611.08553.summary: A graph is word-representable if it can be represented using alternation of letters in words. The class of word-representable graphs generalizes several important graph families and admits a characterization via semi-transitive orientations. Recognizing word-representability is an NP-complete problem, and a major bottleneck in the theory of word-representable graphs is providing efficient justifications of non-word-representability of graphs, rather than merely referring to software verification.

arxiv:2611.08591.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
arxiv:2611.08591.summary: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers.
arxiv:2611.08591.authors: Alireza Behtash, Syo Kamata, Mauricio M. Martinez

arxiv:2611.08625.title: Singularities and Collision Criteria in the Gravitational Straight-Segment Problem with Arbitrary Positive Density
arxiv:2611.08625.summary: We study singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle around a fixed finite straight segment with an arbitrary positive continuous density. We first show that every singularity forces the trajectory to approach the material segment. Using the axial symmetry of the potential, we prove that any trajectory approaching the segment is confined to an invariant plane containing it.
arxiv:2611.08625.authors: F. Crespo, E. Mart\'{\i}nez, J. Vidarte, J. L. Zapata, A. Abdrabou

arxiv:2611.08627.title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
arxiv:2611.08627.summary: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum.

arxiv:2611.08653.title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
arxiv:2611.08653.summary: We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_\alpha f>\lambda\}\bigr) \lesssim_{\alpha,s} \frac1\lambda\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{\alpha,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-R\'ios and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction.

arxiv:2611.08674.title: Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers
arxiv:2611.08674.summary: We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration.

arxiv:2611.08679.title: Special line bundles on tetragonal curves
arxiv:2611.08679.summary: One can associate a pair of vector bundles $(E, F)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ to every tetragonal curve: $E$ is the Tschirnhausen bundle and $F$ records numerical data of the ideal for the curve under its relative canonical embedding. In this note, we show that a Hurwitz--Brill--Noether general tetragonal curve must have balanced $E$, $F$ bundles, and provide counterexamples for the converse when $g = 8$ or $g \geq 10$.

arxiv:2611.08692.title: Stability of large dynamical systems using Gershgorin Disc Theorem
arxiv:2611.08692.summary: Understanding the stability of large nonlinear dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in many fields, including biological, technological, and social networks. Traditional stability methods often rely on explicit eigenvalue calculations or the construction of Lyapunov functions, which become computationally difficult for large interconnected systems. In this work, we introduce a stability classifier that provides a computationally efficient way to determine the stability of complex systems without performing full spectral analysis.

arxiv:2611.08709.title: Levenshtein-type bounds for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes
arxiv:2611.08709.summary: We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal $s$-codes and for minimal energy) for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid $(a,b)$. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials).
arxiv:2611.08709.authors: Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Peter Dragnev, Peter Grabner

arxiv:2611.08760.title: Multi-monopoles and monodromy around the wobbly divisor
arxiv:2611.08760.summary: The multi-monopole equations are a generalisation of the Seiberg--Witten equations where the spinor is coupled to an auxiliary vector bundle. The signed count of multi-monopoles on a 3-manifold can vary according to a new type of wall-crossing phenomenon. For products $S^1\times C$, where $C$ is a closed Riemann surface, we relate the wall and chamber structure to loops in the complement of the wobbly divisor of $C$.

arxiv:2611.08773.title: Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
arxiv:2611.08773.summary: For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+\lambda/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction.
arxiv:2611.08773.authors: Alastair N. Fletcher, Gaven J. Martin

arxiv:2611.08796.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
arxiv:2611.08796.summary: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs.
arxiv:2611.08796.authors: Erik Brodsky, Leonid O Chekhov, Quanyu Tang

arxiv:2611.08806.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
arxiv:2611.08806.summary: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $\mu$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-\'Elie (1997) in dimension one.
arxiv:2611.08806.authors: Richard Aoun, Sara Brofferio, Marc Peign\'e

arxiv:2611.08810.title: Galois lines for the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two
arxiv:2611.08810.summary: We determine all Galois lines for the embedding of the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two into $\mathbb{P}^{3}$ induced by its Frobenius linear series. We also determine the associated Galois groups.

arxiv:2611.08819.title: Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices
arxiv:2611.08819.summary: Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$.

arxiv:2611.08833.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
arxiv:2611.08833.summary: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to…

arxiv:2611.08835.title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
arxiv:2611.08835.summary: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases.
arxiv:2611.08835.authors: Prosenjit Bose, Bobby Miraftab, Tyler Tuttle

arxiv:2611.08862.title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
arxiv:2611.08862.summary: We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $\chi_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $\chi_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows.

arxiv:2611.08885.title: KAM theory for quasi-periodic equilibrium of generalized Frenkel-Kontorova model in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$
arxiv:2611.08885.summary: We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.

arxiv:2611.08889.title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
arxiv:2611.08889.summary: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset.
arxiv:2611.08889.authors: Grigoriy Blekherman, Jiaheng Li, Jianuo Zhou

arxiv:2611.08890.title: A counterexample to Manin's Conjecture for almost Fano varieties
arxiv:2611.08890.summary: We give an example of a smooth rational threefold over a number field with a big anticanonical divisor that does not satisfy the thin set version of Manin's Conjecture. In particular, Manin's Conjecture does not hold for rationally connected almost Fano varieties.

arxiv:2611.08900.title: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories
arxiv:2611.08900.summary: Let $\C$ be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in $\Ind(\C)$ and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in $PSU(2)_k$ for odd $k\ge3$, in $SU(2)_{4m}$ for $m\ge1$, and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal M(2,p)$ for odd $p\ge5$.

arxiv:2611.08973.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
arxiv:2611.08973.summary: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits.
arxiv:2611.08973.authors: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov

arxiv:2611.08979.title: The splitting type of jet bundles on the projective line
arxiv:2611.08979.summary: Given a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on a smooth variety X, one can associate to it its jet bundles, or bundles of principal parts. These bundles encode the Taylor expansions of local sections of $\mathcal{E}$ and arise naturally in the study of differential operators. When $X=\mathbb{P}^1$ is the projective line, jet bundles decompose as direct sums of line bundles, making it natural to study their splitting types.
arxiv:2611.08979.authors: Annet Kyomuhangi, Emanuela Marangone, Claudiu Raicu, Ethan Reed

arxiv:2611.09000.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
arxiv:2611.09000.summary: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

arxiv:2611.09016.title: Twisted Verlinde Formula for Finite Cyclic Orbifolds of Vertex Operator Algebras
arxiv:2611.09016.summary: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold $\left(V^{\otimes k}\right)^{\langle g\rangle}$ associated with a $k$-cycle $g=(1\,2\,\cdots\,k)$.

arxiv:2611.09021.title: Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $\pi/2+\delta$
arxiv:2611.09021.summary: For every $\delta>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $\pi/2+\delta$.
arxiv:2611.09021.authors: Zhenkun Li, Jinmin Wang, Jing Yu

arxiv:2611.09034.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
arxiv:2611.09034.summary: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder.
arxiv:2611.09034.authors: Lei Liu, Pedro A. S. Salom\~ao

arxiv:2611.09049.title: Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
arxiv:2611.09049.summary: High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature.
arxiv:2611.09049.authors: Baoming Shi, Lei Zhang, Xiangcheng Zheng, Shangqin Zhu

arxiv:2611.09051.title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
arxiv:2611.09051.summary: We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.

arxiv:2611.09063.title: Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture
arxiv:2611.09063.summary: Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2\pi i/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$.

arxiv:2611.09064.title: Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.09064.summary: Let $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$.

arxiv:2611.09066.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
arxiv:2611.09066.summary: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems.
arxiv:2611.09066.authors: Antti K\"aenm\"aki, R. D\'aniel Prokaj, K\'aroly Simon, Sascha Troscheit

arxiv:2611.09072.title: Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
arxiv:2611.09072.summary: A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs.
arxiv:2611.09072.authors: Huaibin Zhou, Mingyang Guo, Xiumei Wang

arxiv:2611.09076.title: Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas
arxiv:2611.09076.summary: We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes.

arxiv:2611.09080.title: Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension
arxiv:2611.09080.summary: We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification.

arxiv:2611.09111.title: The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues
arxiv:2611.09111.summary: For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$.

arxiv:2611.09114.title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
arxiv:2611.09114.summary: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
arxiv:2611.09114.authors: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

arxiv:2611.09115.title: Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors
arxiv:2611.09115.summary: We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category.

arxiv:2611.09125.title: Every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most 6
arxiv:2611.09125.summary: We prove that every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most $6$. Weak-strict degeneracy is the weak degeneracy of Bernshteyn and Lee plus one, so it bounds the coloring parameters controlled by weak degeneracy. In particular, every IC-planar graph is $6$-choosable, $6$-DP-colorable and $6$-paintable, which strengthens the theorem of Yang, Wang, Wang and Lih that IC-planar graphs are $6$-choosable.
arxiv:2611.09125.authors: Zhen He, Yilong Li, Tao Wang, Xiaojing Yang

arxiv:2611.09143.title: Spectral Characterizations, Harmonic Analysis, and Phase Transitions in 2-Nice and $k$-Nice Recurrence
arxiv:2611.09143.summary: We investigate the structural mechanisms governing $2$-nice and $k$-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided $2$-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations $\{0, p_1(n), p_2(n)\}$ with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided $2$-nice recurrence.

arxiv:2611.09148.title: Campana points on quadrics with hyperplane boundary
arxiv:2611.09148.summary: Let $Q\subset\mathbf P^{d+1}_k$ be a smooth quadric of dimension $d\ge2$ over a number field, and let $H_i=Q\cap\Pi_i$ be hyperplane sections for $1\le i\le d$. For every integer $m\ge2$, we prove Campana strong approximation for the pair $\bigl(Q,(1-1/m)(H_1+\cdots+H_d)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)$.

arxiv:2611.09181.title: Hecke Algebras for Minimal Equicontinuous Cantor Actions
arxiv:2611.09181.summary: In this work we extend the concept of Hecke algebras to a pair of a separable infinite profinite group and a closed core-free subgroup. Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. We then prove that two minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions with isometric isomorphic Hecke algebras have the same Steinitz order.

arxiv:2611.09190.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures
arxiv:2611.09190.summary: For $0<\rho<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[ \mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1}, \qquad S_i(x)=\rho(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}\rho^j d_{\omega_j}$, where the symbols $\omega_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $\mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(\omega_1\mid X)>0$.

arxiv:2611.09215.title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
arxiv:2611.09215.summary: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\ll\eta\ll 1$.

arxiv:2611.09220.title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
arxiv:2611.09220.summary: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss.

arxiv:2611.09237.title: The Woo-Yong conjecture
arxiv:2611.09237.summary: We prove the Woo-Yong conjecture: the non-Gorenstein locus of a type A Schubert variety is the union of its generically non-Gorenstein maximal singular components. More strongly, at every scheme point, local Weil divisor classes are detected at the generic points of the maximal singular components containing that point. For arbitrary finite crystallographic type, the analogous localization map is injective on the torsion subgroup of the source local class group.

arxiv:2611.09284.title: Dominant root sequences of arbitrary degree
arxiv:2611.09284.summary: We show that for root-subgroup multiplication maps, dominance does not imply birationality. This gives a negative answer to a question of Fang, Fourier and Littelmann. More precisely, for every integer $r\geq 2$, we construct a sequence of positive roots in type $A_{3r-1}$; the associated multiplication map is dominant of generic degree $r$, hence not birational.
arxiv:2611.09284.authors: Ling Chen, Chongrui Li, Minggang Wei

arxiv:2611.09319.title: One complex metric and geometric adelic nefness
arxiv:2611.09319.summary: We prove that an arithmetic adelic line bundle on a smooth quasi-projective variety over a number field has nef geometric part if its prescribed continuous metric at one complex embedding has semipositive first Chern current. The proof constructs semiample approximations to every positive rational ample perturbation by boundary extension, multiplier ideals, and Nadel vanishing, followed by specialization and Galois descent. This gives geometric nefness of Gao--Zhang's canonical Gross--Schoen adelic line bundle.

arxiv:2611.09333.title: Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
arxiv:2611.09333.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $\Gamma$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, and Szegedy.
arxiv:2611.09333.authors: Ethan Ackelsberg, Asgar Jamneshan, Or Shalom

arxiv:2611.09347.title: A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph
arxiv:2611.09347.summary: In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph.

arxiv:2611.09352.title: On the existence of automorphisms acting expansively on the space of one-parameter subgroups of connected Lie groups
arxiv:2611.09352.summary: For a connected Lie group $G$, we consider the action of Aut$(G)$ on Sub$_G$, the set of all closed subgroups of $G$ endowed with the Chabauty topology. We study the action of automorphisms of $G$ on Sub$^p_G$, the closure of the set of all closed one-parameter subgroups of $G$ in Sub$_G$, in terms of expansivity. We show that a nontrivial connected Lie group $G$ with dim$(G)\geq 2$ does not admit any automorphism which acts expansively on Sub$^p_G$.

arxiv:2611.09357.title: On the Motzkin-Straus theorem and clique number for k-uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.09357.summary: In this paper, we establish a Motzkin-Straus type equality for k-uniform hypergraphs under certain conditions, which extends the classical Motzkin--Straus theorem for graphs. Using this equality, we present several spectral bounds for the clique number of k-uniform hypergraphs in terms of the spectral radii of the adjacency, signless Laplacian, and Laplacian tensors. When k=2, the bounds coincide with the corresponding known results for graphs.
arxiv:2611.09357.authors: Chunli Deng, Shaohuan Hao, Haifeng Li

arxiv:2611.09360.title: The center of an associative crossed module
arxiv:2611.09360.summary: In this paper, we define a Drinfeld-type center for an associative crossed module and prove that it is canonically the internal category of an explicit crossed module constructed from Mac Lane's bimultiplications. The resulting center carries a canonical multiplicative lifting, which induces a natural strict braiding, establishing its correspondence to a braided crossed module. We also examine the relationship between this center and Huq's categorical center.
arxiv:2611.09360.authors: Emzar Khmaladze, Manuel Ladra, David Quiroga, Brais Ramos P\'erez

arxiv:2611.09361.title: Positivity of metric entropy of the standard map at large parameters
arxiv:2611.09361.summary: We prove that the standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin2\pi x,\,y+k\sin2\pi x)$ of the two-torus satisfies $\log(2\pi k+4)-2^{430}\le h_m(f_k)\le\log(2\pi k+4)$ for every $k\ge\exp(2^{50000})$, where $h_m$ is the metric entropy with respect to area. Thus $h_m(f_k)=\log k+O(1)$, the order of growth observed numerically since Chirikov; in particular $h_m(f_k)>0$ for all large $k$ and $h_m(f_k)\to\infty$, as conjectured by Sinai. Moreover, for each fixed $c<1$ the points whose top Lyapunov exponent is below $c\log k$ fill an area $O(1/\log k)$.

arxiv:2611.09365.title: Tetragonal conic bundles
arxiv:2611.09365.summary: This paper addresses the birational geometry of three-dimensional algebraic varieties admitting a conic bundle structure. The central focus is on tetragonal transformations -- a special class of birational maps between standard conic bundles that are not fiberwise and play a key role in the birational geometry of such varieties.

arxiv:2611.09367.title: HOMFLY homology for oriented tangles
arxiv:2611.09367.summary: We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to arbitrary oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links $\mathcal{L}$, our construction recovers Khovanov and Rozansky's construction while removing the preliminary step of presenting $\mathcal{L}$ as a braid closure.

arxiv:2611.09369.title: Isomorphic classification of the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups $\mathrm{SL}_2$
arxiv:2611.09369.summary: We classify, up to isomorphism, the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups SL 2 .
arxiv:2611.09369.authors: Julien Bichon (LMBP), Thi Hoa Emilie Nguyen (LMBP)

arxiv:2611.09415.title: Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals
arxiv:2611.09415.summary: We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations.

arxiv:2611.09416.title: A 4-regular graph with 4/5 of its vertices satisfying the \v{S}olt\'es property
arxiv:2611.09416.summary: The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of its vertices. A vertex $v$ is called a \v{S}olt\'es vertex if $G-v$ is connected and $W(G-v)=W(G)$. Since the cycle $C_{11}$ is the only known graph in which every vertex is a \v{S}olt\'es vertex, a natural problem is to construct other graphs with as large a proportion of such vertices as possible.

arxiv:2611.09453.title: Every countable group has the nonsingular weak Rokhlin property
arxiv:2611.09453.summary: We prove that for every countable group $\Gamma$, in the space of nonsingular actions by $\Gamma$, there is an action whose orbit under conjugation is dense. This is the nonsingular analogue of the result of Glasner, Thouvenot, and Weiss that every countable group $\Gamma$ is weak Rokhlin, i.e., there is a dense orbit in the space of probability measure preserving $\Gamma$-actions.
arxiv:2611.09453.authors: Garrett Ervin, Bogl\'arka Geh\'er, Anett Imolay-Kocsis, M\'at\'e P\'alfy, Jenna Zomback

arxiv:2611.09465.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
arxiv:2611.09465.summary: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs.
arxiv:2611.09465.authors: Logan Geenis, Manfred Hartl, Tim Van der Linden

arxiv:2611.09513.title: Mutual-visibility in (d, 5)-graphs with excess
arxiv:2611.09513.summary: The author investigates mutual visibility in regular graphs of girth at least 5, with particular emphasis on graphs with excess. A general upper bound on the mutual-visibility number is established in terms of the degree and order. More significantly, an algebraic inequality is derived that restricts the mutual-visibility number of $(d,5,+\delta)$-graphs.

arxiv:2611.09523.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
arxiv:2611.09523.summary: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).

arxiv:2611.09532.title: Fujita's Very Ampleness Conjecture for $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$-Bundles over Curves
arxiv:2611.09532.summary: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a vector bundle of rank $n\geq 2$ over a smooth projective curve $C$ over $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that $K_{\mathbb{P}_C(\mathcal{E})}+\mathcal{L}_1+\dots+\mathcal{L}_k$ is very ample for arbitrary ample line bundles $\mathcal{L}_i$ when $k\geq n+2$.

arxiv:2611.09537.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
arxiv:2611.09537.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$.

arxiv:2611.09557.title: The splitting of the stable space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms
arxiv:2611.09557.summary: We prove that the space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms on a smooth $G$-manifold $M$ has a tom Dieck style splitting, after stabilization. As an intermediate step, we introduce a space of isovariant $h$-cobordisms on $M$ and prove that this space also has a splitting, even before stabilizing. This completes the proof of the equivariant version of Waldhausen's stable parametrized $h$-cobordism theorem.
arxiv:2611.09557.authors: Thomas Goodwillie, Kiyoshi Igusa, Cary Malkiewich, Mona Merling

arxiv:2611.09564.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
arxiv:2611.09564.summary: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions.
arxiv:2611.09564.authors: Abhishek Sharma, Ayushi Suman, Mehernaz Anvari, Manish Dev Shrimali, Charo I. del Genio, Sarika Jalan

arxiv:2611.09603.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
arxiv:2611.09603.summary: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field.

arxiv:2611.09608.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
arxiv:2611.09608.summary: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case.
arxiv:2611.09608.authors: Yanqiao Jia, Xueting Zhao, Yichuan Yang

arxiv:2611.09610.title: New persistent chain spaces: identifying and computing the relevant persistent Laplacians of a filtration
arxiv:2611.09610.summary: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret.

arxiv:2611.09613.title: Some normal abelian surfaces in $\mathbf{P}^3$
arxiv:2611.09613.summary: Every complex projective surface is birational to a singular surface $S \subseteq \mathbf{P}^3$, but it is unclear whether one can ask that $S$ have only isolated singularities. In particular, it was a folk question as to whether an abelian surface could admit such a model. We present examples to show that there do exist normal abelian surfaces in $\mathbf{P}^3$.
arxiv:2611.09613.authors: Nathan Chen, Robert Lazarsfeld, Federico Moretti

arxiv:2611.09627.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
arxiv:2611.09627.summary: Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.
arxiv:2611.09627.authors: Jadwiga Czy\.zewska, Tom\'a\v{s} Masa\v{r}\'ik, Marcin Pilipczuk, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski

arxiv:2611.09633.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
arxiv:2611.09633.summary: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$.
arxiv:2611.09633.authors: Jane Ivy Coons, Ben Hollering, Niharika Chakrabarty Paul

arxiv:2611.09638.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
arxiv:2611.09638.summary: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane developed by Haiman.
arxiv:2611.09638.authors: Peter L. Guo, Mingyang Kang, Changjian Su, Rui Xiong

arxiv:2611.09675.title: The maximum size of $3$-distance binary codes
arxiv:2611.09675.summary: In this paper, we show that for every positive integer $n \ge 24$, the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of vectors from $\{-1,1\}^n$ with at most three distinct Hamming distances is equal to $\binom{n}{3}+n$. The threshold $n=24$ is best possible.
arxiv:2611.09675.authors: Valjakas Djaljapayan, Hao Huang, Wei-Hsuan Yu

arxiv:2611.09697.title: Finite-Scale Folding and Maximal Asymptotic Variance
arxiv:2611.09697.summary: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.

arxiv:2611.09718.title: How many points does it take to see the homotopy of a space? Minimal acyclic categorical models
arxiv:2611.09718.summary: Every connected homotopy type is the classifying space of a small category, but this general result gives little control over the categories involved. We study finite acyclic categorical models and measure their complexity by the number of objects. Our main tool is the sink lemma, which describes the addition of a sink as the attachment of a cone along an explicit map.

arxiv:2611.09774.title: Exploring the Regular and Singular Loci of Group Representation Varieties
arxiv:2611.09774.summary: Let $B$ be the Borel Subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$, and let $G_m=\langle x,y,z\mid x^2y^3=z^{2m+1}\rangle$, $m\geq2$. The $G_m$ are parafree of rank two and deviation one. We compute the integral homology of the regular and singular loci of $X_m=\mathrm{Hom}(G_m,B)$.

arxiv:2611.09844.title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
arxiv:2611.09844.summary: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$. The resulting score has mean $(3/2)^d$ for every partition, while its distribution reflects the geometry of the tiling.

arxiv:2611.09874.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
arxiv:2611.09874.summary: We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$.
arxiv:2611.09874.authors: Samuel Bronstein, Thomas Le Fils, Arnaud Maret

arxiv:2611.09883.title: Analytic information encoded in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of genus-one plane branches
arxiv:2611.09883.summary: We give an explicit formula recovering the Zariski invariant of a plane branch with one Puiseux pair from its Bernstein-Sato polynomial. Thus the Bernstein-Sato stratification refines the Zariski-invariant stratification. We determine the generic roots in each stratum from the value semigroup and the Zariski invariant, refining Yano's description for a fixed topological class.

arxiv:2611.09886.title: Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores
arxiv:2611.09886.summary: We prove that for any regular CW-complex $X$ there exists a quotient map $X\to Y$ that is a weak homotopy equivalence and which is minimal with that property, meaning that any quotient $Y\to Z$ that is a weak equivalence, must be a homeomorphism. The space $Y$ we obtain is an Alexandroff space: a space in which arbitrary intersections of open sets are open. The weak core $Y$ of $X$ is not unique in general.

arxiv:2611.09976.title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$
arxiv:2611.09976.summary: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.
arxiv:2611.09976.authors: Matthias Kreck, Yang Su, Shengye Zhu

arxiv:2611.09981.title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
arxiv:2611.09981.summary: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $\mu^3_3$, where $\mu_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

arxiv:2611.09995.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
arxiv:2611.09995.summary: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability.
arxiv:2611.09995.authors: Simone Betteti, Matteo Martin, Morten Gram Pedersen, Sandro Zampieri, Giacomo Baggio

arxiv:2611.10010.title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
arxiv:2611.10010.summary: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $\sigma$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures.

arxiv:2611.10053.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
arxiv:2611.10053.summary: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.
arxiv:2611.10053.authors: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto

arxiv:2611.10069.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
arxiv:2611.10069.summary: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions.

arxiv:2611.10078.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
arxiv:2611.10078.summary: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal…

arxiv:2611.10081.title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
arxiv:2611.10081.summary: In this paper, we study the map $\Theta$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$, including the optimal H\"older exponent of $\Theta^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $\Theta$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $\Theta$ has an infinite derivative.

arxiv:2611.10104.title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
arxiv:2611.10104.summary: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula.

arxiv:2611.10131.title: Adaptive visualization for enumerative problems
