arxiv:2611.10131.summary: We present an adaptive visualization framework and its implementation in the julia package AdaptiveVisualization.jl. Our algorithm visualizes functions using an adaptive sampling procedure that concentrates the evaluation budget at interesting regions of the domain. We illustrate our package on our main application: visualizing parameter spaces of enumerative problems.

arxiv:2611.10143.title: Discrete Spoilers: Introducing Abstract Undergraduate Mathematics Using Graph Theory
arxiv:2611.10143.summary: Students often have serious difficulties with many key concepts of the undergraduate mathematics curriculum. We argue that many of these difficulties can be eased by explicitly separating the key ideas from the technical details. To do so, we present finite graphs as a setting where the basic concepts appear more transparently, because on a graph most proofs only require basic techniques from linear algebra.

arxiv:2611.10154.title: Bijecting $m$-Tamari intervals, trees, and tight gradings
arxiv:2611.10154.summary: Tight gradings, which are certain integer gradings on maximal Dyck paths, provide a combinatorial framework for computing all coefficients of wall-functions in rank-$2$ cluster scattering diagrams. We construct a bijection between a special subset of tight gradings and the intervals of the $m$-Tamari lattice, providing a new combinatorial proof of the central wall-function formula proved by Reineke. Inspired by the structure of these gradings, we introduce a class of plane trees called $m$-leafy trees that give a new model for $m$-Tamari intervals.
arxiv:2611.10154.authors: Amanda Burcroff, Kyungyong Lee, Lang Mou

arxiv:2611.10159.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
arxiv:2611.10159.summary: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.
arxiv:2611.10159.authors: A. Yu. Savin, K. N. Zhuikov

arxiv:2611.10167.title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
arxiv:2611.10167.summary: We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $\phi^\star(\alpha)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula.

arxiv:2611.10196.title: Questions of minimality for DDMOGs and cycle ornaments
arxiv:2611.10196.summary: Difference distance magic oriented graphs (DDMOGs) are oriented graphs whose vertices admit a bijective labeling by consecutive positive integers such that every vertex has weight zero, where the weight is the sum of the labels of its in-neighbors minus the sum of the labels of its out-neighbors. We investigate minimality and sparsity questions for DDMOGs and their ornaments. First, we develop new constructions of cycle-based ornaments that reduce the number of cycles required for a given number of attachment nodes and identify minimal cycle lengths in several cases.
arxiv:2611.10196.authors: Roza Aceska, McKailyn Lort, Allison Ripperger, Zach Wilcher

arxiv:2611.10200.title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
arxiv:2611.10200.summary: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.

arxiv:2611.10221.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
arxiv:2611.10221.summary: We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model.
arxiv:2611.10221.authors: Xiangye Xu, Sue Ann Campbell, Francis J. Poulin

arxiv:2611.10243.title: A tale of two periodicities
arxiv:2611.10243.summary: We provide a common explanation for two 4-periodic phenomena arising in the study of connective real K-theory: first, the family of twists of ko over $B\mathbb Z/2$, and second, the torsion in the Picard group of $Q_1$-local $\mathcal A(1)$-modules. These phenomena have been previously studied, as they lead to 4-periodic patterns in Smith homomorphisms, resp. in the ko-homology of $(B\mathbb Z/2)^n$. In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.
arxiv:2611.10243.authors: Arun Debray, Cameron Krulewski, Natalia Pacheco-Tallaj

arxiv:2611.10250.title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
arxiv:2611.10250.summary: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_\gamma - \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates.

arxiv:2611.10255.title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
arxiv:2611.10255.summary: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic.

arxiv:2611.10276.title: Semifree actions and representation varieties
arxiv:2611.10276.summary: A group action on a topological space induces an action on the space's representation variety. We determine the fixed point sets of this latter action for semifree group actions on surfaces and circle bundles over surfaces. We also discuss implications for mapping tori of periodic maps.
arxiv:2611.10276.authors: Patrick Dendis, David L. Duncan, Timothy Tarter, Lior Weber, Colin Willette

arxiv:2611.10299.title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
arxiv:2611.10299.summary: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|\chi_u+\chi_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.

arxiv:2611.10311.title: Up or down by half: a family of Collatz-type maps
arxiv:2611.10311.summary: Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers.

arxiv:2611.10328.title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
arxiv:2611.10328.summary: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists.

arxiv:2611.10350.title: Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property
arxiv:2611.10350.summary: We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets.
arxiv:2611.10350.authors: Xue Liu, Xiaomin Zhou, Xiaoyao Zhou

arxiv:2611.10381.title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
arxiv:2611.10381.summary: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives.

arxiv:2611.10384.title: Generalized near-group tensor categories
arxiv:2611.10384.summary: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite tensor category with exactly one isomorphism class of simple objects which are non-invertible. Semisimple tensor categories $\mathcal{D}$ with this property are called near-group categories, and have been studied by Evans, Gannon, Siehler and others. In this paper, we study such categories in the non-semisimple setting, with the additional assumption that the non-invertible simple object is projective.

arxiv:2611.10391.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
arxiv:2611.10391.summary: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.

arxiv:2611.10408.title: Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices
arxiv:2611.10408.summary: List replicability measures how many accurate hypotheses suffice to contain the output of a learning rule with arbitrarily high confidence. We prove that every nonempty class of $m$ binary concepts on $n$ domain points has list replicability at most $805\ln(2m)\ln(2n)$. This resolves the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak.

arxiv:2611.10409.title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
arxiv:2611.10409.summary: In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and \c{S}ahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions.
arxiv:2611.10409.authors: Chunlin Liu, Kairan Liu, Tao Yu

arxiv:2611.10415.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
arxiv:2611.10415.summary: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.
arxiv:2611.10415.authors: Kenneth Ascher, Kristin DeVleming, Hongyu Luo, Yuchen Liu, Junyan Zhao

arxiv:2611.10426.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
arxiv:2611.10426.summary: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes.
arxiv:2611.10426.authors: Jayan Mukherjee, with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar

arxiv:2611.10437.title: Bulgarian solitaire with distinguishable cells
arxiv:2611.10437.summary: Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells.

arxiv:2611.10438.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
arxiv:2611.10438.summary: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits.

arxiv:2611.10478.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
arxiv:2611.10478.summary: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM…

arxiv:2611.10495.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
arxiv:2611.10495.summary: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings.
arxiv:2611.10495.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu

arxiv:2611.10519.title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
arxiv:2611.10519.summary: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

arxiv:2611.10526.title: On the structural aspects of Convex Subhyperlattices under different orders
arxiv:2611.10526.summary: Nayak et al. (2025) introduced the concept of convex subhyperlattices of a strong join hyperlattice $\mathfrak{L}$ and demonstrated that the collection of all convex subhyperlattices, $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$, together with empty set, forms a lattice. In particular, for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices, they obtained a unique representation of convex subhyperlattices in terms of hyperideals and hyperfilters.
arxiv:2611.10526.authors: N Aishwarya Nayak, Bhargava K, Pallavi Panjarike, Kuncham Syam Prasad, Tapatee Sahoo, Harikrishnan Panackal

arxiv:2611.10557.title: The cofinite regularity spectrum of $F$-irregular graphs
arxiv:2611.10557.summary: For a connected graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if the numbers of copies of $F$ containing its vertices are pairwise distinct. We characterize which connected patterns admit regular $F$-irregular hosts of every sufficiently large degree. Stars admit no regular $F$-irregular host; for every other $F$, every sufficiently large integer $r$ is realized by a connected $r$-regular $F$-irregular graph of diameter two and order $r+o(r)$, optimal to first order.

arxiv:2611.10563.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
arxiv:2611.10563.summary: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry.
arxiv:2611.10563.authors: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Shuangshuang Yin

arxiv:2611.10580.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
arxiv:2611.10580.summary: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion.

arxiv:2611.10624.title: A Simple Computer-Assisted Proof of the 5/6-Bound for Real-Period Pinwheel Scheduling
arxiv:2611.10624.summary: In pinwheel scheduling with real periods, an instance consists of $n$ tasks with real periods $1\le a_1\le a_2\le\cdots\le a_n$. The goal is to find a schedule that assigns one task to each day indefinitely such that, for every task $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every positive integer $\ell$, task $i$ occurs at least $\ell$ times in every block of $\lceil\ell a_i\rceil$ consecutive days. Given an instance $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n)$, its dimension is $n$, its density is $\sum_{i=1}^n1/a_i$, and its potential is $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}1/a_i$.
arxiv:2611.10624.authors: Hiroshi Fujiwara, Grzegorz Gutowski, Katsuhisa Ouchi, Alexander Wolff

arxiv:2611.10645.title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
arxiv:2611.10645.summary: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.

arxiv:2611.10654.title: A Lie-theoretic approach to the type $C_n^{(1)}$ partitions of Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc
arxiv:2611.10654.summary: Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc (CMPP) extended the frequency conditions in Gordon's partition theorem to paths in coloured arrays. Their conjecture for type $C_n^{(1)}$ identifies the generating function of admissible arrays with a principally specialized character. We prove this conjecture for arbitrary boundary data by constructing an ordered Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) basis of the corresponding integrable highest weight module.

arxiv:2611.10701.title: Weighted Matroid Intersection under Minimum Rank Oracle
arxiv:2611.10701.summary: We consider matroid intersection under the minimum rank oracle model, in which two matroids are accessible only through an oracle that returns the minimum of the ranks of a given set in the two matroids. By Edmonds' theorem, this oracle determines the matroid intersection polytope, although it does not reveal the exchangeability graphs on which classical algorithms rely. Recent work by B\'ar\'asz, B\'erczi, Kir\'aly, Oki, Yamaguchi, and Yokoi (2025) showed that unweighted matroid intersection is polynomially solvable in this model.

arxiv:2611.10702.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
arxiv:2611.10702.summary: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$.
arxiv:2611.10702.authors: Zhuo Cheng, Yeyao Hu, Deyu Yu

arxiv:2611.10716.title: The $\nu$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
arxiv:2611.10716.summary: We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $\nu$-Tamari lattice introduced by Pr\'eville-Ratelle and Viennot.

arxiv:2611.10735.title: A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5
arxiv:2611.10735.summary: We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid.

arxiv:2611.10761.title: Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
arxiv:2611.10761.summary: Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors.
arxiv:2611.10761.authors: E. Arthur Robinson, Jr., Ay\c{s}e A. \c{S}ahin

arxiv:2611.10777.title: On maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere
arxiv:2611.10777.summary: We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem.

arxiv:2611.10788.title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
arxiv:2611.10788.summary: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-depth; this depth governs connectivity.
arxiv:2611.10788.authors: Vu A. Le, Hoa Q. Duong, Tuan A. Nguyen

arxiv:2611.10805.title: Abelian categories and double d\'ecalage
arxiv:2611.10805.summary: We show that an additive category is abelian if and only if its functorial nerve is a double d\'ecalage of a pseudo-simplicial object in Cat. In this characterization, the canonical isomorphism between the image and coimage is encoded by a coherent pseudo-simplicial identity.

arxiv:2611.10813.title: An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$
arxiv:2611.10813.summary: For each partition $\lambda$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^\lambda$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_\tau$, where $\tau$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$, $x_\tau$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $\tau$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem.

arxiv:2611.10823.title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
arxiv:2611.10823.summary: For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle. As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space.

arxiv:2611.10827.title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
arxiv:2611.10827.summary: We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening.
arxiv:2611.10827.authors: Artur Akhiiarov, Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Andrei Raigorodskii

arxiv:2611.10862.title: Spectral distribution for biased orientations of random graphs
arxiv:2611.10862.summary: We study the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind for biased orientations of Erdos-Renyi random graphs. In the model $D(n,p,p')$, an edge is present with probability $p$ and, conditional on its presence, is directed from its smaller to its larger endpoint with probability $p'$. Both parameters may depend on $n$, and biased tournaments are the special case $D(n,1,p')$.

arxiv:2611.10879.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
arxiv:2611.10879.summary: The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$.

arxiv:2611.10883.title: The Brualdi--Quinn conjecture on strong edge-coloring holds fractionally and asymptotically
arxiv:2611.10883.summary: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A$ and $B$, and let $\Delta_A$ and $\Delta_B$ be the maximum degrees of the vertices in $A$ and in $B$, respectively. Brualdi and Quinn conjectured that the strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $\Delta_A\Delta_B$. We prove that the fractional strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $\Delta_A\Delta_B$, and that the conjecture holds asymptotically: $\chi_s'(G)\le(1+o(1))\Delta_A\Delta_B$ as $\max\{\Delta_A,\Delta_B\}\to\infty$.
arxiv:2611.10883.authors: Rong Luo, Gexin Yu, Xiangqian Zhou

arxiv:2611.10885.title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
arxiv:2611.10885.summary: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincar\'e series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to…

arxiv:2611.10899.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
arxiv:2611.10899.summary: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bella\"iche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$.

arxiv:2611.10918.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
arxiv:2611.10918.summary: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S.

arxiv:2611.10919.title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
arxiv:2611.10919.summary: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa.

arxiv:2611.10920.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
arxiv:2611.10920.summary: We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences.

arxiv:2611.10927.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
arxiv:2611.10927.summary: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

arxiv:2611.10951.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
arxiv:2611.10951.summary: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

arxiv:2611.10953.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
arxiv:2611.10953.summary: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others.

arxiv:2611.10978.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms
arxiv:2611.10978.summary: The Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

arxiv:2611.10985.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
arxiv:2611.10985.summary: Given a graph $\Gamma$ with vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $\Gamma$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $\Gamma\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}.

arxiv:2611.10995.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
arxiv:2611.10995.summary: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $\Sigma(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $\Sigma(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $\Sigma(p_c)$ completely: $\Sigma(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by…

arxiv:2611.11002.title: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
arxiv:2611.11002.summary: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample.

arxiv:2611.11026.title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
arxiv:2611.11026.summary: We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is…
arxiv:2611.11026.authors: Ever F. Cruzado-Quispe, Javier L\'opez-de-la-Cruz, Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

arxiv:2611.11056.title: Non-log-concave $\tau$-polynomials of regular graphs
arxiv:2611.11056.summary: For any simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for any $j\ge 1$ and $x^{\langle0\rangle}=1$. Brenti (1992) introduced the $\tau$-polynomial and its augmented version, defined by $$\tau(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}c_jx^j, \qquad \overline{\tau}(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}j!c_jx^j.$$ He asked whether $\tau(G,x)$ always has only real roots and whether $\overline{\tau}(G,x)$ always has a log-concave coefficient sequence. In this paper, we show that for any integer $d\ge 4$, there exists an integer $h_d$ such that, for every connected…

arxiv:2611.11069.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
arxiv:2611.11069.summary: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models.

arxiv:2611.11092.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
arxiv:2611.11092.summary: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O.

arxiv:2611.11126.title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
arxiv:2611.11126.summary: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.
arxiv:2611.11126.authors: Fan Chung, Namiko Matsumoto, Arya Mazumdar

arxiv:2611.11128.title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
arxiv:2611.11128.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and let $\tau(G)$ be the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. We prove $\tau(G)\le2\nu(G)$ when each edge belongs to at most four triangles, the edges belonging to four triangles form components with at most two edges, and the maximum average degree is at most $25/2$. No upper bound on maximum vertex degree is imposed.

arxiv:2611.11161.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
arxiv:2611.11161.summary: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness.

arxiv:2611.11171.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
arxiv:2611.11171.summary: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields.

arxiv:2611.11184.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
arxiv:2611.11184.summary: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

arxiv:2611.11185.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
arxiv:2611.11185.summary:
By a $	extit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $
u$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $
u(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $
u(x)= ot$, where $ ot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{ ot,	op\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian.
arxiv:2611.11185.authors: Kishan Dayaram, Zurab Janelidze, Ronald Kerario

arxiv:2611.11187.title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
arxiv:2611.11187.summary: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Buci\'c and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$.

arxiv:2611.11191.title: Token graphs of stars
arxiv:2611.11191.summary: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ has as vertices the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. Let $S_n$ be the star with $n$ leaves. Since every edge of $S_n$ is incident with the center, $F_k(S_n)$ is the inclusion graph of the $(k-1)$- and the $k$-subsets of the leaves.
arxiv:2611.11191.authors: Emmanuel Acosta Troncoso, C\'esar Hern\'andez-Cruz, Ana Trujillo-Negrete

arxiv:2611.11195.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
arxiv:2611.11195.summary: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to…

arxiv:2611.11203.title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
arxiv:2611.11203.summary: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible.
arxiv:2611.11203.authors: Pholphum Kamthorntaksina, Teeradej Kittipassorn, Patid Srikirinth, Puttimet Tulabadee, Nattaporn Witchayapongkul

arxiv:2611.11205.title: Independence number and odd dominating models
arxiv:2611.11205.summary: A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i<j\leq t$. Let $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model.
arxiv:2611.11205.authors: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, David R. Wood, Jung Hon Yip

arxiv:2611.11207.title: On the K\H{o}nig-Egerv\'{a}ry theorem for $k$-trees
arxiv:2611.11207.summary: The famous K\H{o}nig-Egerv\'{a}ry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths.

arxiv:2611.11240.title: Stretched near-groups
arxiv:2611.11240.summary: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$.
arxiv:2611.11240.authors: Andrew Schopieray, Yilong Wang, Zhiqiang Yu

arxiv:2611.11247.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
arxiv:2611.11247.summary: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.
arxiv:2611.11247.authors: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Christoforos Neofytidis

arxiv:2611.11257.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
arxiv:2611.11257.summary: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples.
arxiv:2611.11257.authors: Benjamin M. Kent, Richard E. Turner

arxiv:2611.11259.title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
arxiv:2611.11259.summary: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters.

arxiv:2611.11269.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
arxiv:2611.11269.summary: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c\oe ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion…

arxiv:2611.11270.title: Onsager--Machlup Theory and Transition Pathways for Degenerate Stochastic Systems with Multiplicative Noise
arxiv:2611.11270.summary: Noise-induced transitions between metastable states are central to many nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems, and most probable transition pathways provide an effective means of revealing the underlying transition mechanisms. In this work, we develop an Onsager--Machlup framework for degenerate stochastic dynamical systems driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise. We first derive the Onsager--Machlup action functional for the additive-noise case using the Girsanov transformation, and then extend the result to multiplicative noise through a Lamperti-type transformation.
arxiv:2611.11270.authors: Weichen Wu, Ying Chao, Jinqiao Duan

arxiv:2611.11280.title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
arxiv:2611.11280.summary: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$.

arxiv:2611.11287.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
arxiv:2611.11287.summary: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

arxiv:2611.11294.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
arxiv:2611.11294.summary: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego.
arxiv:2611.11294.authors: Ke Wang, Qiang Zhang, Anlan Zhao

arxiv:2611.11298.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
arxiv:2611.11298.summary: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$.
arxiv:2611.11298.authors: Xubin Hu, Liming Ma, Yipeng Wang

arxiv:2611.11300.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
arxiv:2611.11300.summary: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish.

arxiv:2611.11321.title: Monk and Pieri rules for forest polynomials
arxiv:2611.11321.summary: This article gives Pieri rules for forest polynomials and Monk rule for double forest polynomials. We construct binary relations $\lessdot_i$ and $\prec_i$ based on the local Tamari moves on indexed forests. These relations are explicit and constructive.
arxiv:2611.11321.authors: Haojun Bai, Shu Xiao Li, David G. L. Wang

arxiv:2611.11345.title: Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture
arxiv:2611.11345.summary: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices.

arxiv:2611.11352.title: Zero forcing is not unimodal
arxiv:2611.11352.summary: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal.

arxiv:2611.11358.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
arxiv:2611.11358.summary: We introduce the landscape velocity $\xi$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $\xi$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual…

arxiv:2611.11362.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
arxiv:2611.11362.summary: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.

arxiv:2611.11369.title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
arxiv:2611.11369.summary: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincar\'e disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition.
arxiv:2611.11369.authors: Chunlin Li, Erxiao Wang, Jie Wu, Min Yan

arxiv:2611.11375.title: Linear Objective Problems: A Complexity Framework for Bilevel Optimization
arxiv:2611.11375.summary: Many bilevel and robust optimization problems are complete for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, but such results are usually proven one problem at a time with problem-specific reductions. A recurring obstacle is that the lower level must select an optimal solution rather than merely a feasible one, whereas standard reductions preserve only whether a solution exists, not which solutions are optimal. We introduce linear objective problems (LOP), a framework for optimization problems whose solutions are explicit subsets of a ground set and whose objective is linear in these elements.
arxiv:2611.11375.authors: Christoph Gr\"une, James B. Orlin, Lasse Wulf

arxiv:2611.11406.title: Snowflake $q$-Flipping
arxiv:2611.11406.summary: We prove a weighted extension of Byun's snowflake-flipping theorem for cored hexagons with unit triangular holes along three crossing lines. The ratio of the tiling generating functions of two regions related by a snowflake flip is given by an explicit product. The result recovers Byun's theorem when all lozenge weights are 1 and resolves an open problem posed by the author in 2024.

arxiv:2611.11407.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
arxiv:2611.11407.summary: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

arxiv:2611.11414.title: The strong cylinder conjecture and R\'edei's factorization conjecture in three dimensions
arxiv:2611.11414.summary: In this paper, we prove the strong cylinder conjecture, that is, for every prime $p$, a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathbb F_p^3$ that meets every affine plane in a multiple of $p$ points is a union of $p$ distinct parallel affine lines. We use this result to resolve R\'edei's 1970 factorization conjecture in three dimensions: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ contain zero and every vector in $\mathbb F_p^3$ has a unique expression $a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, then one of the two sets is contained in a plane through zero.
arxiv:2611.11414.authors: Haihua Deng, Weicong Li, Weiye Zhang

arxiv:2611.11463.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
arxiv:2611.11463.summary: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.

arxiv:2611.11476.title: On the Complexity of Extending Prescribed Linear Forests to Hamiltonian Cycles in Hypercubes
arxiv:2611.11476.summary: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $P\subseteq E(Q_n)$ be a set of prescribed edges. It is known that, for $n\ge 2$, every such set $P$ with $|P|\leq 2n-3$ whose edges form a linear forest is contained in a Hamiltonian cycle of $Q_n$. This bound is sharp for general linear forests.

arxiv:2611.11502.title: Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism
arxiv:2611.11502.summary: Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper separates their program into the working hypothesis H, that Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra, and the claim P placed on top of it, that language and physics obey the same principle, and examines the validity of H. MCB employs two coproducts in formulating Merge, corresponding to two different translations of movement (Internal Merge): $\Delta_d$, which deletes the lower copy, and $\Delta_c$, which leaves a trace.

arxiv:2611.11513.title: Induced-Minor-Free Graphs Admit a Star-Based Separator of Size $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$
arxiv:2611.11513.summary: Given an $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, we construct a balanced separator of $G$ consisting of $\tilde{O}(|V(H)|\sqrt{n})$ star subgraphs. Our result is an induced-minor-free analog of the famous separator theorem for $H$-minor-free graphs by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [J. Amer.
arxiv:2611.11513.authors: Arnold Filtser, Nikolai Karol, Hung Le, Florian Lehner

arxiv:2611.11521.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
arxiv:2611.11521.summary: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation.
arxiv:2611.11521.authors: Santosh Mohan Rajkumar, Sriram Narayanan, Samuel E. Otto, Debdipta Goswami

arxiv:2611.11543.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
arxiv:2611.11543.summary: We prove versions of (variations of) Erd\H{o}s sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.

arxiv:2611.11559.title: Multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity
arxiv:2611.11559.summary: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the nonnegative integers, closed under addition and with finite complement. The size of the complement is its genus. The problem of counting semigroups by the largest gap got very important through the so-called Frobenius problem, first documented in 1884.

arxiv:2611.11575.title: Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$
arxiv:2611.11575.summary: Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices).

arxiv:2611.11593.title: Kronecker coefficients of large degree and Littlewood-Richardson inequalities
arxiv:2611.11593.summary: We prove that Kronecker coefficients are uniformly asymptotic to $f^\lambda f^\mu f^\nu/n!$ when all three irreducible dimensions are at least $\sqrt{n!}\,e^{-A\sqrt n}$, for any fixed $A>0$. This strengthens a conjecture of Pak, Panova and Yeliussizov. For triple staircase and triple square partitions, we obtain relative asymptotics with respective limiting factors $e^{-1/24}$ and $e^{-1/3}$.

arxiv:2611.11623.title: When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals
arxiv:2611.11623.summary: We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets.

arxiv:2611.11628.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
arxiv:2611.11628.summary: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $\eta$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences.

arxiv:2611.11631.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
arxiv:2611.11631.summary: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces.

arxiv:2611.11641.title: Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
arxiv:2611.11641.summary: We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $\pi$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(\pi z))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(\pi z))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $\mu_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $\mu_f(O_{1,2}) = \mu_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $\Phi_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}\Phi_j(z)$ with Koenigs…
arxiv:2611.11641.authors: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}, Emrah Yurtseven, Murat Emre \"Ozkaya

arxiv:2611.11660.title: On sinks and mirrors
arxiv:2611.11660.summary: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror.

arxiv:2611.11672.title: Pointed Hopf Algebras from Pale Braidings in Characteristic 2
arxiv:2611.11672.summary: We determine Nichols algebras associated with several families of pale braidings over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. For the rank-$4$ families under consideration, we obtain presentations by generators and relations, explicit monomial bases and dimension formulas. We also study families of arbitrary rank consisting of a two-dimensional pale block and several points, including cases with both vanishing and nonvanishing interaction parameters.
arxiv:2611.11672.authors: Dirceu Bagio, Laura Natalia Orozco Garc\'ia

arxiv:2611.11677.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
arxiv:2611.11677.summary: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.
arxiv:2611.11677.authors: Chris Bowman, Damian de la Fuente, Nicolas Libedinsky, David Plaza

arxiv:2611.11685.title: Rational knots, quivers, and tails of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials
arxiv:2611.11685.summary: We use the knots-quivers correspondence to prove that the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial of a rational knot has a tail and give an explicit formula for calculating the tail in terms of the quiver.
arxiv:2611.11685.authors: Elijah Berry, Rongjiang Guo, Jonathan A. Higgins, Eduardo Perez, Henry Zaslow

arxiv:2611.11699.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
arxiv:2611.11699.summary: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum…

arxiv:2611.11708.title: Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms
arxiv:2611.11708.summary: Let $\Phi:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $\Theta^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $\Phi$. We prove that $\Theta^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two.

arxiv:2611.11709.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
arxiv:2611.11709.summary: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot.
arxiv:2611.11709.authors: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Mark Leone, Roberto Sabella, Hugo Buurmeijer, Luis Pabon, John Irvin Alora, Marco Pavone, George Haller

arxiv:2611.11713.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
arxiv:2611.11713.summary: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection.

arxiv:2611.11718.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
arxiv:2611.11718.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment.
arxiv:2611.11718.authors: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Hehui Zheng, Robert K. Katzschmann, George Haller

arxiv:2611.11758.title: Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps
arxiv:2611.11758.summary: Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$.

arxiv:2611.11778.title: Homomesy of tropical $T$-systems for pairs of simply laced Dynkin diagrams
arxiv:2611.11778.summary: For a pair of simply laced Dynking diagrams $X$ and $X'$, we prove Chin's homomesy conjecture on the number of red and blue mutations in a period of the tropical Zamolodchikov $T$-system associated to $(X, X')$ using Nakanishi's dilogarithm identity.

arxiv:2611.11805.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
arxiv:2611.11805.summary: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response.
arxiv:2611.11805.authors: Lianghao Cao, George Stepaniants, Andrew M. Stuart

arxiv:2611.11813.title: The minimum forcing number of graphs and involutory weighted adjacency matrices
arxiv:2611.11813.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with a perfect matching. The minimum forcing number $f(G)$ of $G$ is the smallest size of a matching in $G$ that is contained in exactly one perfect matching. For the $d$-hypercube $Q_d$ ($d\geq 2$) Diwan (2019) determined $f(Q_d)=2^{d-2}$ by using a linear algebraic method, and Mohammadian (2022) generalized this method and showed that $f(G\square K_2)=n/2$ when a bipartite graph $G$ admits order $n$ and an involutory weighted adjacency matrix over a field $\mathbb F$, where $\square$ denotes the Cartesian product.

arxiv:2611.11828.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
arxiv:2611.11828.summary: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings.

arxiv:2611.11829.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
arxiv:2611.11829.summary: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups.

arxiv:2611.11844.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
arxiv:2611.11844.summary: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

arxiv:2611.11870.title: A Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem for marked graphs
arxiv:2611.11870.summary: The classical Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem characterizes graphs with least eigenvalue at least $-2$ in terms of generalized line graphs, exceptional graphs, and root systems. In this paper, we establish a marked graph extension of this theorem. For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and a binary vector $\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^n$, we completely characterize all marked graphs $\mathbf{G}=(G,\mathbf{b})$ such that $\lambda_{\min}(A(G)+\mathbf{b}\mathbf{b}^\top-J_n)\ge -2$, where $J_n$ denotes the all-ones matrix of order $n$.
arxiv:2611.11870.authors: Chaohui Chen, Muhuo Liu, Haiying Shan, Zoran Stani\'c

arxiv:2611.11930.title: Infinitude of integral Hitchin representations of Coxeter polygons
arxiv:2611.11930.summary: We prove that there are infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a Coxeter $n$-gon($n \geq 9$) group whose boundary parameters are fixed. We construct infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a specific Coxeter $6$-gon or $8$-gon corresponding to positive integral points of a generalized Markoff equation.

arxiv:2611.11933.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
arxiv:2611.11933.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most na\"{\i}ve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups.

arxiv:2611.11945.title: Rigidity and existence of profiled expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials
arxiv:2611.11945.summary: We study expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials of degree $-p$, where $p>0$. We establish asymptotic rigidity for arbitrary solutions with admissible profiles. For general admissible profiles and $0<p<2$, we obtain convergent power-log expansions whose exponents are governed by the leading profiles.

arxiv:2611.11970.title: Five-Entropic Matroids Are Quinary
arxiv:2611.11970.summary: A finite matroid is representable over a field if its elements can be assigned vectors over that field such that the rank of every subset equals the dimension of the span of its vectors.
