For an integer q >= 2, a matroid is q-entropic if there exists a random vector indexed by its ground set, with each coordinate taking values in a common q-element alphabet, such that the entropy of every marginal subvector equals the rank of the corresponding subset multiplied by log q. It remains open to determine for which values of q every q-entropic matroid is representable over a field.

arxiv:2611.11982.title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper \'etale groupoids
arxiv:2611.11982.summary: For suitable proper \'etale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences.
arxiv:2611.11982.authors: Yu Qiao, Bing Kwan So, Hang Wang

arxiv:2611.12008.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
arxiv:2611.12008.summary: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$.
arxiv:2611.12008.authors: Tran Nam Trung, Hoang Le Truong

arxiv:2611.12009.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
arxiv:2611.12009.summary: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up.

arxiv:2611.12015.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
arxiv:2611.12015.summary: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional.

arxiv:2611.12022.title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
arxiv:2611.12022.summary: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time.

arxiv:2611.12029.title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
arxiv:2611.12029.summary: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature.

arxiv:2611.12030.title: Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs
arxiv:2611.12030.summary: For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chv\'atal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian.

arxiv:2611.12043.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
arxiv:2611.12043.summary: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations.

arxiv:2611.12055.title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
arxiv:2611.12055.summary: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$.

arxiv:2611.12065.title: Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
arxiv:2611.12065.summary: A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $\eta=\mathrm{f}^2/F$.
arxiv:2611.12065.authors: Lakshitha Fernando, Eranda Dhananjaya, Rajitha Ranasinghe, Dinusha Priyadarshani

arxiv:2611.12101.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
arxiv:2611.12101.summary: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities.

arxiv:2611.12104.title: Permutons
arxiv:2611.12104.summary: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations.
arxiv:2611.12104.authors: Jacopo Borga, Valentin F\'eray, Peter Winkler

arxiv:2611.12108.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
arxiv:2611.12108.summary: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields.
arxiv:2611.12108.authors: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Benedetto Piccoli, Emmanuel Tr\'elat

arxiv:2611.12153.title: The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields
arxiv:2611.12153.summary: Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

arxiv:2611.12156.title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
arxiv:2611.12156.summary: Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive.
arxiv:2611.12156.authors: Julian Brandon, Bruno Loureiro, N Alex Cayco-Gajic, Arthur Pellegrino

arxiv:2611.12172.title: A Rooted Structure Theorem for $5$-Connected Graphs and $K_6^-$-Minors
arxiv:2611.12172.summary: Jorgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$-minor is apex. For a $6$-connected graph containing a $K_4$ on vertices $a_1,\dots,a_4$, being apex is equivalent to $G-a_i$ having a planar embedding with the other three roots on a common face for some $i$, so that for such graphs the conjecture becomes a rooted planarity statement. Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas showed that the failure of the corresponding three-rooted planarity is witnessed by a legless tripod.

arxiv:2611.12174.title: Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket
arxiv:2611.12174.summary: This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework.

arxiv:2611.12176.title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
arxiv:2611.12176.summary: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions.

arxiv:2611.12191.title: The multiplicity bound for near-group fusion categories of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$
arxiv:2611.12191.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$. We show $k\in\{0,3,4\}$, which then gives a complete characterization of near-group fusion categories determined by $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$.

arxiv:2611.12199.title: Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
arxiv:2611.12199.summary: A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family. In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem.
arxiv:2611.12199.authors: Yuejian Peng, Zilong Yan, Cheng Zhao

arxiv:2611.12201.title: Generalizations of Igusa surfaces
arxiv:2611.12201.summary: We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_p$, respectively.
arxiv:2611.12201.authors: Pascal Fong, Matilde Maccan, Ludvig Modin

arxiv:2611.12214.title: A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
arxiv:2611.12214.summary: The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained.
arxiv:2611.12214.authors: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn

arxiv:2611.12215.title: Globally Simple Heffter Arrays $H(n;k)$ with $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$
arxiv:2611.12215.summary: Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column.

arxiv:2611.12239.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
arxiv:2611.12239.summary: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set.
arxiv:2611.12239.authors: Jaros{\l}aw Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz, Krzysztof Przes{\l}awski

arxiv:2611.12245.title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
arxiv:2611.12245.summary: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one.
arxiv:2611.12245.authors: Sean Dewar, Anthony Nixon, Ben Smith

arxiv:2611.12257.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
arxiv:2611.12257.summary: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $\gamma\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $\gamma$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist…
arxiv:2611.12257.authors: Stavros Garoufalidis, Danylo Radchenko, Campbell Wheeler

arxiv:2611.12263.title: Rates in the weak invariance principle for slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.12263.summary: We obtain rates of convergence in the weak invariance principle for certain classes of slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems. In particular, for systems satisfying a Functional Correlation Bound with rate $n^{-\gamma} \ (\gamma>1)$, we establish an explicit bound in the Wasserstein-$r$ metric for $1\le r<\gamma+1$ whenever the variance grows at a sufficiently fast polynomial rate. The proof is based on Bernstein's ``big block--small block" method.

arxiv:2611.12276.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
arxiv:2611.12276.summary: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

arxiv:2611.12289.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
arxiv:2611.12289.summary: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula.
arxiv:2611.12289.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu, Huaiqing Zuo

arxiv:2611.12302.title: Upper bounds on all-terminal reliability polynomials in terms of cycle basis lengths
arxiv:2611.12302.summary: Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a connected multigraph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The all-terminal reliability polynomial of $G$ can be written as $R_G(q)=(1-q)^{n-1}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{d}H_iq^i$ where $d=m-n+1$ is the cycle rank, each edge fails independently with probability $q\in[0,1]$, and $H_0,\ldots,H_d$ are the associated coefficients. A cycle basis, which consists of cycles that form a basis of the cycle space of a graph, is an important tool for characterizing its cycle structure.
arxiv:2611.12302.authors: Tingzeng Wu, Xueqing Li, Jianxuan Luo, Hong-Jian Lai

arxiv:2611.12323.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
arxiv:2611.12323.summary: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions.

arxiv:2611.12327.title: Singular bifurcations in implicit discrete dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.12327.summary: A periodic orbit of an implicit discrete system can persist when the implicit function theorem no longer guarantees a smooth successor. We develop a joint Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction of the periodic equations and the determinants marking singular transitions. In unrestricted smooth one-parameter families, the generic event is a single evolution fold on a continued orbit.

arxiv:2611.12329.title: Piercing a Chessboard with Restricted Slopes
arxiv:2611.12329.summary: Is it true that for $n\geq 3$, $n-1$ lines are needed to pierce every cell of an $n\times n$ board? This problem was independently rediscovered several times: Alkauskas (1998), Harel-Ackerman-Pinchasi (2012, without claiming the $n-1$ bound), B\'ar\'any-Frankl (2021). However, apparently the first to pose it was T.

arxiv:2611.12330.title: Cut Conditions, Integrality, and Obstructions for Directed Multiflows
arxiv:2611.12330.summary: In contrast to the max-flow/min-cut theorem for single-commodity flows, the cut condition is necessary but not sufficient for the existence of directed multiflows, even with only two commodities. Poremba and Shepherd (IPCO 2023) conjecture that the cut condition is sufficient for all capacities and demands on a directed two-commodity topology if and only if it contains neither of two specific topologies as a relevant minor. We prove this conjecture.
arxiv:2611.12330.authors: Srinwanti Debgupta, Martin Skutella, Philipp Warode

arxiv:2611.12341.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
arxiv:2611.12341.summary: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.
arxiv:2611.12341.authors: Dae-Won Lee, Masaru Nagaoka, Masatomo Sawahara

arxiv:2611.12349.title: Sufficient conditions for spanning trees with bounded total excess in tough graphs
arxiv:2611.12349.summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph and $T$ a spanning tree of $G$. The toughness of $G$ is defined by $t(G)=\min\Big\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}:S\subseteq V(G), c(G-S)\geq2\Big\}$ for $G\neq K_n$. A graph $G$ is said to be $t$-tough if $t(G)\geq t$.
arxiv:2611.12349.authors: Sizhong Zhou, Chunjie Sun, Zhiren Sun

arxiv:2611.12355.title: Edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--\v{S}ir\'{a}\v{n} graphs $H_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 3$
arxiv:2611.12355.summary: Motivated by Hamilton cycle problems and applications to collective communication, we study edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--\v{S}ir\'{a}\v{n} (MMS) graphs. The MMS graph $H_q$ (indexed by a prime power $q$) is a highly symmetric graph arising from finite fields. For every prime power $q\geq 3$, we prove that the MMS graph $H_q$ contains $\big\lceil\frac{q-1}{2}\big\rceil$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

arxiv:2611.12358.title: Induced packing treewidth III. Branch decompositions
arxiv:2611.12358.summary: The notion of induced packing treewidth aims to unify classes defined by forbidden induced subgraphs or induced minors with classes defined by the existence of certain structured tree decompositions. In this paper, we introduce induced packing branchwidth, a branch-decomposition analogue of induced packing treewidth. For a graph $H$, the induced $H$-packing branchwidth of a graph $G$, denoted by $\branchpi_H(G)$, is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of $G$, of the largest number of pairwise anticomplete induced copies of $H$ that cross one displayed cut.

arxiv:2611.12360.title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
arxiv:2611.12360.summary:
Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{6889})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{22})$ for every $\alpha>0$.
arxiv:2611.12360.authors: Hei Chun Leung, Chi Hoi Yip

arxiv:2611.12366.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
arxiv:2611.12366.summary: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth.
arxiv:2611.12366.authors: Qiong Tao, Joonas Lahtinen, Sampsa Pursiainen

arxiv:2611.12380.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
arxiv:2611.12380.summary: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup.

arxiv:2611.12395.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
arxiv:2611.12395.summary: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.
arxiv:2611.12395.authors: Wen Huang, Song Shao, Hui Xu, Xiangdong Ye

arxiv:2611.12402.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
arxiv:2611.12402.summary: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation.

arxiv:2611.12413.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
arxiv:2611.12413.summary: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants.
arxiv:2611.12413.authors: Vladimiro Benedetti (UniCA,LJAD), Daniele Faenzi (UBE,IMB), Simone Marchesi (UB)

arxiv:2611.12417.title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
arxiv:2611.12417.summary: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight.
arxiv:2611.12417.authors: Chongying Dong, Kaiwen Sun, Haowu Wang

arxiv:2611.12444.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
arxiv:2611.12444.summary: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$.

arxiv:2611.12450.title: $\lambda_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
arxiv:2611.12450.summary: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $\lambda_g\psi^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.
arxiv:2611.12450.authors: Renzo Cavalieri, David Klompenhouwer, Paolo Rossi

arxiv:2611.12451.title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
arxiv:2611.12451.summary: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $\Theta_{e_\ell}\Theta_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson.
arxiv:2611.12451.authors: Haojun Bai, Feng Gu, Zhuowei Lin, Dun Qiu, Minhao Zhang

arxiv:2611.12453.title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
arxiv:2611.12453.summary: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $\sigma(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $\sigma(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four.

arxiv:2611.12473.title: The full length of short pants
arxiv:2611.12473.summary: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

arxiv:2611.12490.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
arxiv:2611.12490.summary: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed.

arxiv:2611.12519.title: Chv\'atal's Toughness Conjecture for Dense Almost Regular Graphs
arxiv:2611.12519.summary: Chv\'atal's toughness conjecture asserts that there is a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. Most partial results on this conjecture concern graphs with a restricted structure, such as chordal graphs and $H$-free graphs for small linear forests $H$. We confirm the conjecture with $t_0=4$ for dense almost regular graphs, without any structural assumption: for every $\alpha>0$, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that every $4$-tough graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge\alpha n$ and $\Delta(G)-\delta(G)\le\varepsilon n$ is Hamiltonian.

arxiv:2611.12522.title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
arxiv:2611.12522.summary: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.

arxiv:2611.12525.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
arxiv:2611.12525.summary: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold.

arxiv:2611.12582.title: Exact codegree Tur\'an densities of even zycles
arxiv:2611.12582.summary: We determine the exact codegree Tur\'an density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 8$ with $3\nmid\ell$,showing that $\gamma(Z_\ell)=1/3$. More generally, we prove that $\gamma(Z_\ell)\le 1/3$ for all even $\ell\ge 8$. Our results partially answer a question of Piga and Sch\"ulke [Bull.

arxiv:2611.12590.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
arxiv:2611.12590.summary: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

arxiv:2611.12601.title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
arxiv:2611.12601.summary: We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs.

arxiv:2611.12606.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
arxiv:2611.12606.summary: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

arxiv:2611.12607.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
arxiv:2611.12607.summary: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $\mu$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $\tau$ and $\mu$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2\tau\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_H\mu-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2\tau$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions.

arxiv:2611.12608.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
arxiv:2611.12608.summary: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type…

arxiv:2611.12613.title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
arxiv:2611.12613.summary: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables…

arxiv:2611.12679.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
arxiv:2611.12679.summary: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real…

arxiv:2611.12697.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
arxiv:2611.12697.summary: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$.

arxiv:2611.12707.title: On Symmetric Chain Decompositions for Bruhat--Chevalley Posets
arxiv:2611.12707.summary: We consider Stanley's problem on describing symmetric chain decompositions for the Bruhat--Chevalley posets of partial flag varieties and, more generally, Schubert varieties. These posets describe the containment relations of cell closures in the partial flag variety $G/P$ of a connected complex reductive algebraic group $G$. A famous instance of this problem asks whether the poset of partitions that fit inside a rectangle ordered by containment admits a symmetric chain decomposition (SCD), corresponding to the case of Grassmannian Schubert varieties in type $A$.
arxiv:2611.12707.authors: Aram Bingham, N. Fernando D\'iaz Morera, \"Ozlem U\u{g}urlu

arxiv:2611.12717.title: Fourteenth-canonical birationality of threefolds with positive geometric genus
arxiv:2611.12717.summary: We prove that the pluricanonical map of a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus is birational in every degree at least fourteen. The bound is sharp.

arxiv:2611.12719.title: Perfect loops of proper schemes
arxiv:2611.12719.summary: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$.

arxiv:2611.12722.title: Hidden frequencies in topological dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.12722.summary: We show for certain skew products built over any infinite minimal nilsystem, the frequencies present in the nilsystem are not always enough to govern recurrence for the whole system. This strengthens and generalizes a theorem of Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, and Richter.

arxiv:2611.12723.title: Classification of quasi-lisse simple affine vertex algebras
arxiv:2611.12723.summary: We classify all noncritical levels $k$ for which the simple affine vertex algebra $L_k(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, for every finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. We prove that Fiebig's equivalence between the corresponding noncritical blocks of category $\mathcal{O}$ identifies the relevant parabolic Wakimoto modules and the homomorphisms from the corresponding universal affine vertex algebras. Combining this compatibility with a characterization of semisimple points in associated varieties, we establish that for coprime positive integers $p,q$, $L_{-h^\vee+p/q}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse if and only if $L_{-h^\vee+p/\gcd(q,r)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse,…
arxiv:2611.12723.authors: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

arxiv:2611.12726.title: Residual-Based Spectral Submanifold Reduction of Constrained Multibody Systems on Matrix Lie Groups
arxiv:2611.12726.summary: The parameterization method yields efficient and accurate reduced-order models for nonlinear dynamical systems, but existing procedures that compute them assume polynomial vector fields on vector spaces. Constrained multibody systems instead obey differential-algebraic equations on matrix Lie groups such as $\mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$. Minimal parameterizations of these groups lead to non-polynomial equations that must be approximated or recast before reduction, and current implementations require the nonlinearities as explicit multilinear maps, which are cumbersome to construct for assembled multibody systems.
arxiv:2611.12726.authors: Stefan Holzinger, Tiago Martins, Daniel Rixen

arxiv:2611.12743.title: Periodic vortex dipoles near closed geodesics on Riemannian surfaces
arxiv:2611.12743.summary: We study the motion of a pair $(p_1,p_2)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$ of point vortices with equal magnitude and opposite signs on a closed oriented Riemannian surface $(\Sigma,g)$. Given a closed geodesic that satisfies a non-degeneracy condition we construct a one-parameter family of periodic solutions $(p_1^\varepsilon,p_2^\varepsilon)$, $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, of the Hamiltonian dynamical system for point vortex pairs whose trajectories converge towards the geodesic curve. The two vortices lie on opposite sides of the geodesic, are separated of order $\varepsilon$ and have period $2\pi\varepsilon$.

arxiv:2611.12744.title: Semiampleness of Hodge line bundles and b-semiampleness of the moduli part
arxiv:2611.12744.summary: We give proofs of Hodge semiampleness and b-semiampleness without using o-minimality. We establish a geometric semiampleness criterion for line bundles on proper algebraic spaces. Let $(X,D)$ be a log smooth pair with $X$ a proper algebraic space.
arxiv:2611.12744.authors: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

arxiv:2611.12751.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
arxiv:2611.12751.summary: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all…

arxiv:2611.12780.title: The dimension of multi-index assignment polytopes and Latin-square transversal polytopes, via association schemes
arxiv:2611.12780.summary: We determine the dimensions, and the implicit equations, of several polytopes from integer programming whose vertices are the largest stable sets of highly symmetric graphs. Our main tools are two new dimension formulae within Lee's spectral method, which reads the dimension off of an association scheme: for amorphic schemes it becomes a threshold formula, and for point sets in $GF(q)^d$ invariant under the maps $z\mapsto az+b$ it is $q-1$ times the number of hyperplane directions along which some point is not equidistributed. A single integer point, a witness, then certifies a whole eigenspace.

arxiv:2611.12781.title: Average distance and maximum induced linear forest
arxiv:2611.12781.summary: Let G be a connected graph of order n, let {\mu}(G) denote its average distance, and let L(G) denote the maximum order of an induced linear forest of G, that is, of an induced subgraph whose components are chains. Hansen, Hertz, Kilani, Marcotte and Schindl conjectured that {\mu}(G) {\le} L(G)/2, which can be written as 4W(G) {\le} L(G)n(n-1), where W(G) is the Wiener index of G. This inequality strengthens their bound {\mu}(G) {\le} F(G)/2, where F(G) is the maximum order of an induced forest, as well as Chung's classical bound {\mu}(G) {\le} {\alpha}(G).

arxiv:2611.12786.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
arxiv:2611.12786.summary: We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.
arxiv:2611.12786.authors: Pinxian Bie, Peien Du, Zhengjie Yu

arxiv:2611.12789.title: The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps
arxiv:2611.12789.summary: Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown.

arxiv:2611.12810.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
arxiv:2611.12810.summary: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications.

arxiv:2611.12821.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
arxiv:2611.12821.summary: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_\lambda$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_\lambda = H_0 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $\kappa \in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_\lambda^2 = 1/s_\kappa^2 + \lambda$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $\lambda$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and…

arxiv:2611.12828.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
arxiv:2611.12828.summary: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem.

arxiv:2611.12829.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
arxiv:2611.12829.summary: We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846).
arxiv:2611.12829.authors: Natasha Blitvi\'c, Mohammed Slim Kammoun, Einar Steingr\'imsson

arxiv:2611.12836.title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
arxiv:2611.12836.summary: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed.
arxiv:2611.12836.authors: Justin Asher, Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

arxiv:2611.12847.title: Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon
arxiv:2611.12847.summary: For a simple graph $\Gamma$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(\Gamma,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $\Gamma$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined…
arxiv:2611.12847.authors: Emilio J. Gonz\'alez, Jes\'us Gonz\'alez, Mary Carmen P\'erez-Morales

arxiv:2611.12863.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
arxiv:2611.12863.summary: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende.

arxiv:2611.12866.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
arxiv:2611.12866.summary: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a…

arxiv:2611.12874.title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
arxiv:2611.12874.summary: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,\delta_B,\epsilon_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $\delta_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $\epsilon_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $\iota_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$.

arxiv:2611.12920.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
arxiv:2611.12920.summary: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings.
arxiv:2611.12920.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci, Mario Primicerio

arxiv:2611.12929.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
arxiv:2611.12929.summary: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $\Delta(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior.
arxiv:2611.12929.authors: Dora Sele\v{s}i, Danijela Rajter-\'Ciri\'c, N\'ora Juh\'asz, Gergely R\"ost

arxiv:2611.12931.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
arxiv:2611.12931.summary: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow.

arxiv:2611.12951.title: On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs
arxiv:2611.12951.summary: Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{\delta+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}{\delta}+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $\delta+1$ versus $\delta+2$ gap (resp.\ the $\delta$ versus $\delta+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{\delta+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{\delta+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $\delta \geq 2$.

arxiv:2611.12972.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
arxiv:2611.12972.summary: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work.

arxiv:2611.12996.title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
arxiv:2611.12996.summary: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect.
arxiv:2611.12996.authors: Yi Zheng, Jiansong Deng, Xinyu Wu

arxiv:2611.13031.title: Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays
arxiv:2611.13031.summary: We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials.

arxiv:2611.13044.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
arxiv:2611.13044.summary: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

arxiv:2611.13050.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
arxiv:2611.13050.summary: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix.

arxiv:2611.13065.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
arxiv:2611.13065.summary: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $\Delta$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $\Delta$. For every fixed $\Delta$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $\Delta$-modular.
arxiv:2611.13065.authors: Samuel Fiorini, J. Pascal Gollin, Tony Huynh, Simon Keil, O-joung Kwon, Sang-il Oum, Roohani Sharma, Stefan Weltge

arxiv:2611.13066.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice
arxiv:2611.13066.summary: Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus conjectured that for each non-equilateral triangle $\operatorname{T}$, every 2-coloring of the plane contains a congruent copy of $\operatorname{T}$ with monochromatic vertex set. We confirm this conjecture for triangles with a ratio $\sqrt{7/3}$ between two side lengths. We further prove that every coloring of the plane, regardless of the number of colors used, contains congruent copies of 36 specific triangles with monochromatic or rainbow vertex sets, partially answering a question of Geh\'er, Sagdeev, and T\'oth.

arxiv:2611.13068.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
arxiv:2611.13068.summary: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schr\"odinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.
arxiv:2611.13068.authors: Lingrui Ge, Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Jiangong You

arxiv:2611.13108.title: Waldschmidt constants and invariant geometry for exceptional rank-four complex reflection groups
arxiv:2611.13108.summary: We compute the Waldschmidt constants of the point configurations dual to the reflection arrangements of the exceptional complex reflection groups $G_{29}$, $G_{31}$ and $G_{32}$. They equal $3$ for the forty points of $G_{29}$, $36/11$ for the sixty-point Klein configuration, and $10/3$ for the forty-point Penrose configuration. Together with the known cases $W(F_4)$ and $W(H_4)$, this completes the computation for all exceptional irreducible complex reflection groups of rank four.
arxiv:2611.13108.authors: Krishna Hanumanthu, Jack Huizenga, Jake Kettinger, Lukasz Merta, Tomasz Szemberg, Justyna Szpond

arxiv:2611.13126.title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
arxiv:2611.13126.summary: We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one.

arxiv:2611.13129.title: The uncertainty operator, the Weil ground state and the zeros of zeta: a numerical study and conditional positivity of the Weil quadratic form
arxiv:2611.13129.summary: Applying the Dirichlet principle to the Weil quadratic form $QW_\lambda$ on $L^2([\lambda^{-1},\lambda],d^*u)$--using only the primes $p\le\lambda^2$ of the Euler product--yields canonical finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices whose ground state has a Mellin transform with zeros proved real in full generality when the lowest eigenvalue is simple and even. While $\lambda^2=13$ gave $50$ zeros of $\zeta$, $\lambda^2=250$ ($\lambda\sim16$) gives the first $1000$ zeros with $>500$ correct decimals (the first with $1341$). We explain this via a correspondence between $QW_\lambda$ and Slepian's time-frequency uncertainty operator $U_\lambda=2-P_\lambda-\widehat P_\lambda$, diagonalized by prolate…
arxiv:2611.13129.authors: Ronnie Andrews, Alain Connes, Antonio La Gatta

arxiv:2611.13155.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
arxiv:2611.13155.summary: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces).

arxiv:2611.13171.title: Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval
arxiv:2611.13171.summary: We study representations of the Baumslag-Solitar group $BS(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid ab^ma^{-1}=b^n\rangle$ inside the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the interval $[0,1]$. We prove that for integers $n,m\in \mathbb Z\setminus\{-1,0,1\}$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds into $\mathrm{Diff}_+^1([0,1])$ if and only if $|n|=|m|$. Furthermore, we show that for any $\alpha\in (0,1)$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds inside $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+\alpha}([0,1])$ if and only if $1=|m|=|n|$ or when $1=m\leq n$.

arxiv:2611.13193.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections
arxiv:2611.13193.summary: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem.

arxiv:2611.13208.title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
arxiv:2611.13208.summary: Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial.

arxiv:2611.13226.title: Unilluminable rooms: minimal examples, classifications and exceptions
arxiv:2611.13226.summary: A room with mirrored walls can contain two points that are mutually invisible: no light ray from one reaches the other. Tokarsky built the first polygonal examples by tiling a room with reflected copies of a triangle and making every tile vertex of certain kinds a corner of the room. We study the smallest rooms of this kind, which we call lattice rooms.
arxiv:2611.13226.authors: J. C. F. de Winter, George W. Tokarsky

arxiv:2611.13239.title: A decomposition theorem for minimal W-algebras of type A
arxiv:2611.13239.summary: To any simple Lie algebra, one can associate a minimal affine W-algebra. It is a vertex algebra which is obtained from the universal affine vertex algebra by a chiral Hamiltonian reduction procedure. This reduction is determined by data coming from the minimal nilpotent orbit.

arxiv:2611.13244.title: Stabilization of the zero forcing number of generalized Petersen graphs
arxiv:2611.13244.summary: We show that the zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph $P(n,k)$ is $2k+2$ whenever $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We prove this by showing that the zero forcing number of the infinite generalized Petersen graph $P(\infty,k)$ is $2k+2$ and bounding the width of the closure of every set of at most $2k+1$ vertices. This bound gives a threshold on $n$ beyond which the projection of such a closure onto $P(n,k)$ does not wrap around.
arxiv:2611.13244.authors: Young H. Kim, Youngsoo Kim, Byunghoon Lee

arxiv:2611.13248.title: Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory
arxiv:2611.13248.summary: In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincar\'e $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property. Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory.
arxiv:2611.13248.authors: Baptiste Calm\`es, Emanuele Dotto, Yonatan Harpaz, Fabian Hebestreit, Markus Land, Kristian Moi, Denis Nardin, Thomas Nikolaus, Wolfgang Steimle

arxiv:2611.13265.title: Effect of car-centric social norms on traffic congestion in a compartmental model of transit mode utilization
arxiv:2611.13265.summary: Vehicle traffic congestion is a persistent feature of urban transportation systems around the world.Importantly, congestion is in part a consequence of human decision-making: car traffic is reduced when people choose modes of transportation such as metro trains, buses, or trams, over cars, and it is amplified when there is a persistent social bias towards driving. The underlying feedback loop in which traffic levels influence transportation mode choices, which in turn affect traffic levels themselves, is poorly understood and we study its consequences in the presented work using a compartmental modeling approach. We first consider a simplified model of only car traffic and show that it…

arxiv:2611.13267.title: The Cayley-Bedregal reduction for Milnor and Hirzebruch-Milnor classes
arxiv:2611.13267.summary: The Cayley--Bedregal reduction replaces a complete intersection $\{f_1=\dots=f_r=0\}$ by the hypersurface $\sum_i\varphi_if_i=0$ in the projectivized dual bundle. For an isolated complete intersection singularity of corank $c$, we express the Milnor class of this hypersurface on its singular fibre $\mathbb P^{c-1}$ in terms of the Milnor numbers of generic systems obtained by taking linear combinations of the defining equations. Its degree is the original Milnor number, and the higher components recover the Milnor numbers of the systems with fewer equations.
arxiv:2611.13267.authors: R. Callejas-Bedregal, F. Caraballo, M. F. Z. Morgado, J. Seade

arxiv:2611.13273.title: Properties of the Dichromatic Polynomial
arxiv:2611.13273.summary: The chromatic polynomial is a well-studied function of graphs whose coefficients, factorization, and other properties are well-known to encode structural information about the underlying graph. An analogous notion of graph colouring exists for directed graphs which is also well-studied, but little is yet known about the corresponding dichromatic polynomial. We investigate properties of the dichromatic polynomial, including its coefficient interpretations, root-dense regions, and asymptotic growth.
arxiv:2611.13273.authors: Lila Crew, Benjamin Keller, Katharina Kuehr, Shao Yuan Lin, Megan Ixchel Monroy Rodr\'iguez, Tabitha Williams

arxiv:2611.13274.title: On the Chromatic Number of Cayley Tables of Dihedral Groups
arxiv:2611.13274.summary: A coloring of a Latin square $L$ is an assignment of $k$ colors to its cells such that no two cells sharing a row, a column, or a symbol receive the same color. The smallest $k$ for which such a coloring exists is called the \emph{chromatic number} of $L$, denoted by $\chi(L)$. The Cayley table of a finite group $G$ of order $n$ is a Latin square, which we denote by $L_G$.

arxiv:2611.13277.title: Pulsatile Endocrine Regulation with a Releasable Hormone Pool: Impulsive Feedback Model
arxiv:2611.13277.summary: An impulsive model of endocrine regulation equipped with frequency- and amplitude-modulated pulsatile feedback is extended to study the dynamical effects pertaining to limitations due to the releasable hormone pool. The model describes a three-hormone regulatory loop and is applicable to endocrine systems such as the reproductive, stress, and growth hormone axes. Conditions guaranteeing the existence and uniqueness of a periodic solution with a single feedback-triggered impulse per period (a 1-cycle) are derived, together with monotonicity properties of its characteristics.

arxiv:2611.13278.title: On the number of zeros of polyanalytic polynomials
arxiv:2611.13278.summary: We prove that a complex polynomial $f(z,\bar z)$ of degree $n$ in $z$ and degree $m<n$ in $\bar{z}$, with finitely many zeros, has at most $(4m+1)n-5m$ distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$. The proof uses an approach suggested by GPT-6.1 based on a topological result of Kronheimer and Mrowka (Thom's Conjecture). We provide examples showing that the bound is asymptotically sharp as $n\to\infty$ for each fixed $m$.
arxiv:2611.13278.authors: Erik Lundberg, Zvi Rosen, Teng Zhang

arxiv:2611.13281.title: Constant query LCCs over the reals
arxiv:2611.13281.summary: This note describes a new construction, found by ChatGPT Astra, of constant query Locally Correctable Codes (LCCs) over the real numbers. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries).

arxiv:2611.13284.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry
arxiv:2611.13284.summary: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.
arxiv:2611.13284.authors: Paul Balmer, Rhea Kommerell, Emmy Van Rooy

arxiv:2611.13302.title: Handlebody-links with Euler characteristic -2 up to six crossings
arxiv:2611.13302.summary: We enumerate all non-split handlebody-links with Euler characteristic $-2$ up to six crossings, up to ambient isotopy and mirror image.
arxiv:2611.13302.authors: Giovanni Bellettini, Giovanni Paolini, Maurizio Paolini, Yi-Sheng Wang

arxiv:2611.13305.title: Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful closed braid diagram
arxiv:2611.13305.summary: Every hyperbolic knot admits an arc-faithful closed braid diagram, answering Conjecture 29 of McPhail-Snyder. More precisely, any braid representing the knot can be reworded in the same braid group so that the complete holonomy has distinct incoming parabolic fixed points at every crossing. The construction replaces a pinched crossing by five non-pinched crossings when a suitable third strand is adjacent.

arxiv:2611.13318.title: From oscillations to symmetry breaking in a two-dimensional piecewise-smooth dynamical system
arxiv:2611.13318.summary: We propose a discrete-time dynamical model in which two players, each distributed over two positions, interact only at the positions of their maximal presence, with an intensity set by an external resource. The main idea is that the evolution of the maxima closes into a self-contained two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map that can be analysed exactly. We show that a single critical level of the resource separates two outcomes: below it, the players exchange leadership forever along a stable cycle; above it, the symmetry between them breaks, and an arbitrarily small initial advantage grows into a permanent winner--loser hierarchy.

arxiv:2611.13347.title: Computational Power of Clifford and Ising Quantum Computers
arxiv:2611.13347.summary: We extend the efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. We investigate several different definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation by varying the power of the circuit generator. In case the circuit generator can see the entire input, we give a detailed proof that efficient simulation of classical computation would imply the separation of complexity classes $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{PSPACE}$.

arxiv:2611.13349.title: On Poincar\'e-Type Inequalities for Flags of Distributions
arxiv:2611.13349.summary: In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. As an application, we prove Poincar\'e-type degree inequalities for flags on certain classes of manifolds.
arxiv:2611.13349.authors: Antonio M. Ferreira, Miguel Rodr\'iguez Pe\~na, Fernando Louren\c{c}o

arxiv:2611.13353.title: Coordinatizing coalition lattices
arxiv:2611.13353.summary: Let $P$ denote a finite poset in which no two incomparable elements have an upper bound. The coalition lattice Coal$(P)$ of $P$ consists of all subsets of $P$, ordered as follows: $X$ is less than or equal to $Y$ if and only if there exists an injective map from $X$ to $Y$ that sends each element to an element greater than or equal to itself. The main result coordinatizes Coal$(P)$ with integer vectors.

arxiv:2611.13372.title: Quantifying the impact of 3D diffusion and local versus global removal by surface deposition on indoor airborne transmission
arxiv:2611.13372.summary: The Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] combines architectural layout, people movement, and airborne transmission modelling to predict infection risk in indoor spaces. The modelling assumptions in VIRIS include: (i) uniform aerosol concentration over the building height, allowing airborne transmission to be modelled in a two-dimensional (2D) domain, and (ii) first-order global removal of aerosols to account for surface deposition. Both assumptions lead to underestimating the infectious aerosol concentration in the breathing zone.
arxiv:2611.13372.authors: Neha Bansal, Katerina Kaouri, Thomas E. Woolley

arxiv:2611.13376.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of semialgebraic cones
arxiv:2611.13376.summary: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined through a complementarity problem constrained by a closed convex cone. We show that every closed semialgebraic convex cone is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra, the sets of the cone-constrained eigenvalues, of symmetric matrices relative to the cone are uniformly finite with respect to the matrices. The uniform bound is explicit, and as an application, we derive a uniform bound for the cardinality of spectra of symmetric matrices relative to L\"{o}wner cones.

arxiv:2611.13377.title: Unimodal Singularities of Parametrized Space Curves
arxiv:2611.13377.summary: The aim of the article is to classify unimodal parametrized space curve singularities defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. We provide explicit normal forms of parametrizations up to $\mathcal A$-equivalence. The parametrizations are given by convergent power series over a real valued field, which includes parametrizations given by formal power series and by, for example, convergent power series over the complex numbers or the field of Puisieux series.
arxiv:2611.13377.authors: Gert-Martin Greuel, Khawar Mehmood, Gerhard Pfister

arxiv:2611.13380.title: Positive Codegree Density of Suspensions of Graphs
arxiv:2611.13380.summary: We determine the exact positive codegree density of suspensions of graphs $S^r(G)$ when $\chi(G)=t$ and $t-2$ is prime power. The value is $\gamma^+(S^{r}(G)) = \frac{(t-3)(t-2)^{r-1}}{(t-2)^r-1}$. The case of suspensions of $K_4$ gives the positive codegree density of daisies, answering a question of Balogh, Halfpap, Lidick\'y and Palmer.

arxiv:2611.13381.title: $5I(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample on stable log surfaces
