arxiv:2611.13381.summary: We prove that Bombieri's bound for canonical models of surfaces of general type extends to stable log surfaces, that is, $mI(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample for every $m\geq 5$ and every stable log surface $(X,\Delta)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with reduced boundary and global Cartier index $I$. On the way to this result we determine the cases where $|3I(K_X+\Delta)|$ has base points.

arxiv:2611.13385.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
arxiv:2611.13385.summary: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes.
arxiv:2611.13385.authors: Shin Hong, Jeongsoo Kim, Eunjeong Lee

arxiv:2611.13390.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
arxiv:2611.13390.summary: For any given uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, we show that every $\kappa$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_{\kappa}\star1$ (the $\kappa$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $\kappa$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $\kappa$.
arxiv:2611.13390.authors: Max Pitz, Lucas Real, Roman Schaut

arxiv:2611.13394.title: Edge-coloring spectra of odd-fold graph covers and counterexamples to a conjecture
arxiv:2611.13394.summary: For a loopless multigraph $G$ and an odd integer $\ell\ge3$, let $\Delta(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$, let $s_\ell(G)$ be the minimum chromatic index of a cyclic $\ell$-fold cover of $G$, and let \begin{align*} L_\ell(G):=\max\left\{ \Delta(G),\ \max_{\substack{S\subseteq V(G)\\ |S|\ge3\text{ odd}}} \left\lceil\frac{2\ell|E(G[S])|}{\ell|S|-1}\right\rceil \right\}. \end{align*} In this paper, we prove the sharp upper bound \begin{align*} s_\ell(G)\le\max\{\Delta(G)+1,L_\ell(G)\}. \end{align*} For every nonempty bridgeless cubic graph $H$, we construct two $3\ell$-regular graphs, one a multigraph and the other a simple graph.

arxiv:2611.13407.title: Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets
arxiv:2611.13407.summary: It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$.

arxiv:2611.13415.title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
arxiv:2611.13415.summary: A graph is vertex-transitive if, for any two vertices, there is an automorphism mapping one to the other. We prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph of order $p^n$, where $p$ is a prime and $p^n\geq 3$, has a hamiltonian cycle. Our main tool extends Witte's theorem [JCTB (1986)] on Cayley digraphs of $p$-groups.
arxiv:2611.13415.authors: Farzad Maghsoudi, Dragan Maru\v{s}i\v{c}, Bobby Miraftab

arxiv:2611.13416.title: Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems
arxiv:2611.13416.summary: We introduce two complementary frameworks for studying local periodicity and recurrence in dynamical systems. In the topological setting, we consider continuous maps with nonempty periodic-point sets, restricted to the closures of their periodic points. We define the periodic penetration time of an open set as the least period of a periodic point it contains.

arxiv:2611.13417.title: The Isomorphism Problem for Cayley Graphs on Monogenic Semigroups
arxiv:2611.13417.summary: In this paper, we investigate the structural properties of Cayley graphs of monogenic semigroups and present a complete characterization of their weakly connected components. Several essential properties of these components are rigorously proven. Building upon these structural results, we introduce the notion of labelled colour-permuting isomorphisms between Cayley graphs.
arxiv:2611.13417.authors: Lu Li, Yong Shao, Lingli Zeng

arxiv:2611.13420.title: Minimal dynamics with polynomial and intermediate complexity
arxiv:2611.13420.summary: We study how complicated the orbits of a minimal system can be when the topological entropy vanishes, by looking at the exact order of growth of the number of distinguishable orbit segments, and not only at its exponent. For a broad class of growth rates, including all polynomial ones, we construct minimal homeomorphisms of one-dimensional continua realizing them; in particular, two such systems may have the same polynomial entropy and yet incomparable growth. We also show that passing from a minimal subshift to the maps obtained by running its suspension flow for a fixed time only rescales time in the growth law, and we characterize exactly when this rescaling has no effect.

arxiv:2611.13422.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
arxiv:2611.13422.summary: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,\beta}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Koll\'ar's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric.

arxiv:2611.13424.title: Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category
arxiv:2611.13424.summary: We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.

arxiv:2611.13439.title: Claw-free minimal bricks
arxiv:2611.13439.summary: A graph $G$ is called a \emph{brick} if it is $3$-connected and $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$. A brick is \emph{minimal} if deleting any edge results in a graph that is no longer a brick. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if it contains no induced $K_{1,3}$.

arxiv:2611.13440.title: Genus zero simple knots
arxiv:2611.13440.summary: We classify the simple knots in lens spaces with planar rational Seifert surfaces. As a consequence, we classify the homology classes of all knots in lens spaces that admit planar rational Seifert surfaces.
arxiv:2611.13440.authors: Joshua Evan Greene, Shiyu Liang, John Luecke

arxiv:2611.13445.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
arxiv:2611.13445.summary: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical.

arxiv:2611.13446.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
arxiv:2611.13446.summary: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian.

arxiv:2611.13455.title: Divisibility graphs of semigroups as weighted poset blow-ups
arxiv:2611.13455.summary: We develop a structural theory of divisibility graphs of arbitrary semigroups. For a semigroup $S$, let $S/{\mathcal J}$ be the poset of Green's ${\mathcal J}$-classes ordered by inclusion of principal ideals,and equip each $\mathcal {J}$-class $J$ with the weight $|J|$. We prove that the divisibility graph ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is obtained from the comparability directed graph $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ by replacing each $\mathcal J$-class with a complete symmetric graph of order $|J|$ and by replacing each directed edge $J_u$ to $J_v$ in $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ with all directed edges from every element of $J_u$ to every element of $J_v$.
arxiv:2611.13455.authors: Xuang Yang, Yong Shao, Lingli Zeng

arxiv:2611.13458.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
arxiv:2611.13458.summary: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology.
arxiv:2611.13458.authors: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lafont, Zhenghao Rao, Hongbin Sun

arxiv:2611.13468.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
arxiv:2611.13468.summary: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values.

arxiv:2611.13479.title: Log-Concavity in Narayana Transforms and Stack-Sorting Fibers
arxiv:2611.13479.summary: Given a permutation $\pi$ of size $n$, let $D_\pi(x)$ denote the descent polynomial of the fiber of $\pi$ under West's stack-sorting map. We prove that $D_\pi(x)$ is ultra-log-concave of order $n-1$ and, therefore, log-concave. More generally, we prove that a multivariate refinement of $D_\pi(x)$ recording ascent tops and descent tops is the basis generating polynomial of a laminar matroid.

arxiv:2611.13495.title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems
arxiv:2611.13495.summary: We construct the largest $r$-flower-free system of $k$-uniform sets for $k=3, r=4$ where every element of the ground set $G$ is used at least once. The goal is to maximize $|G|$, also called the span. We define $\mathrm{sp}(k, r)$ to be the maximum $|G|$ for such a system.

arxiv:2611.13535.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
arxiv:2611.13535.summary: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$.
arxiv:2611.13535.authors: Teeradej Kittipassorn, Nattawut Phetmak, Kirati Sriamorn

arxiv:2611.13580.title: The minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in graphs with no proper $k$-coloring
arxiv:2611.13580.summary: Consider an integer $k\geq 3$. Toft and Tuza observed that every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has a cycle of length $0$ modulo $k$. Brewster, McGuinness, Moore, and Noel conjectured the following quantitative strengthening: every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has at least $\frac{(k+1)!}{2k}$ cycles whose lengths are divisible by $k$.

arxiv:2611.13585.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
arxiv:2611.13585.summary: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Seb\H{o} and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected.
arxiv:2611.13585.authors: Swati Gupta, Mehrdad Sohrabi, Levent Tun\c{c}el

arxiv:2611.13586.title: Maximal Triply Even Binary Codes from Elliptic Orthogonal Graphs
arxiv:2611.13586.summary: For a finite set $X$, a binary linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^X$ is called a triply even binary code if $\operatorname{wt}(c)\equiv 0\pmod{8}$ for every $c\in C$. Let $q$ be an odd prime power and $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 2$. Let $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ denote the binary code spanned by all pairwise sums of rows of the adjacency matrix of the elliptic orthogonal graph arising from a $(2n+2)$-dimensional elliptic quadratic space over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

arxiv:2611.13590.title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
arxiv:2611.13590.summary: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $\alpha\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Gr\"unwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $\alpha=1$.
arxiv:2611.13590.authors: Md Babul Hossain, Mohammad Shah Alam

arxiv:2611.13593.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
arxiv:2611.13593.summary: We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$.
arxiv:2611.13593.authors: Gergely Kiss, Caleb Marshall, M\'at\'e Matolcsi, G\'abor Somlai

arxiv:2611.13601.title: Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level
arxiv:2611.13601.summary: For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.

arxiv:2611.13608.title: Triangles without a common vertex
arxiv:2611.13608.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, $t(G)$ triangles, and adjacency spectral radius $\lambda(G)>\sqrt m$. Li, Feng and Peng (2025) conjectured that $t(G)\ge\sqrt m-O(1)$ if no vertex belongs to every triangle of $G$. We prove the stronger bound $t(G)\ge\lambda(G)-C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and give an explicit choice of $C$.

arxiv:2611.13619.title: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem for cycle lengths $3$ and $n$
arxiv:2611.13619.summary: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem asks for a factorization of the complete symmetric digraph $K_v^*$ into directed $2$-factors, each of which is isomorphic to one of two given directed $2$-factors. In its uniform version, one seeks a decomposition of $K_v^*$ into $r$ factors consisting of directed $m$-cycles and $s$ factors consisting of directed $n$-cycles, where $r+s=v-1$. Let $m=3$, and let $n \geq 5$ be odd and not divisible by $3$.
arxiv:2611.13619.authors: Ugur Odabasi, Dan Roberts, Richard M. Low

arxiv:2611.13639.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlev\'e II
arxiv:2611.13639.summary: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlev\'e II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion.
arxiv:2611.13639.authors: Sibasish Banerjee, Babak Haghighat, Jie Sun

arxiv:2611.13656.title: Uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with large maximum degree
arxiv:2611.13656.summary: A graph $G$ is \textit{uniquely $H$-saturated} if it contains no copy of $H$ as a subgraph, but adding any edge to $G$ creates exactly one copy of $H$ in the resultant graph. In this paper, we consider the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs and characterize the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta\geq n-5$. We prove that if $G$ is a uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graph with universal vertex $x$, then $G-x$ is either a star or a Moore graph of diameter 2.
arxiv:2611.13656.authors: Yuying Li, Weiyuan Zhang, Kexiang Xu

arxiv:2611.13660.title: Judicious $r$-partitions of $r$-uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.13660.summary: Bollob\'as and Thomason conjectured that every $r$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges admits an $r$-partition such that each class meets at least $rm/(2r-1)$ edges. In this paper, we establish a lower bound of $(11-\sqrt{13})m/18$ for every $r\ge 2$. This improves Haslegrave's bound $rm/(3r-4)$ for every $r\ge 8$.

arxiv:2611.13676.title: An automated approach to structure theorems for minimally repetitive rich words
arxiv:2611.13676.summary: Recent work on repetitions in rich words has led to the intensive study of the family of infinite rich words $\{{\mathbf u}_d:d\geq 2\}$, where ${\mathbf u}_d$ is the fixed point of the morphism $\varphi_d:\Sigma_d^*\rightarrow \Sigma_d^*$ defined by $\varphi_d(i)=\tt{0}(i+1)$ for $i\in\{\tt{0},\ldots,d-2\}$ and $\varphi_d(d-1)=\tt{0}(d-1)(d-1)$. For $d=2$ and $d=3$, it is known that the repetition threshold for infinite $d$-ary rich words is equal to the asymptotic critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$. Moreover, the structure of ${\mathbf u}_{2d-1}$ underlies the structure of all ``minimally repetitive'' $d$-ary rich words: there is a real number $t_d>E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ such…
arxiv:2611.13676.authors: Lubom\'ira Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Lucas Mol, Edita Pelantov\'a

arxiv:2611.13682.title: Unstable Entropy and Volume Growth for Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms
arxiv:2611.13682.summary: Let $f$ be a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism on a compact manifold $M$ admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting $TM=E^{cs}\oplus E^{u}$ where $E^{u}$ is uniformly expanding. We establish a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy (w.r.t. $E^{u}$): $$h^{u}_{\rm top}\left(f\right)\geq\limsup_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\int_{M}\left|\det \left(Df^{n}_{x}|_{E^{u}}\right)\right|\,dx.$$ Moreover, if there exists a measure of maximal unstable entropy whose Lyapunov exponents along $E^{cs}$ are all non-positive, then equality holds and the $\limsup$ is in fact a limit.

arxiv:2611.13693.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
arxiv:2611.13693.summary: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al.

arxiv:2611.13698.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
arxiv:2611.13698.summary: In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $\chi'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)\Delta(H)$ whenever $\Delta(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture.
arxiv:2611.13698.authors: Chengshuo Qiao, Zhijun Lu, Huimin Song

arxiv:2611.13702.title: Berry phase and Hannay angle as Taylor coefficients of the minimal action
arxiv:2611.13702.summary: For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom whose parameters are varied slowly around a closed loop, with slowness $\delta$, we study the minimal action $\beta_\delta$ of the resulting time-periodic system and its convex conjugate, Mather's $\alpha$-function $\alpha_\delta$, both normalized per unit time. The cycle map of such a system is an area-preserving map of the cylinder which in general is not integrable. We prove that $\beta_\delta(\rho)$ and $\alpha_\delta(c)$ have asymptotic expansions in $\delta$ to every finite order, locally uniformly in the rotational regime of the frozen systems, and we identify the coefficients geometrically.

arxiv:2611.13723.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
arxiv:2611.13723.summary: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$.

arxiv:2611.13728.title: Two Types of Cards in Kelly-Ulam Conjecture
arxiv:2611.13728.summary: We consider the case in Kelly-Ulam conjecture where there are only two types of cards in deck. It was possible to prove that graphs with this property are uniquely reconstructed by their card deck.

arxiv:2611.13747.title: Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent
arxiv:2611.13747.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $F$ a field of characteristic different from $p$. For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le m\le n$, we complete the determination of the essential $p$-dimension of the class of central simple algebras of degree $p^n$ and exponent dividing $p^m$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{ed}_p(\operatorname{PGL}(p^n))=p^{2n-2}+1$, extending a result of Merkurjev for $n=2$.

arxiv:2611.13749.title: Beyond Frankl's conjecture: Maximum sum of sizes of cross-intersecting families with restricted conditions
arxiv:2611.13749.summary: Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be two families of subsets of $[n]$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are \emph{cross-intersecting} if $F \cap G \neq \emptyset$ for all $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and $G \in \mathcal{G}$. Let $n, k_1, k_2, m, r, t$ be positive integers satisfying $n > k_1 + k_2$.
arxiv:2611.13749.authors: Zhen Jia, Qing Xiang, Jimeng Xiao, Huajun Zhang

arxiv:2611.13753.title: Gaussian limits for non-cyclic and elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of the multiplicative group
arxiv:2611.13753.summary: We study the number of non-cyclic Sylow subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$. Pollack suggested investigating whether this count has a limiting distribution after suitable normalization. For uniformly chosen $n\le x$, we prove a Gaussian limit with variance asymptotic to $\tfrac12\log_2x/\log_3x$.

arxiv:2611.13786.title: Limit theorems for dispersing billiards with infinite cusps
arxiv:2611.13786.summary: Extending Lenci's work in CMP (2002), Chaos (2003), we present new insights into semi-dispersing billiards with infinite cusps. We investigate the Convergence to Stable Processes (CSP) and Functional Central Limit Theorems (FCLT) both for the collision map and for the billiard flow. Whereas the billiard map always preserves an infinite measure equivalent to Lebesgue, the billiard flow preserves the Lebesgue measure, which is either finite or infinite depending on the finiteness of the area of the billiard table.
arxiv:2611.13786.authors: Marco Lenci, Fran\c{c}oise P\`ene, Hong-Kun Zhang

arxiv:2611.13803.title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
arxiv:2611.13803.summary: We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here.

arxiv:2611.13813.title: Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
arxiv:2611.13813.summary: For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$.
arxiv:2611.13813.authors: Payal Vasoya, Miral Doshi, Devsi Bantva

arxiv:2611.13823.title: Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors
arxiv:2611.13823.summary: Let $\mathscr{H}_m(n)$ denote the set of real Hankel tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$, and let $\textbf{H}\in\mathscr{H}_m(n)$, where $m\ge3$ and $n\ge1$. Set $M=(m-1)(n-1)+1$. First, we prove that the CP rank $r(\textbf{H})\le M$ and that CP rank is additive under direct sums of $\textbf{H}$ with any real tensor $\textbf{T}$ of the same order.

arxiv:2611.13824.title: On funnel control with star-shaped funnels
arxiv:2611.13824.summary: Funnel control for the trivial control-affine prototype is extended to the case of star-shaped funnels, both in the special case that the dynamical system is formulated in an Euclidean space and the general case of a Riemannian manifold.

arxiv:2611.13838.title: Towards funnel control on Riemannian manifolds
arxiv:2611.13838.summary: Funnel control for time-invariant control-affine systems with relative degree one is transferred to the case of dynamical systems evolving on a Riemannian manifold. It is shown that, under some regularity assumptions, the classical proofs carry over. The regularity assumptions reflect the particularities of the nonlinear theory and degenerate in the classical Euclidean case.

arxiv:2611.13847.title: Counting $K_4$-saturating non-edges in Nosal graphs
arxiv:2611.13847.summary: A non-edge of a $K_4$-free graph is $K_4$-saturating if adding it creates a copy of $K_4$, and $f(G)$ counts these non-edges. Erd\H{o}s and Tuza showed that the minimum of $f$ over $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graphs jumps from zero to a quadratic quantity once the number of edges exceeds $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Balogh and Liu [J.

arxiv:2611.13848.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials
arxiv:2611.13848.summary: Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$.

arxiv:2611.13858.title: A Second Order Extended Zarankiewicz Number for Biquadratic SOS Rank
arxiv:2611.13858.summary: We introduce the \emph{second order extended Zarankiewicz number} $z_{2M}(m,n)$, obtained from the second order Zarankiewicz number $z_2(m,n)$ of L\"ofberg and Qi by relaxing the simplicity condition $(S)$ for the \emph{secondary halves} of 2-edges, while keeping the limited condition $|E_1|=z(m,n)$. We prove the hierarchy $$ BSR(m,n)\ge z_{2M}(m,n)\ge z_2(m,n)\ge z_{SL}(m,n)\ge z_{RL}(m,n)\ge z_{wL}(m,n)\ge z(m,n), $$ and show that $z_{2M}$ is not capped by the universal cell bound. We prove the counting bound $z_{2M}(m,n)\le mn-1$, and a sharper linear-in-$m$ bound for fixed $n$ obtained from orthogonality of coefficient vectors.

arxiv:2611.13861.title: From Complex Regularization to Polynomial Flow: Capture and Escape in Rocking Dynamics
arxiv:2611.13861.summary: We develop a planar polynomial system based on a complex regularization of free rocking and analyze the equilibrium states and phase portraits via an effective radial potential. The conflict between the centrifugal effect, which is introduced by means of regularization, and gravity yields a potential well and an escape barrier for 0 < beta < 27/256; both vanish at a saddle-node bifurcation point. The exact energy conservation law allows us to separate dissipative relaxation, conservative periodic motions along the radial direction, and energy creating trajectories.
arxiv:2611.13861.authors: Francisco Prieto-Castrillo, Set P\'erez-Gonz\'alez, Jes\'us S. P\'erez del R\'io

arxiv:2611.13877.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
arxiv:2611.13877.summary: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.

arxiv:2611.13887.title: Congruences for Dedekind numbers
arxiv:2611.13887.summary: We study congruence properties of Dedekind numbers $d_n$. Our approach relies on actions of $p$-subgroups of symmetric groups on posets of monotone functions and leads to the congruences $d_{10}\equiv 106\pmod{210}$, $d_{11}\equiv 117\pmod{210}$, and $d_{12}\equiv 12\pmod{30}$. In particular, $d_{11}$ is odd, confirming a claim stated by Yamamoto without a proof.
arxiv:2611.13887.authors: Bart{\l}omiej Pawelski, Andrzej Szepietowski, B{\l}a\.zej Szepietowski

arxiv:2611.13896.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
arxiv:2611.13896.summary: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope…

arxiv:2611.13897.title: On the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for the quantum semisimple groups
arxiv:2611.13897.summary: The Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, when it holds for an algebra, characterizes its primitive ideals ( that is, the annihilators of irreducible representations) both algebraically and topologically within the prime spectrum. A stronger form, known as the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, was introduced by Bell, Launois, and Nolan in their work on 'A strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for quantum Schubert cells'. In this paper, we prove that the generic quantized coordinate rings of connected, simply connected semisimple complex algebraic groups satisfy the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence.

arxiv:2611.13901.title: Switching reconstruction of signed graphs: net-degree and balance
arxiv:2611.13901.summary: The switching reconstruction problem for $2$-edge-colored graphs, introduced by Bondy and Mercier, asks whether such a graph is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of the graphs obtained by exchanging the colors of the edges at each vertex; for complete underlying graphs it is the vertex-switching reconstruction problem of Stanley. We study this problem in the language of signed graphs, where the net-degree of a vertex and the notion of balance come naturally into play. We prove that a signed graph on $n\neq4$ vertices is reconstructible when its net-degrees are all positive, all negative or all zero, which generalizes the reconstructibility of regular graphs in Stanley's problem.
arxiv:2611.13901.authors: Matteo Cavaleri, Alfredo Donno, Stefano Spessato

arxiv:2611.13904.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
arxiv:2611.13904.summary: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $\sigma$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $\Omega=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a H\"older Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $\mu \in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (\mu)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $\sigma$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(\mu)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one.
arxiv:2611.13904.authors: Artur O. Lopes, Elismar R. Oliveira

arxiv:2611.13917.title: Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
arxiv:2611.13917.summary: We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$.
arxiv:2611.13917.authors: Jan Diester, Kolja K\"uhn, Manuel Rapp, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

arxiv:2611.13924.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
arxiv:2611.13924.summary: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.

arxiv:2611.13958.title: Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons
arxiv:2611.13958.summary: Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie.

arxiv:2611.13959.title: Triangle Factors in the Semi-Random Graph Process
arxiv:2611.13959.summary: The semi-random graph process is a single player game which starts with an empty graph on $n$ vertices and in each round the player is offered a random vertex and connects it to a vertex selected according to some strategy $\mathcal{S}$. The goal is, in as few rounds as possible, to arrive at a graph that satisfies some graph property $\mathcal{P}$. The main contribution of this work is to show that there is a strategy $\mathcal{S}$ which creates a $K_3$-factor in at most $2.929329 \, n$ rounds w.h.p.

arxiv:2611.13961.title: On the minimum number of entries in a set of maximal mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares
arxiv:2611.13961.summary: In superimposed form, a set of $k\ge2$ mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares of order $n$ is said to be maximal if no additional $k$-tuple may be inserted into any empty cell without violating orthogonality or the Latin property. For $k=2$ and $n\ge 21$ it is shown that the minimum number of filled cells in such a square is $\lceil n^2/3 \rceil$. Likewise for $k=3$ and $n\ge 44$ the minimum number of filled cells is $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil$ or $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil+1$, depending on the residue of $n$ modulo 4.
arxiv:2611.13961.authors: Diane M. Donovan, Mike J. Grannell, Emine Sule Yazici

arxiv:2611.13974.title: Two-parameter versus one-parameter quantum groups: structural differences arising from the type~$D$ phenomenon
arxiv:2611.13974.summary: This paper investigates several differences between two-parameter and one-parameter quantum (affine) algebras. We compare their Hopf algebra structures, algebra structures, automorphism groups of positive parts and extended Borel algebras, and module categories beyond the finite-dimensional setting. These differences are closely related to what we call \textit{``the type $D$ phenomenon''}, which widely appears in the structure of both finite and affine two-parameter quantum groups.
arxiv:2611.13974.authors: Naihong Hu, Marc Rosso, Xiao Xu

arxiv:2611.13977.title: On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals
arxiv:2611.13977.summary: The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight.

arxiv:2611.13996.title: Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry
arxiv:2611.13996.summary: We give a comprehensive study of Frege's modified election method as a proportional allocation rule and as a dynamical system. The method was introduced by Harrenstein, Lackner and Lackner (2022) as a modification of Frege's original proposal (1918), and it coincides with the greedy algorithm for the chairman assignment problem studied by Coppersmith et al. (2011).

arxiv:2611.14005.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
arxiv:2611.14005.summary: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations.
arxiv:2611.14005.authors: Thierry Dana-Picard, Arie Haenel, Daniel Tsirkin

arxiv:2611.14020.title: Hamiltonian GKM spaces via Gromov-Witten theory
arxiv:2611.14020.summary: We use equivariant Gromov-Witten theory to prove the generalised symplectic Mukai inequality for Hamiltonian GKM spaces with large pseudoindex or a special vertex, including smooth Schubert varieties. We also classify all Hamiltonian GKM graphs when the pseudoindex is at least the complex dimension, obtaining a Hamiltonian GKM analogue of the classical Kobayashi-Ochiai classification of complex projective space and complex quadrics. Of independent interest are our connectivity theorem for a low-magnitude subgraph of the GKM graph (reminiscent of Campana and Koll\'ar-Miyaoka-Mori's rational chain connectedness of Fano manifolds), and a local Mukai-type theorem that applies at each vertex.

arxiv:2611.14052.title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
arxiv:2611.14052.summary: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $\Delta-1$, where $\Delta$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum.

arxiv:2611.14054.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
arxiv:2611.14054.summary: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process.

arxiv:2611.14057.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras
arxiv:2611.14057.summary: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras.
arxiv:2611.14057.authors: Odysseas Giatagantzidis, Carolin Hartung, Nupur Jain, Ren\'e Marczinzik, Martin Rubey, Sven Schmitz

arxiv:2611.14069.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
arxiv:2611.14069.summary: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion.

arxiv:2611.14070.title: Treewidth versus Hadwiger number: Graph classes with dominated balanced separators are quasi-linearly treewidth-Hadwiger bounded
arxiv:2611.14070.summary: In a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, the treewidth of a graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is bounded by a function of the size of a largest clique minor of the graph if and only if the class $\mathcal{G}$ excludes some planar graph as an induced minor. Campbell et al. (arXiv 2024) conjectured that such a bounding function can always be chosen to be linear.
arxiv:2611.14070.authors: Cl\'ement Dallard, J. Pascal Gollin, Andrea Munaro

arxiv:2611.14071.title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
arxiv:2611.14071.summary: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.

arxiv:2611.14078.title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
arxiv:2611.14078.summary: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $\alpha/t$ with $\alpha\geq 1$, and that the trajectory…
arxiv:2611.14078.authors: Radu Ioan Bo\c{t}, Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella, Tr\'{\i} Minh L\^e

arxiv:2611.14084.title: Representations of the quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
arxiv:2611.14084.summary: Let $q$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity with $p\ge2$, and let $H=D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ be the Drinfeld double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the dual Hopf algebra and the cross relations of $H$. A change of generator gives a classification of the simple $H$-modules.
arxiv:2611.14084.authors: Hua Sun, Huixiang Chen, Xiaoming Li, Huan Jia

arxiv:2611.14085.title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
arxiv:2611.14085.summary: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics.

arxiv:2611.14105.title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section
arxiv:2611.14105.summary: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincar\'e duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model.

arxiv:2611.14110.title: Loops and mirrors
arxiv:2611.14110.summary: For a smooth affine complex variety X we construct a Q-algebra LH(X), loop cohomology, in terms of the formal-loop space of X. We conjecture that it is isomorphic to the symplectic cohomology of X. The degree-zero loop cohomology subalgebra is finitely generated for polarized log Calabi-Yau X, constructing an intrinsic mirror affine coordinate ring.

arxiv:2611.14125.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
arxiv:2611.14125.summary: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$.

arxiv:2611.14127.title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
arxiv:2611.14127.summary: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable.

arxiv:2611.14131.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory for Lines and Finite Configurations
arxiv:2611.14131.summary: A classical question in Euclidean Ramsey theory, posed by Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus, asks which finite configurations $X\subset\mathbb E^2$ must appear in blue under every red--blue coloring of the plane having no red pair of points distance one apart. For $m \ge 2$, let $\ell_m$ denote the line of $m$ points with consecutive points distance one apart. Tsaturian showed that $\ell_5$ is unavoidable; we improve this to $\ell_7$.
arxiv:2611.14131.authors: Ryan Hoff, Gary Hu, Yumo Liu

arxiv:2611.14140.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
arxiv:2611.14140.summary: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming.
arxiv:2611.14140.authors: Stefan Kuhlmann, Timm Oertel, Nicola Wengiel

arxiv:2611.14144.title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications
arxiv:2611.14144.summary: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$.

arxiv:2611.14160.title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests and complete bipartite graphs
arxiv:2611.14160.summary: For a graph $G$ and an integer $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, where $e(G)$ denotes the number of edges of $G$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. Bialostocki and Dierker (1990) [4] conjectured that $R(F,\mathbb Z_{e(F)})/R(F,2)\to1$ uniformly over all forests $F$ as $e(F)\to\infty$, where $R(F,2)$ is the two-color Ramsey number, and Caro (1991) [9] conjectured that $R(tG,\mathbb Z_t)=t(|V(G)|+d)-d$ for $t\ge2$ disjoint copies of $G$, where $d=\operatorname{def}_t(G)$ is the defect. We disprove the first conjecture by an infinite family of trees.

arxiv:2611.14177.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
arxiv:2611.14177.summary: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions.

arxiv:2611.14178.title: Coxeter cubes on the graph associahedron and separable elements
arxiv:2611.14178.summary: A Coxeter cube is a Boolean lattice inside a finite Coxeter group $W$ such that every square is a Coxeter square in the sense of Dyer and Wang. A Coxeter cube of full dimension based at the identity, which we call a based cube, is the same as a partition of the positive roots into inversion sets with one simple root in each block. These partitions were studied by Dimitrov, Gigliotti, Ossip, Paquette and Wehlau under the name of fine decompositions, and by Hohlweg and Pons as partitions of $w_0$.

arxiv:2611.14187.title: On ergodicity and symmetry for affine systems
arxiv:2611.14187.summary: Let $f$ be a volume-preserving affine diffeomorphism of a compact homogeneous space with smooth centralizer ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$. We establish the following two equivalences: (1) $f$ is ergodic if and only if ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$ is a finite-dimensional Lie group; (2) $f$ is non-ergodic if and only if ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$ contains either $C_c^{\infty}((0,1),\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathrm{Diff}_c^{\infty}((0,1))$. This strengthens the corresponding perturbative version established in arXiv:2504.09084.
arxiv:2611.14187.authors: Danijela Damjanovic, Amie Wilkinson, Chengyang Wu, Disheng Xu

arxiv:2611.14190.title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
arxiv:2611.14190.summary: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.
arxiv:2611.14190.authors: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Thomas Hameister, Xinchun Ma

arxiv:2611.14191.title: The Monophonic Directed Convexities
arxiv:2611.14191.summary: Graph Convexity is a topic with many papers in the literature, especially on the $P_3$, geodesic, and monophonic convexities in undirected graphs. Regarding directed graphs, Erd{\H o}s et al. in 1972 and Chartrand and Zhang in 2000 obtained the first results on the $P_3$ and geodesic convexities for directed graphs, respectively. In this paper, we start the investigation of monophonic convexity on directed graphs.
arxiv:2611.14191.authors: J\'ulio Ara\'ujo, Ana Karolinna Maia, Thiago Marcilon, Nicolas Nisse, Rudini M. Sampaio

arxiv:2611.14194.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
arxiv:2611.14194.summary: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J.
arxiv:2611.14194.authors: Vida Dujmovi\'c, Cyril Gavoille, Gwena\"el Joret, Piotr Micek, Pat Morin, David R. Wood

arxiv:2611.14198.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
arxiv:2611.14198.summary: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known.

arxiv:2611.14234.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
arxiv:2611.14234.summary: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geq\pi(s-1)$.

arxiv:2611.14248.title: The zero-sum constant $\mathsf{s}_p^*$ and inverse problem
arxiv:2611.14248.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime. We denote by $\mathsf{s}_{p}^{*}$ the smallest integer $l$ such that, out of any given $l$ integers coprime with $p$, one can select $p$ integers satisfying that the sum of the $p$ integers is a multiple of $p$, but not a multiple of $p^{2}$. It was conjectured that $\mathsf{s}_p^*=2p+1$.

arxiv:2611.14268.title: A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups
arxiv:2611.14268.summary: We characterize almost symmetric numerical semigroups in terms of their associated Young diagrams, showing that almost symmetry is equivalent to a simple numerical identity relating the genus, the type, and the number of small elements, and also to a combinatorial condition on the hook lengths of the diagram. We then introduce a symmetrization procedure that associates with each almost symmetric numerical semigroup a symmetric numerical set. This yields a map from the set of almost symmetric numerical semigroups to the set of symmetric numerical sets.
arxiv:2611.14268.authors: Manuel Delgado, Meral S\"uer, Mehmet Ye\c{s}il

arxiv:2611.14277.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
arxiv:2611.14277.summary: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections.

arxiv:2611.14283.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
arxiv:2611.14283.summary: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp.

arxiv:2611.14290.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
arxiv:2611.14290.summary: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight.
arxiv:2611.14290.authors: Juan D. V\'elez, Carlos A. Cadavid

arxiv:2611.14294.title: Irrationality and Noether--Lefschetz loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces
arxiv:2611.14294.summary: The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we construct examples of families of surfaces where the locus of points in the base with constant degree of irrationality is not constructible. Second, we explore the notion of gonality loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces, which are characterized by the existence of a smooth curve with fixed gonality.
arxiv:2611.14294.authors: Dori Bejleri, Nathan Chen, Benjamin Church, Kristin DeVleming

arxiv:2611.14298.title: Flagged Grothendieck enumerators and ribbon decomposition determinants
arxiv:2611.14298.summary: We establish Hamel--Goulden-type ribbon decomposition determinantal formulas for a new class of symmetric functions called flagged Grothendieck enumerators. In particular, these functions generalize both canonical refined stable Grothendieck polynomials and their duals. The proof uses Talaska's formula via flows on planar lattice graphs with systems of paths and cycles.

arxiv:2611.14300.title: Negative-Dimensional Simplicial Complexes via the Grothendieck Group of the Join Monoid
arxiv:2611.14300.summary: We introduce a framework that extends classical combinatorial and topological notions of simplicial complexes to a setting that includes simplicial complexes of negative dimension. This is achieved by considering the Grothendieck group of the commutative monoid of finite simplicial complexes under the join operation, which provides formal inverses and allows negative-dimensional objects to be defined. Within this group we adapt standard invariants such as $f$- and $h$-vectors, their corresponding polynomials, and the Euler characteristic.
arxiv:2611.14300.authors: Pedro J. Chocano, L. Felipe Prieto-Mart\'inez

arxiv:2611.14302.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
arxiv:2611.14302.summary: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an…
arxiv:2611.14302.authors: Samuel Bronstein, Colin Davalo, Qiongling Li

arxiv:2611.14304.title: Noetherian connected braided Hopf algebras are affine
arxiv:2611.14304.summary: The well-known Wu--Zhang question asks whether every Noetherian Hopf algebra over a field is affine (finitely generated as an algebra). In this paper, we extend this fundamental problem to the braided setting within the monoidal category ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ of left Yetter--Drinfel'd modules over a Hopf algebra $H$. By developing term-rewriting methods based on reduction orderings and prime-word factorizations in free prebraided algebras, we establish explicit expansions for YD-triangular comultiplications.

arxiv:2611.14316.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
arxiv:2611.14316.summary: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $\Sigma_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle.
arxiv:2611.14316.authors: Juan Diego Velez Caicedo, Carlos A. Cadavid

arxiv:2611.14322.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
arxiv:2611.14322.summary: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial.

arxiv:2611.14327.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
arxiv:2611.14327.summary: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [F\"orster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$.
arxiv:2611.14327.authors: Laura Merker, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

arxiv:2611.14337.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
arxiv:2611.14337.summary: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one.

arxiv:2611.14347.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
arxiv:2611.14347.summary: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor.

arxiv:2611.14367.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
arxiv:2611.14367.summary: K\"uhnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case.

arxiv:2611.14384.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
arxiv:2611.14384.summary: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(\eta(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(\eta(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $\eta$ is the Erd\H{o}s--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval…

arxiv:2611.14386.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
arxiv:2611.14386.summary: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not.

arxiv:2611.14396.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
arxiv:2611.14396.summary: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

arxiv:2611.14402.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
arxiv:2611.14402.summary: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected.
arxiv:2611.14402.authors: Pinxian Bie, Peien Du, Zhengjie Yu

arxiv:2611.14417.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
arxiv:2611.14417.summary: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.

arxiv:2611.14430.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
arxiv:2611.14430.summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$.
arxiv:2611.14430.authors: Jes\'us F. Espinoza, Mart\'in Eduardo Fr\'ias-Armenta, Rosal\'ia G. Hern\'andez-Amador, H\'ector A. Hern\'andez-Hern\'andez

arxiv:2611.14449.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
arxiv:2611.14449.summary: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$.

arxiv:2611.14453.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
arxiv:2611.14453.summary: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Mir\'o-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.

arxiv:2611.14466.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
arxiv:2611.14466.summary: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number.
arxiv:2611.14466.authors: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Rog\'erio Mol

arxiv:2611.14471.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
arxiv:2611.14471.summary: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.
arxiv:2611.14471.authors: Oscar Defrain, Corentin Jazeron, Kazuhisa Makino

arxiv:2611.14475.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
arxiv:2611.14475.summary: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl.

arxiv:2611.14503.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
arxiv:2611.14503.summary: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$\alpha$-bundles} and \emph{$\beta$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov.

arxiv:2611.14506.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
arxiv:2611.14506.summary: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction.

arxiv:2611.14513.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
arxiv:2611.14513.summary: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1.
arxiv:2611.14513.authors: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda

arxiv:2611.14543.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
arxiv:2611.14543.summary: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes.

arxiv:2611.14546.title: The Sprague--Grundy Function of Slow Exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ Piles
arxiv:2611.14546.summary: We give an explicit formula for the normal-play Sprague--Grundy (SG) function of slow exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ piles. A move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. A truncation preserves every legal move sequence.

arxiv:2611.14550.title: Quivers with potential for quantum affine superalgebras
arxiv:2611.14550.summary: We construct a surjective algebra homomorphism from the $K$-theoretic Hall algebras of certain quivers with potential to the (half) quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras.

arxiv:2611.14566.title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
arxiv:2611.14566.summary: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group.

arxiv:2611.14579.title: Random Chowla and Goldbach Conjectures
arxiv:2611.14579.summary: We prove that for a Rademacher random multiplicative function $(f(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and any non-linear polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ admitting a positive constant $\kappa_P$ such that \[\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{n\in\left[N\right]:P(n)\text{ is square-free}\}}{N} =\kappa_P,\] we have \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{\kappa_PN}}\sum_{n\leqslant N}f(P(n)) \xrightarrow[]{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1), \] as $N\rightarrow\infty $, where convergence is in distribution to a standard Gaussian. Using a direct combinatorial argument, we establish paucity estimates for non-trivial square products of square-free polynomial values at every fixed moment order. These estimates yield the Gaussian limit by the method…

arxiv:2611.14631.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
arxiv:2611.14631.summary: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods,…

arxiv:2611.14667.title: Twisted algebras of invariant formal power series over monoids
arxiv:2611.14667.summary: We develop a general monoid-theoretic framework to construct and study graded and color Hopf algebras of formal power series of bounded degree invariant under group actions. Rather than working with external alphabets of commuting, noncommuting, or anti-commuting variables, we start from an abstract monoid $M$ equipped with a $2$-cocycle twisting $\tau:M\times M\to \mathbb{K}$, which is allowed to vanish, a bigrading over a commutative monoid $\mathcal{G}\times\mathbb{N}$ endowed with a bicharacter $\phi$, and a group $G$ acting on $M$ via a bigraded action $\rho$ that is quasi-multiplicative with respect to $\tau$, coupled with a $1$-cocycle weight function $\omega:G\times…
arxiv:2611.14667.authors: Diego Arcis, Camilo Gonz\'alez, Sebasti\'an M\'arquez

arxiv:2611.14674.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with ten vertices
arxiv:2611.14674.summary: We prove that a $4$-polytope with ten vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{25}{384}(10 + 2\sqrt{5})$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of two regular pentagons inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. As for six to nine vertices, the optimum is thus the convex hull of two regular polygons in orthogonal planes. On the combinatorial type of the pair, whose boundary complex is the join of two $5$-cycles, the sharp bound follows from our work on nine vertices.

arxiv:2611.14682.title: Lagrangian cobordisms and morphisms of persistence modules
arxiv:2611.14682.summary: We consider a version of Legendrian contact homology filtered by the action of Reeb chords. In this version, a union of two disjoint exact Lagrangian cobordisms with Legendrian boundary conditions gives rise to a morphism between persistence modules. We discuss a certain algebraic invariant of such morphisms and use it to obtain obstructions to Lagrangian isotopies of the cobordisms, as well as applications to symplectic and contact dynamics.

arxiv:2611.14689.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
arxiv:2611.14689.summary: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$.
arxiv:2611.14689.authors: Felipe Monteiro, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva
