arxiv:2611.14694.title: Real positive definite counterexamples to a monotonicity conjecture for the $q$-permanent
arxiv:2611.14694.summary: The $q$-permanent $P_q$ of an $n\times n$ matrix weights the term of each permutation $\sigma$ by $q^{\inv(\sigma)}$, where $\inv(\sigma)$ is the number of inversions of $\sigma$. It interpolates between the determinant ($q=-1$) and the permanent ($q=1$). Extending a conjecture of Bapat on $[-1,1]$, it was conjectured in 2010 that the $q$-permanent of every non-diagonal real symmetric positive definite matrix is strictly increasing on an interval $(\varepsilon,+\infty)$ with $\varepsilon<-1$.
arxiv:2611.14694.authors: Carlos M. da Fonseca, Dev D. Goyal

arxiv:2611.14702.title: Chaotic-Periodic Alternation in a Financial System with Double Delays
arxiv:2611.14702.summary: In this paper we present the chaotic-periodic alternation phenomenon within a three-dimensional nonlinear financial system subjected to Pyragas-type time-delayed feedback, as well as the lag effect of the interest rate in the price index dynamics. Through numerical analysis, transitions to chaos, including period-doubling cascades, period-halving routes, and incommensurable-period dynamics are characterized. The emergence of chaotic-periodic alternation are found and described.
arxiv:2611.14702.authors: Jes\'us Salinas-Gutierrez, V\'ictor F. Bre\~na-Medina, Marcos \'Angel Gonz\'alez-Olvera, Anah\'i Flores-P\'erez

arxiv:2611.14730.title: Connected regular $\Gamma$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
arxiv:2611.14730.summary: Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $\Gamma$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $\Gamma$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $\Gamma$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kov\'a\v{r} and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$.
arxiv:2611.14730.authors: Ahmet Batal, Sylwia Cichacz, Hubert Grochowski

arxiv:2611.14738.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
arxiv:2611.14738.summary: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT.
arxiv:2611.14738.authors: Wyatt Olson, Jared Soundy, J. Z. Schroeder

arxiv:2611.14743.title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
arxiv:2611.14743.summary: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products. Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit.

arxiv:2611.14747.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
arxiv:2611.14747.summary: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor.

arxiv:2611.14754.title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
arxiv:2611.14754.summary: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981.
arxiv:2611.14754.authors: Zachary Halberstam, Mitchell Lee, Carl Schildkraut

arxiv:2611.14756.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
arxiv:2611.14756.summary:
The multivariate breeder's equation $\Delta ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\infty\lambda_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$.

arxiv:2611.14771.title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
arxiv:2611.14771.summary: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $\beta$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in \S 7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $\beta$.

arxiv:2611.14773.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
arxiv:2611.14773.summary:
We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $
u$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}ight)^
u$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}ight)^
u$ are isomorphic if and only if $
u$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$.
arxiv:2611.14773.authors: Nicolle Gonz\'alez, John Lentfer, Pablo S. Ocal

arxiv:2611.14793.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
arxiv:2611.14793.summary: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$.

arxiv:2611.14802.title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
arxiv:2611.14802.summary: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$\Omega$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.
arxiv:2611.14802.authors: Muhammad Waqar Ul Hassan, G. Stacey Staples

arxiv:2611.14806.title: Real monopole Floer homology and the Alexander polynomial
arxiv:2611.14806.summary: We prove that the Euler characteristic of the framed real monopole Floer homology of the double branched cover of a link is given by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at $\sqrt{-1}$. For knots $K$ with determinant one, this formula shows that Miyazawa's degree invariant of $K$ can be computed in terms of the Alexander polynomial of $K$. The proof involves a new connected-sum formula and oriented skein exact triangles for some new variants of real monopole Floer homology, called the diagonal and cone real monopole Floer homology, which admit mod-two gradings.

arxiv:2611.14810.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
arxiv:2611.14810.summary: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness.
arxiv:2611.14810.authors: Kevin Coulembier, Johannes Flake, Joseph Newton, Victor Ostrik

arxiv:2611.14812.title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
arxiv:2611.14812.summary: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.

arxiv:2611.14816.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
arxiv:2611.14816.summary: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup.
arxiv:2611.14816.authors: Patricio Almir\'on, Julio Jos\'e Moyano-Fern\'andez, Adri\'an Olivares-Fern\'andez

arxiv:2611.14817.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
arxiv:2611.14817.summary: A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmovi\'c, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path.

arxiv:2611.14819.title: Permutation codes via spectral graph theory
arxiv:2611.14819.summary: We use the Eigenvalue Method to obtain upper spectral bounds on the size of permutation codes in the Hamming, Ulam, Cayley and Kendall metrics. For the Kendall metric, we improve the double-ball upper bound of Buzaglo and Etzion [IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 2015] at minimum distance four and lengths seven and eight. For the Cayley metric, we improve the sphere packing bound, and determine when these spectral improvements occur.
arxiv:2611.14819.authors: Aida Abiad, Delio Jaramillo-Velez, Kirsten D. Morris, Joachim Rosenthal

arxiv:2611.14824.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.14824.summary: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition.

arxiv:2611.14841.title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
arxiv:2611.14841.summary: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values.

arxiv:2611.14847.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
arxiv:2611.14847.summary: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

arxiv:2611.14873.title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
arxiv:2611.14873.summary: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

arxiv:2611.14906.title: The frustration index of fully frustrated hypercubes
arxiv:2611.14906.summary: The frustration index of a signed graph is the minimum number of edges meeting every negative cycle. Let $F_n$ be the frustration index of the signed $n$-cube $Q_n$ in which every square is negative. Using signings constructed from weighted cubes, we prove that for every positive integer $r$, \[ F_{r^2+1}=(r^2-r+1)2^{r^2-1}.

arxiv:2611.14909.title: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs
arxiv:2611.14909.summary: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, we say that a set $A\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ is an $(r,c)$ subspace evasive set if and only if for any affine subspace $U\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ with bounded dimension $\dim(U)\leq r$, the intersection size $|A\cap U|$ is at most $c$. The probabilistic method shows the existence of $(r,c)$ subspace evasive sets with $|A| = q^{(1-\epsilon) n}$ with $c = O(r/\epsilon)$. However, the best explicit constructions by Dvir--Lovett (STOC 2012) and Ben-Aroya--Shinkar (CJTCS 2013) have $c$ growing as an exponential function of $r$.
arxiv:2611.14909.authors: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Mahdi Cheraghchi, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami, Aaron Putterman, Zihan Zhang

arxiv:2611.14913.title: Exact Values and Bounds for Four Color Quadratic Polynomial van der Waerden Numbers
arxiv:2611.14913.summary: For a nonzero polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $P(0)=0$, let $W(P(x);4)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every four coloring of $[N]$ contains distinct integers $u,v$ of the same color with $v-u=P(d)$ for some integer $d$. The best known general upper bounds for polynomial van der Waerden numbers are primitive recursive but remain enormous compared with the few known exact values. In this paper we determine the exact four color polynomial van der Waerden numbers for \[ \begin{gathered} x^2+x,\quad 2x^2+x,\quad 3x^2+x,\\ x^2+7x,\quad 2x^2+7x,\quad 3x^2+7x,\\ x^2+9x,\quad 2x^2+9x,\quad 3x^2+11x.
arxiv:2611.14913.authors: Ishan Kumthekar, William Gasarch, William Regli, Ian Whitehouse

arxiv:2611.14936.title: Relative divisors and intersections of noncommutative rational localizations
arxiv:2611.14936.summary: The simple constituents of monic pencils determine singularity support in a free skew field. For a pencil inverse algebra that is a free ideal ring, the multiplicities of the nonbase constituents compute the scalar-regular part of Cohn's matrix divisor theory. For independent generic invertible matrices of size at least two, every entry of a nonidentity free-group word is an atom with one relative singularity component.

arxiv:2611.14988.title: Thin Edges in Braces
arxiv:2611.14988.summary: A connected graph with at least two vertices is matching covered if each of its edges is contained in a perfect matching. A bipartite matching covered graph is a brace if no nontrivial cut meets every perfect matching in exactly one edge.An edge $e$ of a brace $G$ is thin if $G-e$ is matching covered and its retract is a brace. Every brace can be reduced to $K_2$ or $C_4$ by successively deleting thin edges and taking retracts.

arxiv:2611.15008.title: The Merino-Welsh conjecture for sparse and dense graphs
arxiv:2611.15008.summary: The Merino-Welsh conjecture states that the Tutte polynomial $T_G(x,y)$ of a loopless and bridgeless graph $G$ satisfies the inequality $\max\{T_G(2,0),T_G(0,2)\}\geq T_G(1,1).$ It is known to hold for several graph classes, among them sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In this paper, we improve the previously known sufficient density conditions and show that the multiplicative version of the conjecture also holds for sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In particular, we show that for a connected graph $G$ with $m$ edges and $n$ vertices, the Merino-Welsh conjecture holds if either $m\leq1.64(n-1)$ and $G$ is loopless or $m\geq2.55(n-1)$ and $G$ is bridgeless,…

arxiv:2611.15014.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent for the integrated density of states
arxiv:2611.15014.summary: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime.

arxiv:2611.15027.title: Sidorenko inequalities and symmetry-forcing for graph orientations
arxiv:2611.15027.summary: We study directed graphs whose homomorphism densities never increase or never decrease when the host edge directions are randomized. We call these properties oriented Sidorenko (OS) and oriented anti-Sidorenko (OAS), respectively. A directed graph is symmetry-forcing if equality between its original and randomized densities forces quasi-random edge directions.

arxiv:2611.15034.title: On piecewise-regular and quasirational functions
arxiv:2611.15034.summary: We fully characterize piecewise-regular functions on nonsingular real algebraic varieties in terms of continuous quasirational functions. We also obtain extension theorem for piecewise-regular functions defined on closed semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n.$

arxiv:2611.15038.title: A symmetry on Young tableaux with walls and holes
arxiv:2611.15038.summary: The Pons--Batle conjecture on tree-child networks was regarded as a specific and challenging problem in the phylogenetics community. We found an unexpected weighted symmetry for a class of three-row Young tableaux with walls and holes. This weighted symmetry implies the Fuchs--Yu identity, which together with the bijection of Chang, Fuchs, Liu, Wallner, and Yu leads to a simple proof of the Pons--Batle conjecture.
arxiv:2611.15038.authors: Zhicong Lin, Feihu Liu, Jing Liu

arxiv:2611.15043.title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
arxiv:2611.15043.summary: We study the relation between electrical positivity introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy $[9]$ and total positivity of symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks. A particularly convenient framework for our purpose is provided by a construction of an embedding of electrical network into the positive Lagrangian Grassmannian, see Section $1.1$. Employing this technique, we demonstrate that mentioned below two types of positivity do not coincide, see Theorem $2.2$.

arxiv:2611.15065.title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
arxiv:2611.15065.summary: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $\Delta$.
arxiv:2611.15065.authors: Ashleigh Adams-Jessmore, Sean T. Griffin, Tim Ryan

arxiv:2611.15116.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
arxiv:2611.15116.summary: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence.
arxiv:2611.15116.authors: D. E. K\k{e}dzierski, D. Koellmer, P. Kraso\'n

arxiv:2611.15122.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
arxiv:2611.15122.summary: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis.

arxiv:2611.15124.title: Domination in token graphs of graphs with domination number two
arxiv:2611.15124.summary: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two $k$-subsets adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper we study the domination number of $F_k(G)$ for graphs $G$ whose domination number $\gamma(G)$ is at least two, with a primary focus on the case $\gamma(G)=2$. For $k=2$, we give an upper bound for $\gamma(F_2(G))$ in terms of a dominating pair of $G$, and show that this bound is sharp for every double star $S_{a,b}$ with $2\le a\le b$; moreover, we determine the exact value for every double star, namely $\gamma(F_2(S_{a,b}))=2a+b-1$ for $1\le a\le b$.
arxiv:2611.15124.authors: Germ\'an Ben\'itez-Bobadilla, Fernando Esteban Contreras-Mendoza, Sergio Gerardo G\'omez-Galicia, Ana Trujillo-Negrete

arxiv:2611.15129.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
arxiv:2611.15129.summary: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic.

arxiv:2611.15148.title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
arxiv:2611.15148.summary: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy.

arxiv:2611.15164.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
arxiv:2611.15164.summary: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J.

arxiv:2611.15179.title: Volume asymptotics for a family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
arxiv:2611.15179.summary: For the family $\{\mathcal{M}_{g,k}\}_{g\geqslant k\geqslant 0}$ of orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary and cusps introduced by R.~Frigerio, B.~Martelli, and C.~Petronio, the volume of the manifolds depends only on the non-negative integer parameters $g$ and $k$; thus the volume function $Vol(g,k)$ is well defined. The main result of the paper is an asymptotic description of this function: it is approximated by a linear function of $g$ and $k$ whose coefficients are explicitly expressed in terms of the volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and the regular ideal octahedron; moreover, the volume does not exceed the linear approximation by a difference of order…

arxiv:2611.15182.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
arxiv:2611.15182.summary: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness.

arxiv:2611.15191.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
arxiv:2611.15191.summary: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+\Delta)\) is nef and big, then \((X,\Delta)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata.

arxiv:2611.15210.title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
arxiv:2611.15210.summary: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$.

arxiv:2611.15221.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
arxiv:2611.15221.summary: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields.
arxiv:2611.15221.authors: Manuela Aguiar, Ana Dias, Fahimeh Mokhtari

arxiv:2611.15233.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
arxiv:2611.15233.summary: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

arxiv:2611.15244.title: Small cells in great-circle arrangements
arxiv:2611.15244.summary: We study the areas of the cells determined by an arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ distinct great circles on the unit sphere, with no three concurrent. Let $m(\mathcal{A})$ and $M(\mathcal{A})$ denote the smallest and largest cell areas, respectively. Our first result is the bound \[ m(\mathcal{A})\le \frac{C_*+O(n^{-3/4})}{n^2}, \qquad C_*=7.0666071493\ldots , \] where the implied constant is absolute.

arxiv:2611.15249.title: Growth function of the cactus groups
arxiv:2611.15249.summary: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

arxiv:2611.15299.title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
arxiv:2611.15299.summary: A hereditary graph class is small if it contains at most $n!c^n$ labelled graphs on $n$ vertices for some constant $c$. Small classes include proper minor-closed classes and classes of bounded twin-width. We prove that every small class has linear neighbourhood complexity, that is, in every graph in the class, vertex neighbourhoods intersect any $k$-vertex set in only $O(k)$ distinct ways.
arxiv:2611.15299.authors: John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev, Maksim Zhukovskii

arxiv:2611.15308.title: Path complexes with concatenation and their relation to digraphs
arxiv:2611.15308.summary: The path homology theory is based on the notion of path complex and is a part of GLMY-theory created and developed by Grigor'yan, Lin, Muranov, and Yau in a cycle of papers in 2012-2014. In this paper we define a path complex with concatenation ($PC$-complex) which is a particular case of a path complex. We define a natural topology on a set of vertices of any $PC$-complex, and describe properties of this topology and its relation to the discrete topology of Alexandroff.

arxiv:2611.15312.title: Nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic for rank-2 vector bundles over curves
arxiv:2611.15312.summary: We describe the Nonabelian Hodge Theory correspondence in positive characteristic between nilpotent Higgs bundles and flat bundles with nilpotent p-curvature, as constructed in the seminal paper by Ogus-Vologodsky, in the special case of rank-2 vector bundles over a smooth projective curve. In this set-up we can rephrase this correspondence as a shift of the extension class of a rank-2 vector bundle by a cohomology class encoding a W_2-lift of the curve. As an application, we obtain that a general rank-2 vector bundle of degree 0 admits a connection with non-zero nilpotent p-curvature.

arxiv:2611.15327.title: The maximum product of nontrivial cross $t$-intersecting families
arxiv:2611.15327.summary: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be nonempty families of $k$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|A\cap B|\ge t$ for all $A\in\mathcal A$ and $B\in\mathcal B$, and suppose that each family has fewer than $t$ common elements. For $k\ge t+2\ge4$ and $n\ge(t+1)(k-t+1)$, we prove \[ |\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\le\max\{h_t(n,k)^2,b_t(n,k)^2\}, \] where \[ h_t(n,k)=\binom{n-t}{k-t}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-t}+t,\quad b_t(n,k)=(t+2)\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-1}+\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-2}. \] The bound is sharp, and we characterize all extremal pairs, whose families have equal sizes but need not coincide.

arxiv:2611.15330.title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
arxiv:2611.15330.summary: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.

arxiv:2611.15340.title: Non-concordant knots with the same trace
arxiv:2611.15340.summary: Miller and Piccirillo demonstrated the existence of non-concordant knots that share the same 0-trace. In this short note, we generalize their result by showing that every smooth concordance class contains a knot K such that, for every nonzero integer n, there exists a knot $K_n$ whose n-trace is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to that of K, but for which $p[K_n] \ne p[K]$ in the topological concordance group for every positive integer p. Furthermore, $p[K_n]$ is distinct from $p[K']$ for any knot K' obtained from K by mirroring and/or reversing its orientation.

arxiv:2611.15344.title: On the statistical reliability of chaotic simulations at reduced precision
arxiv:2611.15344.summary: Reduced-precision arithmetic is increasingly used to accelerate scientific simulation, while AI workloads are driving its growing prominence in hardware design. Yet small arithmetic errors do not necessarily imply accurate statistics. Finite representation limits spatial resolution, while rounding can merge trajectories that should separate in chaotic systems, progressively concentrating probability on a shrinking collection of computer states.

arxiv:2611.15353.title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
arxiv:2611.15353.summary: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism.

arxiv:2611.15358.title: The minimum size of the 3-dimensional torus
arxiv:2611.15358.summary: We prove a conjecture of K\"uhnel, Lassmann, and Lutz, first asked in 1984, that the minimal number of vertices in a triangulation of the $3$-dimensional torus is $15$.
arxiv:2611.15358.authors: Seunghun Lee, Geunho Lim, Eran Nevo

arxiv:2611.15361.title: On the structure of the sets of connections between libration points and some applications
arxiv:2611.15361.summary: This paper presents a methodology for the global description of the sets of heteroclinic and homoclinic connections between the center manifolds of the collinear libration points of the spatial circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The approach builds on high-order parameterizations of the center-stable and center-unstable invariant manifolds and uses them to extract global information on how connections are organized across broad energy ranges. It involves: (a) constructing connectivity maps at the level of invariant tori, which encode which tori in the neighborhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected through heteroclinic and homoclinic trajectories; (b) refining this description to the…

arxiv:2611.15369.title: Combinatorial results for semigroups of order-preserving mappings
arxiv:2611.15369.summary: We investigate combinatorial properties of the semigroup of all order- preserving mappings on {1, 2, . . . , n} and of its subsemigroup of all decreasing order-preserving mappings. We show that the cardinal of the latter is the nth Catalan number and obtain a new proof of the standard Catalan identity. Using ballot arguments and the Reflection principle we find the probability that a random order-preserving mapping is indecomposable, and via the Wallis product we show that the mean number of orbits is of order root n.

arxiv:2611.15376.title: Set-coloring Ramsey numbers with multiple intersections
arxiv:2611.15376.summary: For integers $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$, we introduce the Ramsey number $R(G;r,s,t)$, defined as the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]$ to each edge of $K_N$ yields a copy of $G$ whose edges have at least $t$ colors in common. This generalizes the classical set-coloring Ramsey number $R(G;r,s)=R(G;r,s,1)$, studied since the work of Erdos, Hajnal, and Rado. We show that $t$ cannot in general be eliminated by reparametrization: infinitely many quadruples $(G;r,s,t)$ satisfy $R(G;r,s,t)\ne R(G;a,b)$ for every $a\ge b\ge1$.
arxiv:2611.15376.authors: Guantao Chen, Laihao Ding, Qiong Fan, Xiaolan Hu, Suyun Jiang, Chunxiang Wang

arxiv:2611.15425.title: A polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in fixed dimension
arxiv:2611.15425.summary: In the Traveling Salesman Problem, a route must visit all customers and return to its starting point while minimizing its total length. The Minimum Latency Problem, also known as the Traveling Repairman Problem, instead minimizes the sum of the times at which customers are first visited. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in every fixed dimension, with arbitrary nonnegative customer weights.

arxiv:2611.15477.title: Extremal disc packings in compact hyperbolic surfaces of minimal genus
arxiv:2611.15477.summary: A compact hyperbolic surface is $k$-extremal if it contains $k$ disjoint embedded discs of the largest possible radius; such surfaces are uniformized by surface subgroups of the triangle groups $\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We determine all extremal $k$-packings in every $k$-extremal surface of minimal genus, orientable of genus $2$ and non-orientable of genus $3$: $373$ surface groups in total, all treated in a unified way; $264$ of them had never been studied before. The computation is automatic and verified in exact arithmetic, each packing being certified by an element $\alpha\in\mathrm{PGL}_2$ over an explicit number field with $\alpha^{-1}K\alpha<\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$.

arxiv:2611.15486.title: Independent sets in regular uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.15486.summary: We prove that, for all integers $r\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$, every finite simple $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices satisfies \[ \operatorname{ind}(H)\le \operatorname{ind}(H_d^r)^{n/(rd)}, \] with equality if and only if $H$ is a disjoint union of copies of $H_d^r$. Here $\operatorname{ind}(G)$ denotes the number of independent sets in $G$, and $ H_d^r$ is the $d$-regular $r$-partite $r$-graph on $rd$ vertices obtained by taking all $r$-sets consisting of one vertex from a fixed $d$-vertex set and one of $d$ pairwise disjoint $(r-1)$-sets partitioning the remaining vertices. This settles the conjecture of Balogh, Bollob\'as and Narayanan, who proved the bound for…
arxiv:2611.15486.authors: An Chang, Lusheng Fang, Guorong Gao, Caihong Yang

arxiv:2611.15501.title: Latroids on Young's Lattice
arxiv:2611.15501.summary: Latroids are a generalization of matroids and polymatroids, given by a submodular rank function on a modular lattice. We study integer-valued latroids whose length function is the height of a finite modular lattice, without assuming that the lattice is complemented. We show that their cyclic flats form a lattice and, together with their ranks, determine the rank function.

arxiv:2611.15505.title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
arxiv:2611.15505.summary: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately.

arxiv:2611.15508.title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
arxiv:2611.15508.summary: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger.

arxiv:2611.15512.title: Every rank-three matroid is Z-Rayleigh
arxiv:2611.15512.summary: We prove that every matroid of rank or corank at most three is $Z$-Rayleigh: its multivariate Tutte polynomial satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for every positive weighting and every parameter $0<q\le1$. This settles a conjecture of Mani and answers the rank-$3$ spanning-correlation question of Cocks and the correlated-matroid question of Semple and Welsh. For simple rank-$3$ matroids, we obtain an explicit decomposition of each spanning-set Rayleigh difference into the corresponding basis Rayleigh difference, positively weighted squares, and a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients.

arxiv:2611.15536.title: Strictly Deza Graphs among the Prime Graphs of Solvable Groups
arxiv:2611.15536.summary: We study strictly Deza graphs that occur as prime graphs of finite solvable groups and admit a partition into two cliques. Using Gruber's characterization of the prime graphs of finite solvable groups, we relate this problem to bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs. We first show that a non-complete regular graph with a partition into two cliques has equal parts.

arxiv:2611.15540.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
arxiv:2611.15540.summary: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$.

arxiv:2611.15551.title: Gluing Geometric Chains Of Manifolds And Orbifolds With Corners
arxiv:2611.15551.summary: Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces.

arxiv:2611.15554.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
arxiv:2611.15554.summary: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven.

arxiv:2611.15558.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
arxiv:2611.15558.summary: We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture.

arxiv:2611.15605.title: Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields
arxiv:2611.15605.summary: We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.

arxiv:2611.15611.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
arxiv:2611.15611.summary: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Pl\"ucker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables.

arxiv:2611.15630.title: Categorical orbifold theory
arxiv:2611.15630.summary: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$.
arxiv:2611.15630.authors: Chongying Dong, Siu-Hung Ng, Li Ren, Feng Xu

arxiv:2611.15635.title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
arxiv:2611.15635.summary: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $\Delta(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r \Delta(r)=\Theta(\sqrt{N})=\Theta(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum.

arxiv:2611.15643.title: Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes
arxiv:2611.15643.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$.

arxiv:2611.15649.title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
arxiv:2611.15649.summary: We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator. Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update.

arxiv:2611.15673.title: Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
arxiv:2611.15673.summary: We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions.
arxiv:2611.15673.authors: Honghao Gao, Shijie Gu, Zhenkun Li, Jian Wang

arxiv:2611.15685.title: Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
arxiv:2611.15685.summary: Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.
arxiv:2611.15685.authors: Lifan Guan, Chengyang Wu, Weisheng Wu

arxiv:2611.15696.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
arxiv:2611.15696.summary: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives.

arxiv:2611.15702.title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.15702.summary: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.
arxiv:2611.15702.authors: Christian B\"ohning, Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer, Alena Pirutka, Zhijia Zhang

arxiv:2611.15708.title: Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
arxiv:2611.15708.summary: Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface.
arxiv:2611.15708.authors: Wai Yeung Lam, Carl O. R. Lutz

arxiv:2611.15723.title: Shuffles of permutations in cycle form
arxiv:2611.15723.summary: We study a variation of the shuffle operation on permutations, which acts on their cycle structure instead of their one-line notation. Given two permutations $\sigma\in S_k$ and $\tau\in S_{n-k}$, the $\textit{shuffle-by-cycle}$ $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \tau$ is the set of all permutations in $S_n$ whose set of cycles can be separated into two disjoint subsets: one whose standardization is $\sigma$, and one whose standardization is $\tau$. One can think of the sets $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \tau$ as refinements of conjugacy classes.
arxiv:2611.15723.authors: Ron M. Adin, Sergi Elizalde, Ira M. Gessel, Yuval Roichman

arxiv:2611.15725.title: Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties
arxiv:2611.15725.summary: Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties.

arxiv:2611.15741.title: Skew Zero Forcing Matroids
arxiv:2611.15741.summary: Matroid theory and skew zero forcing (SZF) in graphs are both topics of mathematical interest, but very little is known about their overlap. When a matroid arises from a graph in the traditional way, the edges of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. However, the SZF color change rule for graphs can be viewed as a closure operator on the vertices of a graph.
arxiv:2611.15741.authors: Dennis Hall, Simon Pfeil, Jesse Taylor

arxiv:2611.15751.title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
arxiv:2611.15751.summary: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension.
arxiv:2611.15751.authors: Peter Banda, John Caughman, Tobi Lehman

arxiv:2611.15755.title: Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids
arxiv:2611.15755.summary: For a regular matroid on $m$ elements with positive weights and weighted girth $g_w$, we prove that the number of circuits of weight at most $\alpha g_w$ is bounded by $(Km)^{2\alpha}$, for every real $\alpha\ge1$ and an absolute constant $K$. This improves the previous $m^{O(\alpha^2)}$ bound of Gurjar and Vishnoi and matches classic graph cut and cycle counting bounds of Karger and Subramanian. We also show this is asymptotically optimal for all real $\alpha\geq 1$ under the Erd\H{o}s girth conjecture, while unconditional optimality holds for half-integer $\alpha$ by prior results.

arxiv:2611.15768.title: Space-Filling Hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.15768.summary: We seek space-filling hypersurfaces of a projective space over a finite field. They are hypersurfaces contain all rational points. The main goal is to construct a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree.
arxiv:2611.15768.authors: Victoria Bourgeois-Conti, Han-Bom Moon, Erick Perez, Amelia Warren

arxiv:2611.15790.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
arxiv:2611.15790.summary: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-S\"oderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table.

arxiv:2611.15799.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
arxiv:2611.15799.summary: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, \Theta)$ satisfies that $I_X(2\Theta)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre.

arxiv:2611.15801.title: Exponential Multiple Riordan Arrays
arxiv:2611.15801.summary: We extend exponential double Riordan arrays to exponential multiple Riordan arrays $[g;f_1,\ldots,f_\ell]$, whose columns are generated, in exponential form, by a function $g$ of $t^\ell$ and $\ell$ multipliers $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell$ used cyclically. We prove an $\ell$-case fundamental theorem, define the exponential multiple Riordan group, and determine its identity, inverses, and its Appell, associated, and $\ell$ Bell-type subgroups; the group is the semidirect product of its Appell and associated subgroups. We compute the production matrix in terms of $2\ell$ sequences, the $c_r$- and $r_r$-sequences ($0\leq r\leq \ell-1$), give its bivariate generating function in terms of generalized…

arxiv:2611.15811.title: $q$-$\gamma$-positivity of two $q$-Narayana polynomials
arxiv:2611.15811.summary: We address the question of $q$-$\gamma$-positivity of $q$-Narayana polynomials for $q$-super Catalan numbers $A_{n,m}(q)$ and their duals, $B_{n,m}(q)$. We offer three main results. First, both the $q$-$m$-Narayana polynomials, whose coefficients refine the q-super Catalan numbers, and the dual q-Narayana polynomials are $q$-$\gamma$-positive of index one.

arxiv:2611.15817.title: Tree Decomposition of Product and Nest Graphs for Assortment Optimization under the Generalized Nested Logit Model
arxiv:2611.15817.summary: The generalized nested logit model extends the nested logit model by allowing each product to belong to multiple nests. The overlapping nests in the generalized nested logit model can capture complex substitution patterns, and the model has found applications in many areas. We study the assortment optimization problem under the generalized nested logit model and prove that it is NP-hard when there are only two nests or when any two distinct nests have at most one product in common.
arxiv:2611.15817.authors: Yuheng Wang, Paat Rusmevichientong, Huseyin Topaloglu

arxiv:2611.15826.title: Second homology of some quandles
arxiv:2611.15826.summary: We derive formulas from Eisemann's formula for the second quandle homology of quandles. We prove that for a finite injective quandle $Q$, the second quandle homology $H_2(Q)$ can be computed in a representation group of $Q$, which is a finite quotient of the enveloping group of $Q$, by giving a formula for that. We use this to compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the subquandle of $k$-cycles of $S_n$ and $Q$ the quandle corresponding to the conjugacy class of a diagonalizable element of $SL(n,q)$, with some exceptions.

arxiv:2611.15830.title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
arxiv:2611.15830.summary: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree.

arxiv:2611.15846.title: Conflict-Free Cuts: Exploring the Boundaries of Tractability
arxiv:2611.15846.summary: A conflict-free cut of a host graph $G$ is an edge cut containing no conflicting pair of edges. The conflicts are specified by a conflict graph $\widehat G$ whose vertex set is $E(G)$. The conflict-free cut problem asks if the given instance $(G, \widehat G)$ has a conflict-free cut.

arxiv:2611.15899.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
arxiv:2611.15899.summary: We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Koll\'ar. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar.

arxiv:2611.15908.title: Some families of birational cubic and Verra fourfolds
arxiv:2611.15908.summary: We study the birational relationship between cubic fourfolds and Verra fourfolds, which are double covers of the product of two projective planes. We show that in?nitely many divisors in the moduli space of cubic fourfolds containing a plane parametrize cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. Our approach relies on the geometry of quadric surface bundles and their associated K3 surfaces, together with the study of Brauer classes.

arxiv:2611.15938.title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map
arxiv:2611.15938.summary: Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks.

arxiv:2611.15943.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
arxiv:2611.15943.summary: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$.
arxiv:2611.15943.authors: Dominik Burek, Tymoteusz Chmiel, S{\l}awomir Cynk, Marcin Oczko

arxiv:2611.15954.title: Riordan Arrays as Structured Operators for Artificial Intelligence
arxiv:2611.15954.summary: Riordan arrays have traditionally been studied as infinite lower-triangular matrices that encode generating-function transformations and combinatorial relationships. This note proposes a complementary direction: using Riordan arrays as structured operators in artificial intelligence and data analysis. For a data sequence with generating function $A(z)$, a Riordan array $(g(z),f(z))$ produces the transformation \[ A(z)\longmapsto g(z)A(f(z)).
arxiv:2611.15954.authors: Dennis Davenport, Dewayne A. Dixon, Moussa Doumbia

arxiv:2611.15955.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
arxiv:2611.15955.summary: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $\alpha > 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $\alpha \neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{\mu\}$ where $\mu$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $\pi\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points.

arxiv:2611.15962.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
arxiv:2611.15962.summary: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.
arxiv:2611.15962.authors: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Do Kien Hoang

arxiv:2611.15986.title: K3 surfaces and BHK Mirror symmetry: A counterexample
arxiv:2611.15986.summary: For K3 surfaces of BHK type, there are two versions of mirror symmetry that might be applied, namely BHK mirror symmetry and LPK3 mirror symmetry of Dolgachev, which involved choosing a polarizing lattice. It has been conjectured that for a pair of BHK mirror K3 surfaces, one can choose a polarizing lattice as the invariant lattice of some nonsymplectic diagonal symmetry. We provide a counterexample, showing that LPK3 mirror symmetry cannot be realized by polarizing surfaces by the invariant lattice of a diagonal symmetry.
arxiv:2611.15986.authors: Alexis Barrett, Archer Clayton, Ben DeVries, Nathan Priddis

arxiv:2611.15992.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
arxiv:2611.15992.summary: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was previously established by SAT searches of the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound.

arxiv:2611.15996.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
arxiv:2611.15996.summary: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $\mu$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $P\Gamma_N$ generated by a semigroup $\Gamma_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $P\Gamma_N$ and that the chain graphs of $P\Gamma_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single…

arxiv:2611.16008.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
arxiv:2611.16008.summary: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

arxiv:2611.16024.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
arxiv:2611.16024.summary: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius.

arxiv:2611.16030.title: Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors
arxiv:2611.16030.summary: We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus.

arxiv:2611.16034.title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
arxiv:2611.16034.summary: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang.
arxiv:2611.16034.authors: David Favero, Mykola Sapronov, Dash Stevanovich

arxiv:2611.16036.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
arxiv:2611.16036.summary: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $\Pi_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties.

arxiv:2611.16055.title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
arxiv:2611.16055.summary: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp.

arxiv:2611.16068.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
arxiv:2611.16068.summary: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class.
arxiv:2611.16068.authors: Milena Brockhof, Giovane Galindo, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

arxiv:2611.16078.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
arxiv:2611.16078.summary: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=\Gamma(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $\lambda$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $\lambda$-length.
arxiv:2611.16078.authors: Jonah Gaster, Didac Martinez-Granado, Christopher-Lloyd Simon

arxiv:2611.16124.title: On classifying knotted surfaces
arxiv:2611.16124.summary: These notes, which are based on four lectures delivered at the summer school "Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds" at PCMI in 2026, discuss classifications of locally flat surfaces in simply-connected $4$-manifolds.

arxiv:2611.16135.title: A global rigidity criterion for Coxeter $3$-polytopes
arxiv:2611.16135.summary: We give a combinatorial condition ensuring global projective rigidity of simple hyperbolic Coxeter $3$-polytopes. As an application, we prove that every right-angled L\"obell polytope is globally rigid.

arxiv:2611.16136.title: Almost unimodular quantum groups
arxiv:2611.16136.summary: We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $\delta$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight.
arxiv:2611.16136.authors: Aldo Garcia Guinto, Lucas Hall, Brent Nelson

arxiv:2611.16137.title: Quantization of Betti Mapping Stacks
arxiv:2611.16137.summary: We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.
arxiv:2611.16137.authors: John Francis, Owen Gwilliam, Rajiv Kaipa

arxiv:2611.16140.title: The lower boundary of the $\{K_2,K_{p},K_{q}\}$-profile
arxiv:2611.16140.summary: We determine the asymptotically sharp minimum number of $q$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $\gamma n^2$ edges and $\delta n^{p}$ $p$-cliques for $q>p>2$. The question of determining the minimum number of $r$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $\gamma n^2$ edges was previously resolved by Razborov for $r=3$, Nikiforov for $r=4$ and Reiher for all $r\geq 5$. For all $r\geq 3$, the minimum is attained by a complete multipartite graph where all parts are equal except for one that can be smaller or by a limit of such graphs.

arxiv:2611.16145.title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
arxiv:2611.16145.summary: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$.

arxiv:2611.16153.title: Enumerating Pyranim Isomorphisms
arxiv:2611.16153.summary: We study a Nim-adjacent poset game, where chips are arranged in a pyramid and two players take turns removing chips that do not currently support chips to the upper-left and upper-right; upon removing this chip, all supported chips above are also removed. Play continues until the final chip is removed. We use a bijection between the game states, Dyck paths, and unit interval graphs to count the number of possible game states up to isomorphism.

arxiv:2611.16160.title: Contiguity of unions of perfect matchings and random regular uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.16160.summary: For fixed integers $s\ge3$ and $r$ satisfying $\log(r!)>\frac{r(s-1)}s\log r$, the union of $r$ independent uniform perfect matchings of the complete $s$-uniform hypergraph is mutually contiguous to the uniform simple $r$-regular $s$-uniform hypergraph, as $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $s$. In particular, $r=\lceil e^s\rceil$ suffices. The main input is the sharp entropy inequality for random permutations of Bristiel and Caputo.

arxiv:2611.16178.title: Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
arxiv:2611.16178.summary: Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights.
arxiv:2611.16178.authors: Masatake Hirao, Koji Imamura, Hiroshi Nozaki, Masanori Sawa, Tomoki Tamaru

arxiv:2611.16226.title: On subgroup regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
arxiv:2611.16226.summary: A subset $D$ of the vertex set of a graph is called an $(a,b)$-regular set if each vertex in $D$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $D$, and each vertex outside $D$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $D$. A proper subgroup $H$ of $G$ is called an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,\alpha)$ if it is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $GC(G,S,\alpha)$ for some generalized Cayley subset $S$ of $G$ induced by the involutory automorphism $\alpha$. This paper investigates subgroup $(0,b)$-regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs.
arxiv:2611.16226.authors: Qianfen Liao, Weijun Liu, Peng-Li Zhang

arxiv:2611.16231.title: A Polynomial Bound on Split Rank
arxiv:2611.16231.summary: We prove that the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomially bounded in its input length, resolving a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang. If the defining system has dense binary encoding length $L$, then $O((L+1)^9)$ split rounds suffice to reach the integer hull in arbitrary dimension.

arxiv:2611.16243.title: Antipodal paths: a short proof by counting intersections
arxiv:2611.16243.summary: We give a short elementary proof of Norine's antipodal-coloring theorem: every red--blue edge coloring of a hypercube in which antipodal edges have opposite colors contains a monochromatic path joining antipodal vertices.

arxiv:2611.16254.title: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
arxiv:2611.16254.summary: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant.

arxiv:2611.16256.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
arxiv:2611.16256.summary: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code.

arxiv:2611.16262.title: The graph $a$-Tur\'an theorem
arxiv:2611.16262.summary: We prove analogues of Tur\'an's theorem and the Erd\H{o}s--Stone theorem for graph $a$-numbers. The $i$th $a$-number $a_i(G)$ equals the $i$th rational Betti number of the real toric manifold associated with the graph associahedron of $G$. We show that the Tur\'an graph $T_r(n)$ maximizes every $a$-number among $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.16268.title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
arxiv:2611.16268.summary: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link.
