On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities.
arxiv:2611.16268.authors: Diogo da Silva Machado, Jos\'e Seade

arxiv:2611.16294.title: Nondifferentiability on Irrational Invariant Graphs of Smooth Area-Preserving Twist Maps
arxiv:2611.16294.summary: For a fixed irrational rotation number and every $1\le r<\infty$, we construct an exact area-preserving $C^r$ twist map preserving a Lipschitz graph. The set of nondifferentiability points has Hausdorff dimension $d=2/(r+1)$ and zero $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. At the same rotation number, we construct a $C^\infty$ twist map whose invariant graph is nondifferentiable on exactly one two-sided orbit.

arxiv:2611.16295.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
arxiv:2611.16295.summary: Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$.
arxiv:2611.16295.authors: Yotam Dikstein, Izhar Oppenheim, Inga Valentiner-Branth

arxiv:2611.16299.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS) at 33 Orders
arxiv:2611.16299.summary: A Latin square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array over symbols $\{0,1,\ldots n-1\}$, such that the same symbol does not appear twice in any row or any column. Two Latin squares of order $n$ are orthogonal if, when superimposed, they yield each of the $n^2$ ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. A set of two or more Latin squares are mutually orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS) if each pair of distinct squares is orthogonal.

arxiv:2611.16328.title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
arxiv:2611.16328.summary: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $\Gamma$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $\Gamma$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.

arxiv:2611.16336.title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
arxiv:2611.16336.summary: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane.
arxiv:2611.16336.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

arxiv:2611.16338.title: Total edge irregularity strength of cubic graphs
arxiv:2611.16338.summary: We show that every finite simple cubic graph on $n$ vertices has total edge irregularity strength $n/2+1$, confirming the Ivan\v{c}o-Jendrol' conjecture for cubic graphs. The key step is to algorithmically construct a $\{1,n/2+1\}$-vertex labeling such that half of the vertices are labeled $1$ and the average degree of the subgraph induced by them is close enough to two. We extend such a labeling to a total edge irregular $(n/2+1)$-labeling, possibly after a local adjustment to a single vertex.
arxiv:2611.16338.authors: Aleams Barra, Suhadi Wido Saputro, Hajime Tanaka

arxiv:2611.16340.title: The Bolza Surface Does Not Locally Minimize the Diameter Function
arxiv:2611.16340.summary: We study the diameter function on the Teichm\"uller space of closed hyperbolic Riemann surfaces. Although the Bolza surface maximizes the systole among hyperbolic surfaces of genus 2, its extremal behavior with respect to the diameter function is less clear. Using first variations of distances at diameter pairs and linear programming duality, we establish a sufficient criterion for a surface not to be a local minimizer of the diameter function.

arxiv:2611.16352.title: Weighted summability criteria for stability and instability of discrete dynamics with general growth rates
arxiv:2611.16352.summary: Following the time rescaling introduced by Dragi\v{c}evi\'{c} and Silva in their paper [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst.
arxiv:2611.16352.authors: Ariana G\u{a}in\u{a}, Cristian L\u{a}zureanu, Nicolae Lupa

arxiv:2611.16354.title: Postcritically Finite Unicritical Polynomials over CM Fields
arxiv:2611.16354.summary: A rational map of degree at least two is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has a finite forward orbit. For the unicritical family $f_{d,c}(z)=z^d+c$ with $d\ge2$, we call $c$ a PCF parameter if $f_{d,c}$ is PCF. As discussed by Baker and DeMarco, these parameters are analogous to $j$-invariants of elliptic curves with complex multiplication.

arxiv:2611.16362.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded Cohen-Macaulay rings
arxiv:2611.16362.summary: We say that a standard graded algebra is cyclotomic if all roots of its $h$-polynomial lie on the complex unit circle. We study which products of cyclotomic polynomials can occur as $h$-polynomials of standard graded Cohen--Macaulay algebras without being of complete intersection type. For each fixed positive integer $a$, we reduce the nonexistence problem for multiplicities $ap$ over all sufficiently large primes $p$ to finitely many cases.

arxiv:2611.16377.title: Universal optimality on finite Lee tori
arxiv:2611.16377.summary: We study subsets of finite Lee tori that minimize pair energy among sets of the same cardinality for every discretely completely monotone potential. At half occupancy on a product of even cycles, the two checkerboards minimize both total pair energy and maximum individual energy. They are the only minimizers for every nonconstant classical completely monotone potential on $(0,\infty)$, proving the checkerboard conjecture of Bouman, Draisma, and van Leeuwaarden for this class.

arxiv:2611.16391.title: Differential equations for twisted intertwining operators in abelian orbifold conformal field theory
arxiv:2611.16391.summary: Let $ V $ be a vertex operator algebra with two commuting automorphisms $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ (possibly of infinite order and non-semisimple). We derive a Jacobi identity for a twisted intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is a $ g_1 $-twisted $ V $-module, $ W_2 $ is a $ g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module, and $ W_3 $ is a $ g_1 g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module. For any abelian group $ G $ of automorphisms of a CFT-type vertex operator algebra, under certain Noetherian assumptions, we derive differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N)…

arxiv:2611.16436.title: Continuous representations of topological monoids via reconstruction
arxiv:2611.16436.summary: We study continuous representations of topological monoids on discrete modules via a finite-restriction reconstruction method. For an arbitrary topological monoid $\mathscr{M}$, we construct a transformation monoid $\mathscr{E}_\mathscr{M}$ whose uniformly continuous representations are equivalent to continuous representations of $\mathscr{M}$ on discrete modules. By the finite-restriction reconstruction, these categories are equivalent to categories of sheaves of modules over special sites.
arxiv:2611.16436.authors: Zhenxing Di, Liping Li, Li Liang

arxiv:2611.16443.title: The spectrum of free projective geometries over finite chain rings
arxiv:2611.16443.summary: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime ideal of residue order $q$, and $\mathcal{O}_r=\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{p}^r$ which is a finite chain ring; the motivating example is $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$. The free projective geometry $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{fr}(\mathcal{O}_r)$ is the graph whose vertices are the nontrivial free submodules of $\mathcal{O}_r^{d}$, two of them adjacent when one strictly contains the other. For every $d$, $q$ and $r$ we reduce its adjacency matrix to explicit symmetric matrices (blocks) of size at most $d-1$.

arxiv:2611.16449.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
arxiv:2611.16449.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$.

arxiv:2611.16453.title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
arxiv:2611.16453.summary: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space.
arxiv:2611.16453.authors: Linfang Hou, Si Li, Yongchang Zhu

arxiv:2611.16458.title: Chromatic polynomials of signed graphs with a balancing vertex
arxiv:2611.16458.summary: We study the zero-free chromatic polynomial $Z_\Sigma(q)$ of a signed graph $\Sigma$ and the characteristic polynomial $\chi_\Sigma(q)=Z_\Sigma(q-1)$ of its associated hyperplane arrangement containing all coordinate hyperplanes. For a connected signed graph on $n\ge 2$ vertices with a balancing vertex, we prove the equivalence of the following four conditions: (i) $Z_\Sigma(q)$ is the chromatic polynomial of an ordinary graph; (ii) the numerator of $\sum_{q\ge 1}\chi_\Sigma(q)t^q$, written with denominator $(1-t)^{n+1}$, has nonnegative coefficients; (iii) $\Sigma$ has a balanced block; and (iv) $\chi_\Sigma(2)=0$. We also provide explicit counterexamples showing that neither the…
arxiv:2611.16458.authors: Akihiro Higashitani, Go Kamata, Masato Konoike

arxiv:2611.16462.title: New $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant infinite families and the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image
arxiv:2611.16462.summary: Let $a$ denote the stabilization of the Euler class of the sign representation of $\mathrm{C}_2$. In this paper, we show that the Behrens-Shah periodic $u$-self-equivalence of $C(a^i)$ -- a direct consequence of J.F. Adams' calculation of James periodicity -- determines the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image of the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant sphere spectrum, recovering a recent theorem of Guo-Li-Lu-Wu-Xu-Yang-Zhang via a different method.
arxiv:2611.16462.authors: Mason Adams, Prasit Bhattacharya, Arannya Bhattacherjee, Alex Waugh

arxiv:2611.16470.title: On the algebraic bipartite graphs $D(4s,q)$
arxiv:2611.16470.summary: Lazebnik-Ustimenko graphs $D(k,q)$ constitute a notable family of $q$-regular, edge-transitive bipartite graphs characterized by high symmetry and large girth, with wide applications in algebraic graph theory and coding theory. The precise girth of $D(k,q)$ is governed by a celebrated conjecture proposed by F\"{u}redi et al., which remains unresolved in general cases. Although prior works have validated this conjecture for several specific parameter regimes and established fundamental structural properties of graph girth, a systematic characterization of girth cycles for even-indexed subfamilies of \(D(k,q)\) is still absent.
arxiv:2611.16470.authors: Chen Zhang, Xiaoyan Cheng, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu

arxiv:2611.16518.title: Counting Triangulated 3-Spheres, Nuclei, and Polyhedra
arxiv:2611.16518.summary: We exploit two-dimensional dual polyhedra to study triangulated $3$-spheres and nuclei. First, we show that the long-standing open problem of whether the number of triangulated $3$-spheres is exponentially bounded is equivalent to the corresponding problem for one-vertex generalized triangulations, and hence also for special spines of the $3$-ball. This also establishes an equivalent counting problem for nuclei.

arxiv:2611.16529.title: Characterizations of products of projective spaces and quadrics
arxiv:2611.16529.summary: We characterize products of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using Schur functors and positivity of vector bundles. First, we obtain characterizations of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using positivity of arbitrary Schur functors of extensions of a unipotent bundle by the tangent bundle, generalizing several existing results. We then prove that almost nef regular foliations whose direct sum is a subbundle of the tangent bundle determine a product decomposition, if the corresponding Schur functors admit suitable positive Schur submodules.

arxiv:2611.16531.title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$
arxiv:2611.16531.summary: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$.

arxiv:2611.16554.title: The asymptotic number of $BCK(p)$-terms
arxiv:2611.16554.summary: A $BCK(p)$-term is a closed lambda-term in which each abstraction binds at most $p$ variables; for $p=1$ these terms are related to the axiom system BCK of combinatory logic. We determine the number of $BCK(p)$-terms of size $n$, up to a constant multiplicative factor, for every $p\ge2$. For $p=2$ the result is fully explicit: \[ f\_n\sim A\,n^{2n/5}2^{n/5}e^{-2n/5}n^{-3/5}e^{P(n^{1/5})}, \] where $P$ is an explicit polynomial of degree $4$.

arxiv:2611.16570.title: On graceful labeling of Jahangir graphs
arxiv:2611.16570.summary: For a graph with q edges, a graceful labeling assigns distinct integers from {0,...,q} its vertices so that the absolute differences across the edges are exactly 1,...,q. A Jahangir graph J_{n,m}, with n >= 2 and m >= 3, consists of an outer cycle on nm vertices and a hub joined to m equally spaced vertices of that cycle, with q = (n+1)m edges. This family of graphs is known to be graceful.

arxiv:2611.16593.title: A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperk\"ahler fourfolds
arxiv:2611.16593.summary: We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperk\"ahler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained.
arxiv:2611.16593.authors: Franco Giovenzana, Andr\'es Rojas, Jieao Song

arxiv:2611.16613.title: Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
arxiv:2611.16613.summary: We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections.
arxiv:2611.16613.authors: Seung-Yeal Ha, Xinyu Wang, Chen Wu, Fanqin Zeng

arxiv:2611.16616.title: Quantitative Accumulation of Invariant Circles Near a Non-splitting Separatrix
arxiv:2611.16616.summary: For a smooth area-preserving cylinder map with a non-splitting separatrix and an exact symplectic linearization at its saddle, we prove accumulation by smooth essential invariant circles when the boundary transition is sufficiently $C^4$-close to a translation. As an application, we give an answer to Herman's open problem in 1983.

arxiv:2611.16635.title: Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
arxiv:2611.16635.summary: We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.

arxiv:2611.16649.title: On 2-Homogeneous Colourings of Cubic Bipartite Graphs
arxiv:2611.16649.summary: A proper vertex colouring is 2-homogeneous if every open neighbourhood contains exactly two colours. We show that every cubic bipartite graph admits a 2-homogeneous colouring with at most four colours, proving a conjecture of Janicov\'a, Madaras, Sot\'ak and Lu\v{z}ar. For 3-connected det-extremal cubic bipartite graphs, we establish the stronger bound $\chi_h^{(2)}(G) = 3$, showing that every such graph admits a fall 3-colouring.
arxiv:2611.16649.authors: Rong-Xia Hao, Jianbing Liu, Federico Romaniello

arxiv:2611.16654.title: Exact Tur\'an densities of even zycles
arxiv:2611.16654.summary: We determine the exact Tur\'an density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 4$ with $3\nmid\ell$, showing that $\pi(Z_\ell)=5/9$. More generally, we prove that $\pi(Z_\ell)\le 5/9$ for all even $\ell\ge 4$. In the range of equality, we also establish a stability theorem, showing that every almost extremal $Z_\ell$-free $3$-graph is close in edit distance to the classical Tur\'an construction.

arxiv:2611.16659.title: Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
arxiv:2611.16659.summary: We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.
arxiv:2611.16659.authors: Zoe Geiselmann, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner, Marcel Wack

arxiv:2611.16672.title: Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
arxiv:2611.16672.summary: Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$. The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$.
arxiv:2611.16672.authors: Jos{\'e} F. Fernando, Riccardo Ghiloni, Wies{\l}aw Paw{\l}ucki

arxiv:2611.16674.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
arxiv:2611.16674.summary: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root.

arxiv:2611.16675.title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
arxiv:2611.16675.summary: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences.
arxiv:2611.16675.authors: Miaomiao Lv, Juan Zhang, Zhen Jin

arxiv:2611.16680.title: Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives
arxiv:2611.16680.summary: We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives.

arxiv:2611.16690.title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
arxiv:2611.16690.summary: We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. As a consequence, the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement in quantum information is undecidable.

arxiv:2611.16695.title: Free G\"odel algebras over G\"odel hoops
arxiv:2611.16695.summary: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from G\"odel algebras to G\"odel hoops. If $H$ is a G\"odel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the G\"odel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a G\"odel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary G\"odel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction.

arxiv:2611.16706.title: Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
arxiv:2611.16706.summary: In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model.
arxiv:2611.16706.authors: Aaron Loh, J. D. Mireles James

arxiv:2611.16746.title: Topological Entropy of Group Cellular Automata is Effectively Computable
arxiv:2611.16746.summary: Topological entropy is a fundamental invariant of dynamical systems, quantifying their complexity. For cellular automata, however, determining topological entropy is generally algorithmically intractable. We study group cellular automata, namely cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism.
arxiv:2611.16746.authors: Niccol\`o Castronuovo, Alberto Dennunzio, Jarkko Kari, Luciano Margara

arxiv:2611.16762.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
arxiv:2611.16762.summary: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis.

arxiv:2611.16763.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
arxiv:2611.16763.summary: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation.

arxiv:2611.16768.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
arxiv:2611.16768.summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface.

arxiv:2611.16769.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
arxiv:2611.16769.summary: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$.

arxiv:2611.16775.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
arxiv:2611.16775.summary: Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[ b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[ b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor} \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$.

arxiv:2611.16784.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
arxiv:2611.16784.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds…

arxiv:2611.16834.title: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
arxiv:2611.16834.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $a,m\in\Bbb Z_{(p)}$ and $a(a+1)m\not\equiv 0\pmod p$. In this paper, we deduce the congruence for $(\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k}) (\sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k(k+1)})$ modulo $p^3$. As applications we obtain many congruences for \begin{align*}&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k(k+1)^r},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k(k+1)^r}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k(k+1)^r}\quad(r=1,2,3) \\&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k}, \quad…

arxiv:2611.16837.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
arxiv:2611.16837.summary: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$.

arxiv:2611.16839.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
arxiv:2611.16839.summary: We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $\delta$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2\delta)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.
arxiv:2611.16839.authors: A. Yu. Chirkov, S. I. Veselov, D. V. Gribanov, D. S. Malyshev, N. Yu. Zolotykh

arxiv:2611.16849.title: Constrained intersection representations and forbidden patterns
arxiv:2611.16849.summary: We study the interplay between two types of graph classes: the ones defined by intersections of geometric objects and the ones defined by the absence of a substructure. More precisely, we study intersection graphs that are grounded, that is, the objects lie above a horizontal line that they touch, and ordered graphs with forbidden patterns, that is, ordered graphs that avoid a set of ordered induced subgraphs. These two approaches are fundamentally different, but it is known that several interesting graph classes have both types of characterizations, and we aim to understand whether this is a general phenomenon.
arxiv:2611.16849.authors: Laurent Feuilloley, Michel Habib, Amalia Sorondo

arxiv:2611.16858.title: Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders
arxiv:2611.16858.summary: The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $\gamma$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $\gamma$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$.

arxiv:2611.16862.title: Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
arxiv:2611.16862.summary: In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces.
arxiv:2611.16862.authors: Peixuan Liu, Zhiyuan Liu, Yuanqi Jiang

arxiv:2611.16867.title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
arxiv:2611.16867.summary: LLM agents, i.e., language models run by a harness, can now write, run and debug software autonomously. This raises the question of whether they can also carry out control system design. In this paper, we consider control system design as a task for LLM agents and grade the designed controller as control engineers do: the controller is given in a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, evaluated on held-out seeds against an ordered set of requirements, under specified physical perturbations and structural certificates, without using neural networks.
arxiv:2611.16867.authors: Jieqiang Wei, Fahad Ali, Jonny Reichwald, Silun Zhang

arxiv:2611.16874.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
arxiv:2611.16874.summary: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph.

arxiv:2611.16883.title: Optimal Polyomino Fences
arxiv:2611.16883.summary: The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments.
arxiv:2611.16883.authors: Alexis Langlois-R\'emillard, Mia N. M\"u{\ss}ig, Helmut Podhaisky, Erika Roldan, G\"unter Rote, Maximilian Br\"omme, Matthes Norden, Maximilian Prietzel, Daniel Yu, Mykhailo Lyader

arxiv:2611.16894.title: Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
arxiv:2611.16894.summary: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points in a closed unit disk and $\rho$ for the number of points per unit area, we show that neither set can be covered when $\mathcal{N}(d)<2\sqrt3\,\rho$, and we determine these spacings exactly, thirteen intervals for $\mathcal{S}_d$ and twelve for $\mathcal{H}_d$.
arxiv:2611.16894.authors: Teeradej Kittipassorn, Nattawut Phetmak, Kirati Sriamorn

arxiv:2611.16899.title: Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity
arxiv:2611.16899.summary: We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.

arxiv:2611.16900.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
arxiv:2611.16900.summary: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions.
arxiv:2611.16900.authors: Tyler Franke, Ingo Runkel, Volker Schomerus

arxiv:2611.16901.title: Edge-wise Graph Alignments
arxiv:2611.16901.summary: Pairwise graph ``alignments'', usually defined as maximum common subgraphs, have been considered in many application domains, including the comparison of molecular structures. Most commonly, the problem is formulated as maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS) or maximum common edge subgraph (MCES) problems. Sometimes these formulations are restricted to connected common subgraphs.
arxiv:2611.16901.authors: Akbar Davoodi, Christoph Flamm, Daniel Merkle, Peter F. Stadler

arxiv:2611.16911.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
arxiv:2611.16911.summary: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure.

arxiv:2611.16953.title: Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support
arxiv:2611.16953.summary: We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $\alpha$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,\alpha)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass--Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.

arxiv:2611.16957.title: Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
arxiv:2611.16957.summary: An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Koml\'os, and Szemer\'edi and of Kim. Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstra\"ete proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor.
arxiv:2611.16957.authors: Ayush Basu, Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku

arxiv:2611.16962.title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
arxiv:2611.16962.summary: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators.

arxiv:2611.16963.title: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
arxiv:2611.16963.summary: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_\Gamma$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

arxiv:2611.16965.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
arxiv:2611.16965.summary: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already…

arxiv:2611.16970.title: Rainbow matchings in non-uniform hypergraph systems
arxiv:2611.16970.summary: Let $s\geq 1$, $r_1, r_2,\dots, r_{s+1}$ be given positive integers and $r=\max\{r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{s+1}\}$. We prove that if $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ is a family of hypergraphs on a ground set of $n$ vertices, $n\geq 4r^2(s+1)$, such that $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$ and $|\mathcal{F}_i|>\binom{n}{r_i}-\binom{n-s}{r_i}-\binom{n-s-r}{r_i-1}+1$, for all $i \in [s+1]$, then $\mathcal{F}$ admits a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ or there exists $W \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $W$ is a vertex cover of $\mathcal{F}_i$, for all $i \in [s+1]$. This improves upon the previously known range $n>2r^3s$ to $n>4r^2(s+1)$.

arxiv:2611.16972.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
arxiv:2611.16972.summary: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
arxiv:2611.16972.authors: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang

arxiv:2611.16987.title: A lift of Baxter's cyclic summation identity with applications to quantum topology
arxiv:2611.16987.summary: While studying the chiral Potts model Baxter discovered a cyclic analogue of Ramanujan's ${}_1\psi_{1}$ summation identity. This identity was subsequently interpreted by Faddeev and Kashaev as a pentagon relation for the quantum dilogarithm function, a key ingredient in cyclic quantizations of Teichm\"uller theory. Existing forms of the identity involve multivalued functions so one must either accept overall phase ambiguities or keep track of branches on a complicated covering space.

arxiv:2611.17004.title: Real log canonical tresholds and real log canonical tresholds with signs
arxiv:2611.17004.summary: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

arxiv:2611.17014.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
arxiv:2611.17014.summary: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.
arxiv:2611.17014.authors: Marco Aldi, Samuel Bevins, Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis, Sergio Da Silva, Quincy Frias, Tom\'as Mej\'ia G\'omez

arxiv:2611.17022.title: Large diameter for $(\Delta+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
arxiv:2611.17022.summary: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2\mu$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + \mu$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $\mu$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures.

arxiv:2611.17047.title: Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
arxiv:2611.17047.summary: We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph.
arxiv:2611.17047.authors: Jennifer Biermann, Kuei-Nuan Lin, Augustine O'Keefe

arxiv:2611.17049.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
arxiv:2611.17049.summary: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric.
arxiv:2611.17049.authors: Erwin Luesink, Archishman Saha, Tanya Schmah, Cristina Stoica

arxiv:2611.17075.title: The structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups of the real projective plane
arxiv:2611.17075.summary: In this paper we study the structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups $B_n(RP^2)$ of the real projective plane $RP^2$. It is known that the isomorphism classes of these subgroups are comprised of cyclic, dicyclic and binary polyhedral groups. Using specific elements of $B_n(RP^2)$, we construct embeddings of the cyclic and dicyclic subgroups, we show that there is a single conjugacy class of the maximal dicyclic groups, and for small values of n, we also construct embeddings of the bin- ary tetrahedral and octahedral groups.

arxiv:2611.17106.title: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
arxiv:2611.17106.summary: We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain. We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension.

arxiv:2611.17113.title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpi\'nski spaces
arxiv:2611.17113.summary: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpi\'nski spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpi\'nski type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpi\'nski spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the N\'eron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots.

arxiv:2611.17120.title: Equidistribution of curves in hypersurfaces of low degree
arxiv:2611.17120.summary: We prove that over $\mathbb{C}$, for any smooth projective curve $\mathscr{C}$ and any smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ such that $n \geq 2^d(d-1)$, Faisant's equidistribution principle holds for $(\mathscr{C},V)$. In other words, for any reasonable set of jet conditions $W$, the moduli space $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ of degree $e$ maps $\mathscr{C} \to V$ satisfying conditions $W$ converges in the Grothendieck ring of complex varieties, after renormalisation, as $e \to \infty$. This provides the dimension and decomposition into irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ for $e$ large enough.

arxiv:2611.17133.title: $Z_\infty$-algebras: Zinbielification of $B_\infty$ and quasi-shuffle algebras
arxiv:2611.17133.summary: Commutative $B_\infty$-algebras provide a natural generalisation of the shuffle and quasi-shuffle algebras, giving deformations of the shuffle algebra. We introduce a Zinbiel analogue in $Z_\infty$-algebras, giving deformations of the half-shuffle Zinbiel algebra. All commutative $B_\infty$-algebras have been shown to be isomorphic to the shuffle algebra, though this isomorphism is not canonical.

arxiv:2611.17136.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
arxiv:2611.17136.summary: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.

arxiv:2611.17138.title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
arxiv:2611.17138.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $\tau$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra…
arxiv:2611.17138.authors: Andrea Appel, Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki, Bart Vlaar

arxiv:2611.17149.title: K3 tails in the KSBA moduli of Kunev surfaces
arxiv:2611.17149.summary: In the context of compact moduli spaces of Koll\'ar, Shepherd-Barron, and Alexeev stable surfaces, a degeneration can acquire an exceptional K3 component in the limit, or more simply a K3 tail. We study this phenomenon for Kunev surfaces: minimal surfaces of general type with $K^2=p_g=1$ that arise as $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-covers of the projective plane branched along two general cubics and a line. We classify the K3 tails that occur when the branch curve degenerates to a singular curve with a non-log canonical isolated semi-quasihomogeneous singularity, and describe the corresponding boundary strata.
arxiv:2611.17149.authors: Yongnam Lee, Elisa Scattone, Luca Schaffler

arxiv:2611.17155.title: Algebraic and geometric aspects of Demazure weaves
arxiv:2611.17155.summary: These are notes to supplement my talks at the Current Developments in Mathematics Conference in 2026. They are an expository account of recent work in the study of braid varieties and their relation to low-dimensional contact and symplectic topology. A driving theme is the development and use of Demazure weaves to construct cluster algebra structures on the coordinate rings of such braid varieties.

arxiv:2611.17168.title: Discrete Helicity on Graphs: Pfaffian Energies and Clique Bounds
arxiv:2611.17168.summary: We introduce a helicity functional of each order on graphs for real-valued edge forms, and give it a unified local Pfaffian realization. Motivated by the continuous energy inequality, we further construct a discrete version of helicity energy, and prove sharp Maclaurin inequalities for these energies. In particular, a special case of these Maclaurin inequalities yields a lower bound on the clique number, depending on the choice of edge form.

arxiv:2611.17183.title: New bounds on the boxicity of Kneser graphs
arxiv:2611.17183.summary: For a graph $G=(V,E)$, the boxicity $\operatorname{box}(G)$ is the least integer $d$ such that $G$ is the intersection graph of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ is the graph whose vertex set corresponds to the family of $k$ sized subsets of an $n$ sized ground set, and a pair of vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding sets are disjoint. In this short paper, we provide new bounds for the boxicity of $K(n,k)$.
arxiv:2611.17183.authors: L. Sunil Chandran, Suraj Kumar Sahoo

arxiv:2611.17189.title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
arxiv:2611.17189.summary: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two.

arxiv:2611.17197.title: Matching statistics in regular hypergraphs and applications
arxiv:2611.17197.summary: For fixed $k\ge3$, we determine the first sublinear correction to the logarithm of the matching partition function for a class of $n$-vertex $d$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs, uniformly for activities in each fixed compact interval of $(0,\infty)$.Our hypotheses include every regular linear hypergraph of polynomial degree and a class of nonlinear hypergraphs described by higher codegrees and intersection patterns, which we introduce here. The weighted counting estimate implies an averaged version of Kahn's conjecture: under the uniform measure, the expected number of uncovered vertices is $(1+o(1))nd^{-1/k}$, with concentration and large deviations on this scale. The proof combines a…

arxiv:2611.17198.title: Patterns, Distances, and Structure in Sparse Sets
arxiv:2611.17198.summary: A central theme in modern harmonic analysis, with strong connections to Ramsey theory, is the tension between randomness and structure: to what extent can a "large" set avoid prescribed configurations, and when must such patterns inevitably appear? The answer depends delicately on how size is measured, with notions such as Hausdorff dimension, Fourier dimension, and density leading to strikingly different phenomena. In this mini-course, we explore this theme through two complementary perspectives.

arxiv:2611.17205.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erd\H{o}s-Graham irregularity problem
arxiv:2611.17205.summary: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erd\H{o}s Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $0<c<1$ the ratio $f_c(n)/n$ has $\limsup$ equal to $c/2$, attained along odd $n$, and, along the integers $n$ whose least non-divisor equals a prime power $q$, tends to \[ \max\Bigl\{\frac cq,\; c-\frac12+\frac{1-c}{q}\Bigr\} \qquad\text{whenever } 2^{q-2}\min\{c,1-c\}\le 1 .

arxiv:2611.17219.title: Structure-Preserving Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Dynamics on Arbitrary Time Scales
arxiv:2611.17219.summary: The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron combines a passive membrane law with threshold-triggered firing and reset. We formulate this hybrid neuron model, under constant input, on an arbitrary Hilger time scale $\mathbb{T}$. Our central result is that, after the first spike, the firing times satisfy $t_{n+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}^{+}(t_n+T_c)$, where $T_c$ is the classical reset-to-threshold travel time.
arxiv:2611.17219.authors: Billur Kaymak\c{c}alan (University of Turkish Aeronautical Association), Behiye \.{I}layda Sel\c{c}uk (Bilkent University)

arxiv:2611.17232.title: Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison
arxiv:2611.17232.summary: Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited.

arxiv:2611.17237.title: Permutation patterns and higher connectivity in inversion graphs
arxiv:2611.17237.summary: We prove that any permutation $\pi \in S_n$ whose inversion graph is $k$-connected has at least $\frac{k+1}{2}n - C$ inversions, where $C$ depends only on $k$. In particular, inversion graphs beat the general lower bound $\frac{kn}{2}$ for the number of edges in a $k$-connected graph. Furthermore, we characterize the permutation patterns $\sigma$ having the property that if $\pi$ avoids $\sigma$, then the bound improves to $kn - C$.

arxiv:2611.17244.title: Higher Categorical Bistellar Moves
arxiv:2611.17244.summary: We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.

arxiv:2611.17252.title: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete
arxiv:2611.17252.summary: Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary.

arxiv:2611.17259.title: Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity
arxiv:2611.17259.summary: We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdio\u{g}lu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph.

arxiv:2611.17277.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
arxiv:2611.17277.summary: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

arxiv:2611.17282.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
arxiv:2611.17282.summary: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form.

arxiv:2611.17293.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
arxiv:2611.17293.summary: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.

arxiv:2611.17315.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
arxiv:2611.17315.summary: We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems.

arxiv:2611.17326.title: A hyperbolic area proof of the Kahn-Lyubich Covering Lemma and its generalization
arxiv:2611.17326.summary: The Covering Lemma of J. Kahn and M. Lyubich is a fundamental analytic tool for controlling conformal moduli of annuli under branched coverings of finite degree.
